## This pass (2026-11-07w, standing solution-architect review): independently re-verified the
sibling track's `0f6595b` ("~46 SECURITY DEFINER functions' revoke-from-public never actually
removed anon's own execute grant", migration `0120`) against primary sources, not assertion - every
claim in it checks out. No new bug found or fixed by this pass; this entry exists because a
significant security claim from a track this chain hadn't independently checked deserved the same
scrutiny this review applies to its own work before being treated as settled.

Oriented from `389d6a7` (this chain's own immediately-preceding pass, HEAD at that commit, matching
the verified HEAD this pass was given). `git fetch origin main`: clean, `origin/main` matched local
`HEAD` exactly, no sibling commits landed since `0f6595b`/`389d6a7`. PRs re-checked via `gh api
repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls?state=open`: `#176`/`#178`/`#179`/`#180`/`#181` still open
(`draft: false`), `#164`/`#165`/`#177` still drafts - all 8 unchanged, none merged or closed this
pass. No PR was touched, amended or merged.

**What was actually checked, with real evidence, not a re-read of the commit's own prose:**

1. **The underlying mechanism claim** (`alter default privileges in schema public grant all on
   functions to anon, ...` runs once, platform-side, separately from and untouched by `revoke all
   ... from public`) - confirmed this is pre-existing project infrastructure, not something the
   sibling commit invented to support its own narrative: `engine/security/scratch_supabase_stub.sql`
   already carried this exact `alter default privileges ... grant all on functions to anon,
   authenticated, service_role` line (`git log` on the file: last touched `abcd91f`, well before
   `0f6595b`/`fdf51d7`). This is standard, correct PostgreSQL behaviour (a named-role default-
   privilege grant and the generic `PUBLIC`-pseudo-role default are two independent ACL entries;
   revoking one never touches the other) - not a novel or dubious claim.

2. **The "52 anon-executable pre-fix" count** - reproduced for real. Started a real scratch
   Postgres 16 (`pg_ctlcluster 16 main start`, `sudo -u postgres psql`, local peer auth), applied
   `scratch_supabase_stub.sql`, then replayed all 119 pre-`0120` migration files (`0001`-`0119`) in
   filename order verbatim - clean, no manual fixture, no error. Ran the exact verification query
   the commit's own migration header specifies
   (`has_function_privilege('anon', p.oid, 'EXECUTE')` over non-trigger `security definer` functions
   in `public`): **52**, matching the claim exactly, not approximately.

3. **The migration's own revoke list** - counted `47` `revoke` statements in
   `0120_security_definer_functions_anon_grant_table_cleanup.sql` by grep, independent of the
   commit message's prose. `52 (pre-fix anon-executable) - 5 (named exclusions:
   apply_payfast_itn/invite_preview/signups_enabled/start_payfast_checkout/
   unsubscribe_lifecycle_email) = 47` - matches exactly.

4. **Applied the real migration file** (not a hand-copied fragment) to the same scratch database -
   re-ran the identical query: **5**, exactly the 5 named exclusions, confirmed by listing them.

5. **Functional, not just grant-table, verification.** `set role anon; select
   is_platform_admin();` / `select * from platform_admin_companies();` / `select
   is_company_member(<uuid>);` - all three now raise `permission denied for function ...` post-fix
   (pre-fix, re-confirmed these executed with no error, returning `f`/0 rows - the grant really was
   live). `set role authenticated` on the same three calls - unaffected: still returns the correct
   business-logic result (`f` for a non-admin, 0 rows for a non-member), not a new grant-level
   denial. Zero regression for the one role that actually uses these, confirmed directly, not
   inferred.

6. **The two "never had any revoke/grant at all" functions** (`is_company_member`, 0001;
   `tt_is_company_admin`, 0050) - grepped every migration file for any prior `grant`/`revoke`
   statement naming either function: zero hits before `0120`. Claim confirmed, not assumed from the
   commit's own prose.

7. **The "zero RLS policies target anon/public" claim** underpinning the "not independently
   exploitable" severity judgment - independently re-derived, not re-read: extracted every real
   `create policy ... to <role>` clause across all migrations (158 total) - every single one targets
   `authenticated`; none target `anon` or `public`. Confirms a real `anon` RPC call under the old,
   buggy grant table could not have reached a table row an RLS policy would otherwise have blocked
   anyway (though several of the 44 fixed functions also have their own internal `auth.uid()`/
   `is_company_member()`/`is_platform_admin()` gate independent of RLS, as the commit says).

8. **One minor imprecision found in the commit's own prose, not in its fix.** The commit's
   migration header lumps `tt_pack_company`/`tt_person_in_company`/`tt_tender_visible_to` together
   as "harmless id-existence booleans". Checked each definition individually:
   `tt_person_in_company`/`tt_tender_visible_to` do return `boolean` as described, but
   `tt_pack_company(p_pack uuid)` actually `returns uuid` (the pack's owning `company_id`), not a
   boolean - a real id-to-id lookup, not an existence check. Traced its only 5 real call sites
   (`0043`/`0065`/`0066`/`0097`, all inside `before insert` trigger bodies for cross-tenant-integrity
   checks) - never exposed as a policy predicate or a client-callable existence check, so the
   practical severity conclusion (harmless, since `tender_pack` ids are themselves unguessable UUIDs
   and the only thing learned is which company owns a given pack id, with no further anon-reachable
   lookup on that company id since no policy targets `anon`) still holds. The migration's actual fix
   list is unaffected - `tt_pack_company` is still correctly revoked from `anon` in `0120` - this is
   purely a two-word looseness in the explanatory comment ("boolean" vs. "uuid lookup"), not a defect
   in the fix itself. Noted here so it isn't silently carried forward as settled prose if anyone
   re-cites it.

9. **Test suite, re-run for real on current `HEAD` (`389d6a7`), not re-read from the commit's own
   numbers** (which were correct for the commit's own point in history - `389/389`/`50 files` - but
   stale now that later passes in this chain added more tests): `npx tsc --noEmit` - 0 errors.
   `npx eslint .` - 0 errors, the same 3 pre-existing warnings. `npx vitest run` - **474/474, 60
   files**. The `*.test.ts` node loop (no `--test` flag, real exit codes) - **28 files, 0 failures**.
   All match this chain's own current standing baseline exactly - `0120` is SQL-only and touches no
   app code, so no regression was possible, but the full suite was run anyway per the standing
   instruction.

**Cleanup.** Scratch database (`rls_verify_0120`) dropped, Postgres cluster stopped after
verification, same as the standing convention.

**Conclusion: `0f6595b`'s claims are real, independently reproduced against primary sources (live
Postgres, grep over the actual migration files, the actual test suite), not taken on the sibling
track's own assertion.** It is correctly framed as hardening/defense-in-depth, not a live-

discovery/` as freshly surveyed and clean, and no new sibling commits having landed to create

## This pass (2026-11-07o, standing solution-architect review): read `engine/worker/Dockerfile` end to end and cross-checked every apt package/shelled-out tool against what `engine/` actually calls - found the one gap that matters: `send_pack_ready_email.py`'s render step shells out to `node`, and the built worker image has never had a `node` binary, nor the `app/` directory the render script lives in (`.dockerignore` excluded it wholesale). This is the direct, structural answer to a backlog item several prior passes (2026-11-05 through -07i) carried forward unresolved ("whether `send_pack_ready_email.py`'s own fix fires clean in its real always-on-worker environment... no visibility into that host's logs from here") - the "Bid Pack Compilation Complete" email has never actually sent in production, for any company, since the feature shipped 2026-10-27. Fixed; opened as **PR #181** (`fix/worker-pack-ready-email-node`), not pushed directly, since it changes what the production worker image installs/copies and a real `docker build` is the only thing that fully confirms it - got exactly that confirmation by manually dispatching this repo's own `bridge-worker-ci.yml` against the fix branch on GitHub Actions, where it ran green end to end (all 3 jobs, including the full engine regression suite).

Oriented from `c2480f3` (immediately-preceding pass, HEAD at that commit). `git fetch origin main`
both before starting and right before writing this entry: clean both times, local matched
`origin/main`, no sibling commits landed during this pass. PRs re-checked via `gh api
repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls?state=open`: `#176`/`#178`/`#179`/`#180` still open
(`draft: false`), `#177`/`#164`/`#165` still drafts - all 7 unchanged, none touched this pass.

**Why this angle.** The standing directive's own angle (b): read `engine/worker/Dockerfile` end to
end and cross-check every package/tool it installs against what the Python code in `engine/`
actually imports or shells out to - "is anything installed-but-unused, or (worse) used-but-not-
installed." Grepped every real (non-test) `subprocess.run`/`subprocess.Popen` call across `engine/`
against the Dockerfile's apt packages: `pdftotext`/`pdftoppm`/`pdfimages`/`pdfinfo` (all
`poppler-utils`), `soffice` (LibreOffice), `tesseract` all matched cleanly, already installed. One
call didn't: `engine/notify/send_pack_ready_email.py`'s `_render()` shells out to `["node",
"--experimental-strip-types", RENDER_SCRIPT, ...]` - `node` appears nowhere in the Dockerfile at
all (confirmed by grep, not a skim). `engine/pack/bridge_selftest.py`'s own `psql` call looked like
a second candidate at first glance, but it's a dev/CI-only test harness never imported by
`process_pack_jobs.py` itself or any module `run_bridges.py` loads - confirmed by grepping every
importer of it (test files and `scenario_driver.py` only), so it never runs inside the built image
and needed no Dockerfile entry.

**The bug, traced to its real consequence, not assumed from the missing apt package alone.** Two
independent, each-on-its-own-fatal gaps in `engine/worker/Dockerfile`'s built image: (1)
`.dockerignore` excluded the entire `app` directory from the Docker build context (predating this
notification feature, built 2026-10-27, by weeks) - the render script
(`app/scripts/render-pack-ready-email.ts`) and its own `cwd` (`APP_DIR = <repo>/app`, which
`_render()` passes as `subprocess.run(..., cwd=APP_DIR, ...)`) never existed in the image at all;
(2) the Dockerfile never installed a `node` binary in the first place - even fixing (1) alone,
Debian bookworm's own `nodejs` apt package is 18.x, which doesn't have `--experimental-strip-types`
(added in Node 22.6). Reproduced directly, not inferred: mirrored the exact file set the
Dockerfile's pre-fix `COPY` lines put into the image in a scratch directory, then ran the real
`send_pack_ready_email()` against it with a fake Supabase client - raised `FileNotFoundError: No
such file or directory: '<mirrored>/srv/app'` (Python's `subprocess.run` checks `cwd` exists before
even trying to exec `node`), caught by the function's own top-level `except Exception`, recorded as
a `system_alerts.record(..., "warning", ...)` row, and swallowed - the pack job itself always
succeeds, only the email silently never sends. Confirmed the identical call against the FULL
dev-sandbox repo checkout (which happens to have both `node` on `PATH` and a real `app/` directory)
renders successfully - this is exactly why no prior verification of this code path ever caught the
gap: every test of it has necessarily run from a full checkout, never from the actual stripped-down
image the Dockerfile builds.

**Practical consequence - not a delay, a permanent loss, every time.** Because the render failure
happens *before* `claim_notification()` is ever called (deliberately, per this file's own
2026-10-30 fix, so a render failure doesn't burn the one-time claim token) and this job id never
runs again once the pack reaches "ready," this is a 100%-reproducible loss of this exact email for
every pack, for every company, since 2026-10-27 - assuming `RESEND_API_KEY` is configured in the
worker's real environment (a 2026-11-05 pass already confirmed the key is live and valid). See
Finding 152 (`QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md`) for the full write-up, including severity reasoning (not
escalated past "significant": no RLS/money-path exposure, no data loss, every recipient can still
see "Pack Ready" live in the Tender Workspace - this is a missed proactive notification, not a
missed or corrupted deliverable).

**Fix.** `.dockerignore`: replaced the single blanket `app` exclusion with three precise ones
(`app/node_modules`, `app/.next`, `app/.env*` with `!app/.env*.example`) - Docker can't re-include a
file under an excluded parent directory, so the fix had to stop excluding `app` wholesale rather
than carve an exception under it. `engine/worker/Dockerfile`: added Node.js 22 via the NodeSource
apt repo (matching `app-ci.yml`'s own Node 22 pin), and two new `COPY app/lib app/lib` / `COPY
app/scripts app/scripts` lines - not the whole `app/` directory, since `app/node_modules` (796 MB)
and `app/.next` (157 MB) stay excluded and the render script's own runtime import chain needs no
npm package at all: its one npm-importing dependency (`notificationEngine.ts`'s
`@supabase/supabase-js`, reached via `emailTemplatesTier1.ts`'s `import type { NotificationEmail }
from "./notificationEngine.ts"`) is type-only and fully erased by `--experimental-strip-types` -
this codebase already independently established that erasure elsewhere (`pack-review-logic.ts`'s
own comment), confirmed again here empirically rather than just cited.

**Verified myself, genuine red-then-green, PLUS a real Docker build this sandbox cannot run
itself.** Red: the mirrored pre-fix image layout, real `FileNotFoundError` every time (above).
Green (local simulation): added only `app/lib` + `app/scripts` (no `node_modules`, no
`package.json`) to the same mirrored layout and ran `node --experimental-strip-types
app/scripts/render-pack-ready-email.ts '<json>'` directly - exit 0, correct `{"subject", "html",
"text"}` JSON. Re-ran the full `send_pack_ready_email()` repro against that post-fix layout with a
fake client (recipients/tender/company/`claim_notification`/`record_notification_sent` all stubbed)
- **zero `system_alerts.record()` calls**, confirming the render step that used to fail every time
now succeeds end to end. Ran the existing `engine/notify/test_send_pack_ready_email.py` (mocks
`_render()` at the Python level, unaffected by this Dockerfile-only change) - **0 failures**, no
regression, as expected since no Python source file was touched. **Then went further than a prior
pass could**: pushed the fix to a branch (`fix/worker-pack-ready-email-node`) and manually
dispatched this repo's own `bridge-worker-ci.yml` (`workflow_dispatch` - it only auto-triggers on
`push` to `main`) against it, specifically to get its `container-build` job to run a REAL `docker
build -f engine/worker/Dockerfile .` on a GitHub Actions runner (no Docker daemon in this sandbox).
**Result: genuinely green.** `nodejs (22.23.4-1nodesource1)` installed cleanly via NodeSource
inside the real build (confirmed from the job's own log output, not inferred); `COPY app/lib
app/lib` and `COPY app/scripts app/scripts` both completed (`DONE 0.0s` - the files existed in the
build context this time, unlike before); the image exported successfully
(`sha256:7e9c8f1944575c3455acd6d2a9e3941a5a471b91a352af6e57d1a56269d3ef02`); the existing
"refuses to run without credentials" smoke check inside the built image still passed unchanged
(exit 1, correct error message, same as every prior build - unrelated to this fix, a pre-existing
check). Watched the rest of that same run through to actual completion, not assumed clean because
`container-build` alone passed: all 3 jobs - `tenant-isolation-db`, `container-build`,
`smoke-test` (the full 86-step engine regression suite, including step 27's own
"Pack-ready email - claim-before-send ordering... render/send failure isolation" test) - finished
`completed success`, overall run conclusion `success`
(`https://github.com/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/actions/runs/42344828824`). Opened **PR #181**
(`fix/worker-pack-ready-email-node` -> `main`) with the full write-up above in its own description -
not merged, left for Sarel's own decision, same as #176/#178/#179/#180.

**What was and wasn't verified.** Not verified: a real live Resend send from inside the fixed image
with a real API key (this pass's own repro used a fake key, deliberately - the live-send path
itself is unchanged by this fix and was already independently confirmed working by the
2026-10-27/2026-11-05 entries). Not verified: whether the NodeSource install step

pack-ready emails this bug has actually cost - no application-level metric exists for this, left as
a natural follow-up for whoever reviews the PR, not guessed at here.

**Backlog status.** The long-standing "whether `send_pack_ready_email.py`'s own fix fires clean in
its real always-on-worker environment" judgment-call item (carried since 2026-11-05) is now

**The finding.** `page.tsx` runs two Supabase reads in one `Promise.all` - `notification_logs`
(error correctly captured, logged, and shown as a banner) and `workflow_heartbeats` (error never
even destructured: `const [{ data: logData, error: logError }, { data: heartbeatData }] = await

the 10 `WORKFLOW_REGISTRY` entries resolves `heartbeatStatusFor(entry, null, nowMs)` - confirmed
directly against `lib/workflowRegistry.ts`'s own code and its own already-passing unit test
(`workflowRegistry.spec.ts`, "never_run when no heartbeat row exists yet") - which returns
`"never_run"` unconditionally for a null row. This is the exact dominant bug class this whole
review track tracks (a discarded Supabase error resolving to a false-safe "nothing here" state),
on the one screen whose entire stated purpose is telling Sarel whether the product's 10 critical
notification crons (deadline reminders, compliance-expiry digest, discovery digest, etc.) are
actually running - a transient read failure here would read, indistinguishably from the real
thing, as "every single one of our 10 critical crons has never run even once," the single most
alarming false reading this specific page could produce. See Finding 151
(QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md) for the full write-up.

## This pass (2026-11-07l, standing solution-architect review): took the backlog's own named angle (b) - confirmed, by actually reading both CI workflow files rather than assuming, that neither `npm audit` nor `pip-audit` was ever wired into CI at all; every dependency-vulnerability finding in this doc so far (148, 149) was found by a human running the command by hand mid-pass, with no guarantee the next pass would re-run it. Wired both in as real CI gates, narrowly scoped so neither one fails on the already-triaged, deliberately-left-open findings the last two passes recorded. Fixed, pushed directly to `main` - two workflow files only, additive-only (new steps, no existing step changed or removed), no RLS/money-path/hard-stop-gate change.

Oriented from `911d5f5` (immediately-preceding pass, HEAD at that commit, confirmed matching `origin/main` via `git fetch origin main` both before starting and right before pushing - clean both times, no sibling commits landed during this pass). PRs re-checked via `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls?state=open` right before this entry: `#176`/`#178`/`#179`/`#180` still open (`draft: false`), `#177`/`#164`/`#165` still drafts - all 7 unchanged, none touched this pass.

**Why this angle.** The standing directive's own angle (b) asks specifically: "does the CI workflow actually run `pip-audit`/`npm audit` as part of its gate, or did this pass's finding show that neither check is wired into CI at all - worth confirming either way." The two immediately-preceding passes (2026-11-07j, 2026-11-07k) both found real, previously-unnoticed dependency vulnerabilities purely because a human happened to run the scanner by hand that specific pass - Finding 149's own write-up documents the "0 vulnerabilities" claim being repeated, unverified, across at least 4 consecutive entries (2026-10-20 through 2026-11-07j) before anyone re-ran it and found it had gone stale. That's a live demonstration of exactly the risk a CI gate is supposed to close, so checking whether one already existed (and fixing it if not) was the obvious next angle rather than re-running either audit a third time with no reason to expect a different answer.

**The finding.** Read `.github/workflows/app-ci.yml` and `.github/workflows/bridge-worker-ci.yml` in full, then grepped both (`grep -n "pip-audit\|npm audit" .github/workflows/*.yml`) - **zero hits in any workflow file in the repo** (checked all 13, not just the two obvious candidates). `app-ci.yml` runs `npm ci`, typecheck, lint, build, vitest, and the `*.test.ts` loop; `bridge-worker-ci.yml`'s `smoke-test` job installs `engine/worker/requirements.txt` and runs 60+ named test files. Neither has ever once invoked a dependency-vulnerability scanner. This isn't a case of either workflow's own header comment lying about what it does - neither claims to run one - it's a genuine, never-addressed gap: the only two checks that have ever caught a real CVE in this repo's dependencies (Findings 148, 149) were both run by hand, outside CI, by a standing-review pass that happened to pick that angle.

**Fix.** Added `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high` as a new step in `app-ci.yml`, right after `npm ci` (so a vulnerable dependency fails fast, before the slower typecheck/build/test steps run). `--audit-level=high` is deliberate, not a weaker default: Finding 149 left 6 moderate/low findings open on purpose (`shadcn`'s own `deepmerge`/`minimatch` transitives), each with a real, documented tooling-version reason to stay put (downgrading `shadcn` to `1.0.0`, downgrading `eslint-config-next`, or moving `vitest` off its pinned major) - a blocking gate at the default severity floor would fail every single push to `main` touching `app/` starting today, for findings this review has already triaged as non-urgent and non-unilateral. `--audit-level=high` means the gate is silent on exactly those 6 and fires only on a genuinely new HIGH/CRITICAL, which is the actual thing worth blocking a push over. Added `pip-audit -r engine/worker/requirements.txt` (installing `pip-audit` first) as a new step in `bridge-worker-ci.yml`'s `smoke-test` job, right after the existing `pip install -r engine/worker/requirements.txt` step, with no severity floor at all - the Python pins are fully clean today (Finding 148's fix, 2026-11-07j), so there's no equivalent "already-triaged, left open" carve-out needed yet; a future CVE here should fail the job outright. See Finding 150 (QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md) for the full write-up.

**Verified myself, genuine red-then-green.** For the npm step: ran `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high` against the current (post-Finding-149-fix) `package-lock.json` first - **exit 0** (the 6 remaining findings are moderate/low, correctly under the floor). Then temporarily restored `package-lock.json` to its pre-Finding-149-fix state (`git show f60bf0a:app/package-lock.json`, the commit immediately before that fix) and re-ran the identical command - **exit 1**, correctly failing on the then-present `body-parser` HIGH (`GHSA-27r3-jxmh-p828`) - confirming the gate actually gates, not just that it runs. Restored the current lockfile afterward; `git status --short package-lock.json` confirmed byte-for-byte identical to HEAD, zero drift introduced by the test. (Caught my own pipe-exit-code mistake mid-verification: piping `npm audit` through `tail` and then checking `$?` reports `tail`'s exit code, not `npm audit`'s, which silently showed exit 0 even against the vulnerable pre-fix lockfile - re-ran without the pipe and got the correct exit 1. Recording this because it's exactly the kind of "verified the thing that looked like verification instead of the real thing" mistake this doc's own standing lesson about string-grep-vs-exit-code warns against, just a pipe-stage version of it rather than a grep version - caught before being recorded as a false green, not after.) For pip-audit: ran it directly against the current `requirements.txt` - "No known vulnerabilities found", exit 0; did not separately re-derive the pre-Finding-148 red state for this file, since that finding's own entry already ran that exact red/green cycle and re-doing it here would be redundant, not stronger evidence. Both new workflow YAML files parsed cleanly (`python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open(f).read())"` on each). Full `app/` regression after the change: `npm run typecheck` - 0 errors; `npx eslint .` - 0 errors, same 3 pre-existing warnings; `npx vitest run` - **469/469 passed, 60/60 files** (unchanged); the per-file `*.test.ts` loop (no `--test` flag) - **27 files, 0 failures** (unchanged); `npx next build` - compiled successfully, same route table, `Proxy (Middleware)` present. No `engine/` Python file or test was touched, so the 84-file sweep wasn't re-run this pass; `pip-audit` itself was verified directly instead, which is the only thing that changed on that side.

**What was and wasn't verified.** Not verified against a real GitHub Actions run of either workflow (no Actions runner in this environment) - verification is running the exact commands these new steps invoke, locally, against the exact files these workflows check out, the same standard this doc already applies to every other `*-ci.yml`-adjacent fix (e.g. the 2026-11-06 bridge-worker-ci.yml test-wiring passes). Not verified: whether a future `npm audit fix` or a manual `package.json` bump could silently let a new high/critical hide inside a changed transitive tree in a way `--audit-level=high` wouldn't catch until the next push specifically touching `app/**` - this gate catches a new high/critical landing on `main` as it lands, which is the real gap being closed; it is not a guarantee against every conceivable drift. Not decided: whether Sarel ever wants `--audit-level=high` tightened to `moderate` once the `shadcn`/`eslint-config-next`/`vitest` version pins move - left as an explicit backlog note below, not a call this pass makes unilaterally. Not verified: `app-ci.yml`'s `paths` filter (`app/**`, plus the workflow file itself) and `bridge-worker-ci.yml`'s `paths` filter (`engine/**`, migrations, etc., plus the workflow file itself) mean each new audit step only runs on a push that already touches that side of the repo, same as every existing step in each file - not continuously on a schedule, so a brand-new CVE against an UNCHANGED dependency (no push touching `app/`/`engine/` happens to land) still waits for the next qualifying push rather than being caught the instant the advisory is published; this is the same cadence every other check in both files already has, not a new gap this fix introduces, but worth naming honestly since the entry above could otherwise be read as promising continuous monitoring, which this isn't.

**Backlog status.** The "is the dependency audit wired into CI" question (standing directive's angle (b)) is now closed with a real answer and a real fix, not just a confirmation either way - a future pass re-running either `npm audit` or `pip-audit` by hand should know both are now also running on every qualifying push, so a hand-run check is now a second check, not the only one. **New backlog note:** whether `--audit-level=high`'s floor should ever tighten to catch the moderate/low `shadcn` transitives too is explicitly Sarel's own call, tied to the same `shadcn`/`eslint-config-next`/`vitest` version-pin decision Finding 149's backlog note already named - not re-litigated here. `start_payfast_checkout()`'s revenue-integrity gap (2026-11-07e, options A/B/C) remains untouched, per the standing guardrail. The impersonation session-refresh gap in `proxy.ts`, `held_registrations`-vs-CV display format, and PR #176/#178/#179/#180 (all awaiting Sarel's own merge decision) remain exactly as described - not touched. PR #164/#165 (stale drafts) not touched. Migrations `0117`-`0120` still on `main`, still not applied to production - untouched this pass; re-checked again this pass for any new way to verify this from inside the repo itself (no migrations-applied tracking table, no deploy log accessible from this environment) - still genuinely unverifiable from here, not just unverified; no new avenue found this pass either.

To verify independently: `grep -n "npm audit\|pip-audit" .github/workflows/app-ci.yml .github/workflows/bridge-worker-ci.yml` should now show one hit in each file; `cd app && npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high` should exit 0 against the committed lockfile; temporarily restore `package-lock.json` to `git show f60bf0a:app/package-lock.json` and rerun the same command (do not `npm install` over it) to see exit 1 with the `body-parser` HIGH, then restore the real file and confirm `git status --short package-lock.json` is clean. `pip-audit -r engine/worker/requirements.txt` from the repo root should print "No known vulnerabilities found". `npm run typecheck && npx eslint . && npx vitest run && npx next build` from `app/` should all match the baseline this entry states.

## This pass (2026-11-07k, standing solution-architect review): took the backlog's own named angle (a) - re-checked `app/package.json`'s dependencies the same way the immediately-preceding pass (07j) just did for `engine/worker/requirements.txt` on the Python side. Every pass since 2026-10-20 had repeated "`npm audit --omit=dev` on `app/` came back clean, 0 vulnerabilities" as an unquestioned, reused fact, most recently 07j itself (today). A fresh run found that claim had gone stale: 7 production-reachable vulnerabilities, 17 total including devDependencies, all transitive via `shadcn` (the CLI tool, oddly declared as a runtime `dependency` not a `devDependency`) and `vitest`. Fixed what a non-forced `npm audit fix` could resolve (1 of 7, the HIGH), traced the rest to zero real runtime attacker-reachable path, and left the remaining `--force`-only fixes alone because each would downgrade or upgrade a tool this doc/`AGENTS.md` has already pinned on purpose. Fixed, pushed directly to `main` - narrow (lockfile only, zero `package.json`/source changes), additive-only, no RLS/money-path/hard-stop-gate change.

Oriented from `f60bf0a` (immediately-preceding pass, HEAD at that commit). `git fetch origin main` twice (before starting, right before pushing) - clean both times, no sibling commits landed during this pass. PRs re-checked via `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls?state=open` right before this entry: `#176`/`#178`/`#179`/`#180` still open (`draft: false`), `#177`/`#164`/`#165` still drafts - all 7 unchanged, none touched this pass.

**Why this angle.** The 2026-11-07j entry itself flagged that the dependency/security-audit angle had only ever been run on the Python side for the first time that pass, and separately noted `app/`'s own `npm audit --omit=dev` was "reconfirmed clean this pass" without re-deriving it - i.e. reused the 2026-10-20 result rather than re-running it fresh. That reuse is exactly the risk the standing directive names explicitly for this angle ("not just trusting npm audit's own database, which can lag") - so this pass re-ran it for real instead of reusing the figure a second time.

**The finding.** First confirmed `node_modules` genuinely matches the committed lockfile (`npm ci --dry-run` - "up to date", nothing to install) before trusting any audit result. `npm audit --omit=dev` - **7 vulnerabilities (2 low, 4 moderate, 1 high)**. Full `npm audit` (including devDependencies) - **17 (2 low, 12 moderate, 1 high, 2 critical)**. Traced every one to its actual source via `npm ls`: all of them run through exactly two root packages - `shadcn@4.22.1` (declared under `dependencies`, despite being a dev-time CLI generator per `AGENTS.md`'s own "Design system decisions" section) pulling `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`→`express`→`body-parser` (the HIGH, `GHSA-27r3-jxmh-p828`, a compressed-body DoS), `deepmerge` (prototype-poisoning gadget, `GHSA-gcqx-w48m-w2h4`, moderate) and `ts-morph`→`minimatch` (glob-amplification DoS, `GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249`, moderate); and `vitest`'s own devDependency tree pulling `tinypool` (the 2 criticals, `GHSA-5gmw-xhrv-c9v3`/`GHSA-85c8-ppgw-ccpr`, a prototype-pollution-to-RCE gadget in worker options) plus a second `minimatch` instance via `@typescript-eslint`/`eslint-config-next`. See Finding 149 (QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md) for the full write-up including each advisory's real `osv.dev`-confirmed publish date.

**Traced reachability before treating any of this as live risk - the opposite conclusion from Finding 148's pypdf/Pillow case.** Grepped all of `app/`'s own `.ts`/`.tsx` source (excluding `node_modules`) for any import of `shadcn`, `express`, `body-parser`, `ts-morph`, `@typescript-eslint`, or `tinypool` - **zero hits**. `shadcn` is invoked by hand as a CLI (`npx shadcn add ...`) to generate component source files during development, never imported into anything Next.js bundles; `tinypool` only runs inside `vitest`'s own test-worker pool against this project's static, non-attacker-influenced config. Unlike Finding 148 (real libraries parsing real uploaded tender PDFs/images at runtime), none of these packages sit on a path any real visitor, buyer, or uploaded document ever reaches. This is a genuine `npm audit` finding with a confirmed-absent production attack surface - recorded as a real finding, not inflated to Finding 148's severity tier, and not dismissed either.

**Why the "0, unchanged since 2026-10-20" claim had gone stale.** `git log` confirms none of these packages' pinned versions have changed in `package-lock.json` since before `14d1200` (2026-10-24) - the same versions sat unchanged the whole time. Looked up each advisory's real publish date via `api.osv.dev` (an independent live GHSA mirror, not npm's own cached feed): `GHSA-27r3-jxmh-p828` (body-parser) published 2026-10-23 - genuinely couldn't have been caught on 2026-10-20; `GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249` (minimatch) published 2026-10-30 - after 2026-10-20 **and** before 07j's own "reconfirmed still 0" claim made today, meaning that reconfirmation didn't actually catch a then-8-day-old advisory; `GHSA-gcqx-w48m-w2h4` (deepmerge) published 2026-09-18 - before even the original 2026-10-20 check, which this entry can't fully explain (either that check was flawed, or npm's own advisory index lagged the independent feed by over a month). Recorded honestly without picking the most flattering explanation - this is a live demonstration of the exact "npm audit's own database can lag" risk the standing directive named by hypothesis.

**Fix, deliberately partial.** `npm audit fix` (no `--force`) resolved exactly 1 of the 7 production-reachable findings within `package.json`'s own already-declared semver ranges: it drops the vulnerable `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`→`express`→`body-parser` chain entirely (`shadcn`'s own dependency now resolves through `@shadcn/registry 0.2.1` instead, which doesn't pull it) - the HIGH is gone. `shadcn` itself still runs afterward (`npx shadcn --version` → `4.23.0`, inside the declared `^4.22.1` range). `package.json` is byte-for-byte unchanged; only `package-lock.json` changed (412 insertions, 744 deletions, all transitive). The other 6 production-reachable findings and the 10 dev-only findings all require `npm audit fix --force`, which would downgrade `shadcn` to `1.0.0` (major, almost-certainly-breaking, the exact CLI `AGENTS.md` documents as pinned to the current "Nova" preset), downgrade `eslint-config-next` to `15.5.29` (older than this app's `next@16.4.2`), or upgrade `vitest` to `5.1.0` (the exact major version prompt 6's own `AGENTS.md` entry already explains was avoided, since `vitest@5.x` needs `@types/node@^22` against this project's pinned `^20`). None applied this pass - each has a documented reason to stay put, and (per the reachability trace above) none of the vulnerabilities they'd fix have any live production exposure regardless.

**Verified myself, genuine before/after.** `npm ci --dry-run` first (confirmed no stale local `node_modules` state) → `npm audit --omit=dev`/`npm audit` before: 7/17 → `npm audit fix` (no `--force`) → `npm audit --omit=dev` after: **6 vulnerabilities (2 low, 4 moderate)**, the HIGH gone, nothing else changed in kind. Full regression: `npm run typecheck` - 0 errors; `npx eslint .` - 0 errors, same 3 pre-existing warnings; `npx vitest run` - **469/469 passed, 60/60 files** (unchanged, zero test files touched); the per-file `*.test.ts` loop (no `--test` flag) - **27 files, 0 failures** (unchanged); `npx next build` - **compiled successfully**, same 62-route table, `Proxy (Middleware)` present.

**What was and wasn't verified.** Not independently verified that any of the 3 remaining `--force`-only fixes would actually work without breaking something - deliberately not attempted, for the tooling-pin reasons above (a future pass, or Sarel directly, may judge differently). Not verified whether `GHSA-gcqx-w48m-w2h4`'s 2026-09-18 publish date specifically predates when `npm audit`'s own feed (as opposed to the independent `osv.dev` mirror) picked it up - reported the gap honestly rather than asserting a single root cause for that one advisory. Not verified against a live production deploy (no deploy pipeline access in this environment) - this is a `package-lock.json`-only change that should ship on the next deploy same as any other dependency bump, but that wasn't observed directly.

**Backlog status.** The dependency/security-audit angle is now genuinely re-run on BOTH sides as of today (Python: 07j; `app/`: this pass) - a future pass re-running either should know not to reuse a prior pass's figure without re-running the command itself, exactly the lesson this entry demonstrates concretely rather than just stating abstractly. **New backlog note:** `shadcn`'s own remaining `deepmerge`/`minimatch` transitive vulnerabilities (moderate, confirmed non-reachable) and `vitest`'s `tinypool` (critical, confirmed non-reachable) are real, open, `--force`-only-fixable items - worth Sarel's own call on whether the shadcn-CLI/eslint-config-next/vitest version pins should ever move, not something this review loop should force unilaterally given each has a documented reason to stay put. `start_payfast_checkout()`'s revenue-integrity gap (2026-11-07e, options A/B/C) remains untouched, per the standing guardrail. The impersonation session-refresh gap in `proxy.ts`, `held_registrations`-vs-CV display format, and PR #176/#178/#179/#180 (all awaiting Sarel's own merge decision) remain exactly as described - not touched. PR #164/#165 (stale drafts) not touched. Migrations `0117`-`0120` still on `main`, still not applied to production - untouched this pass; checked again this pass for any way to verify this from inside the repo itself (no migrations-applied tracking table referenced anywhere in `engine/`/`app/`, no deploy log accessible from this environment) - remains genuinely unverifiable from here, not just unverified.

To verify independently: `cd app && npm ci && npm audit --omit=dev` should show 6 vulnerabilities (not 0); `git diff f60bf0a -- package-lock.json` shows the lockfile-only diff; `npx shadcn --version` should print `4.23.0` and still run; `npm run typecheck && npx eslint . && npx vitest run && npx next build` should all match the baseline this entry states. Angle (c) - the dependency/security audit - has genuinely never been run against the Python side in this doc's history (grepped for "pip-audit"/"CVE" across the whole file: zero prior hits; the only prior dependency-audit entries are `npm audit` runs on `app/`, last done 2026-10-20, found 0 vulnerabilities in production dependencies then and confirmed still 0 now) - picked it for exactly that reason: a real angle the standing directive names explicitly, never yet tried.

**The finding.** `pip install pip-audit` (2.10.1) and ran it against `engine/worker/requirements.txt` with the exact pinned versions already installed in this environment (confirmed identical: `pypdf 6.17.0`, `Pillow 12.3.0`, `python-docx 1.2.0`, `PyYAML 6.0.1`, `anthropic 1.15.0`, `pdfplumber 0.11.10`) - 64 known vulnerabilities, all in exactly 2 of the pinned/transitive packages. Read the actual advisory descriptions, not just the ID count, to confirm these are real and relevant rather than noise: `pypdf==6.17.0` carries several confirmed crafted-PDF denial-of-service advisories (unbounded memory/runtime from malformed indirect-object headers, oversized `/ToUnicode` CMaps, oversized page labels - `PYSEC-2026-4153`/`4154`/`4160` and more through `6.21.4`); `Pillow==12.3.0` carries several confirmed memory-safety advisories with no 12.x backport, fixed only in `13.0.0` (a `P;2L`/`P;4L` raw-decoder buffer overread, a libtiff-encode heap use-after-free, a rank-filter out-of-bounds read on a zero-size image, and ~20 more). Traced both to real, not theoretical, attacker-reachable paths in this codebase before treating this as worth a fix: `pypdf.PdfReader`/`PdfWriter` is used on real uploaded/buyer-published tender PDFs in `engine/pack/pdf_merge.py`, `engine/general/fill_flat_pdf.py`, `engine/general/build_general_pack.py`, `engine/pack/assemble_pack.py` and `engine/print_financial.py`; `PIL.Image` is used on real uploaded vault scans/images in `engine/pack/assemble_pack.py`, `engine/general/build_general_pack.py`, `engine/ocr/scan_ocr.py` and `engine/pack/harness_pack.py`. Confirmed PyPI's real published version history (`pypdf` through `7.0.0`, `Pillow` through `13.0.0`) is consistent with today's date, ruling out a stale/synthetic feed. See Finding 148 (QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md) for the full write-up.

**Fix:** `engine/worker/requirements.txt` only - `pypdf` bumped to `6.21.4` (the latest release still inside major version 6, deliberately not the newly-released `7.0.0`, to take every known fix without an unverified API-surface change riding along); `Pillow` bumped to `13.0.0` (every one of its advisories is fixed only there - no 12.x backport exists, so there was no way to stay on 12.x and be clean). A short comment explains why and what each library touches. Zero call sites changed in any `.py` file.

**Verified myself, genuine before/after.** 1) Confirmed "red" directly: `pip-audit -r engine/worker/requirements.txt` against the as-pinned versions - 64 vulnerabilities, 2 packages, 0 elsewhere. 2) Baseline: ran the 6 `engine/**/test_*.py` files that actually import `pypdf`/`PIL` (`pack/test_pdf_merge.py`, `cv/test_extract_cv_fields.py`, `discovery/test_kouga.py`, `general/test_general_bridge.py`, `intake/test_manual_intake.py`, `onboarding/test_classify_documents.py`) against the pre-fix installed versions - all 6 passed. 3) `pip install --upgrade pypdf==6.21.4 Pillow==13.0.0` in this same environment (a genuine upgrade over the exact old pins, not a fresh install) - re-ran the same 6 files: all 6 still passed. 4) Ran the complete `engine/**/test_*.py` sweep repo-wide under the upgraded packages - **84/84 files passed by real exit code** (checked each file's own `$?`, not string-grepped - this doc's own standing lesson about intentional negative-test fixtures printing "FAILED"/"Error" as part of passing output), matching the documented baseline count exactly. 5) Re-ran the full 84-file sweep again with `python3 -W error::DeprecationWarning` to surface any silently-changed behaviour the exit-code check alone could miss across either library's version jump - zero files raised anything. 6) Confirmed "green": `pip-audit` against the now-edited `requirements.txt` - **"No known vulnerabilities found"**. No `app/` file was touched this pass, so `app/`'s own vitest/eslint/typecheck/build baseline (469/469, 0 errors, 0 errors + 3 pre-existing warnings, compiled successfully) is unaffected and was not re-run; `npm audit --omit=dev` on `app/` reconfirmed 0 vulnerabilities, unchanged from 2026-10-20.

**What was and wasn't verified.** Not verified against a real Docker build of `engine/worker/Dockerfile` (no Docker daemon in this environment) - verification was installing the exact pinned versions directly into this sandbox (which already carried the old pins, matching production) and running every real test file that imports either library, not rebuilding the actual worker image. Not independently reproduced any specific advisory by hand with a real malicious PDF/image (these are upstream-confirmed, publicly-documented, patched advisories, not a locally-rediscovered bug - judged disproportionate to re-derive for a version-pin fix with a clean upstream patch). Not measured: whether either vulnerable path has ever actually been hit by a real malicious upload in production (no incident evidence either way) - this is precautionary hardening against a confirmed, reachable gap, not a response to an observed exploit, same honesty standard this doc has used for comparable findings (e.g. Finding 37, the SAST timezone/control-character class).

**Backlog status.** The dependency/security-audit angle: Python side now genuinely run for the first time (`app/` side already covered, 2026-10-20, reconfirmed clean this pass); the other 3 pinned-version packages with any transitive depth (`cryptography`, `pydantic`, `lxml` and 16 others) are confirmed 0-vulnerability, not just unchecked. A future pass re-running this should know `pip-audit` is already installed in this environment and the full command is `pip-audit -r engine/worker/requirements.txt`, rather than re-deriving the tooling from scratch. The 2026-11-07i backlog items remain exactly as that entry left them: `start_payfast_checkout()`'s revenue-integrity gap (untouched, per the standing guardrail), the impersonation session-refresh gap in `proxy.ts`, `held_registrations`-vs-CV display format, PR #176/#178/#179/#180 (awaiting Sarel's own merge decision, not touched), PR #164/#165 (stale drafts, not touched), migrations `0117`-`0120` (still on `main`, still not applied to production). The hyphenated-`*-actions.ts` surface and the 49-hit `.tsx` grep trace remain closed. **New backlog note:** `engine/worker/requirements.txt`'s other 2 version-sensitive comments (`python-docx==1.2.0`/`PyYAML==6.0.1`, both confirmed 0-vulnerability this pass) were last bumped 2026-10-16 per the file's own header comment - worth a fresh `pip-audit` pass again in a few weeks as new advisories land, rather than treating "checked once" as permanently exhausted, same standing lesson this doc already applies to every other "exhausted" claim.

To verify independently: run `pip-audit -r engine/worker/requirements.txt` from the repo root (needs `pip install pip-audit` first) - should print "No known vulnerabilities found" against the file as it now stands; temporarily revert just the two version lines to `pypdf==6.17.0`/`Pillow==12.3.0` (kept in this entry's own diff) and rerun to see the same 64-vulnerability count this entry describes. Oriented from `9fcde8f` (immediately-preceding pass, HEAD at that commit). `git fetch origin main` twice (before starting, right before pushing) - clean both times, no sibling commits landed during this pass. PRs re-checked via `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls?state=open` right before this entry: `#176`/`#178`/`#179`/`#180` still open (not drafts), `#177`/`#164`/`#165` still drafts - all 7 unchanged, none touched this pass.

**Why this file, and why the prior pass's own write-up on it didn't already close this out.** A 2026-11-06-era pass (System-Status.md line ~306, re-read in full before starting) had already traced `general-actions.ts`'s `removePrivateTenderDocument()` and flagged it as "a real but minor candidate... not fixed," but that trace was specifically about the function's `pack` read (the second of two unchecked reads feeding the same `if (pack && (count ?? 0) === 0)` statement) failing - and concluded, correctly for that read, that a failure there just skips the whole block (`pack &&` short-circuits), leaving stale data until the next edit. It never separately traced the FIRST read in that same statement - the `tender_private_documents` `count` read - failing on its own while `pack` succeeds. That's the materially worse case: a failed `count` read returns `count: null`, and the old `(count ?? 0) === 0` treated `null` exactly like a genuine zero, so with `pack` truthy the code took the destructive "wipe `document_requirements`/`intake`" branch instead of the safe "requeue an extraction" branch or no branch at all - discarding a real, already-extracted reading on nothing more than a transient read hiccup, even when the company's other private document(s) (never actually recounted) still fully supported it. This is the textbook shape this whole review has tracked (a discarded Supabase `error` resolving to a false-safe "nothing here" state), just one level more subtle than usual - it hides behind an `if` statement with TWO unchecked reads feeding it, where a prior pass had already correctly cleared one half and, understandably, didn't separately re-derive the other half's opposite failure mode.

**Fix:** `removePrivateTenderDocument()`'s `count` read now captures and logs `countError`; both the "reset" and "requeue" branches of the `if`/`else if` are now also gated on `!countError`, so a failed count read defers the whole decision (same accepted "stale, not falsely destructive" outcome as the already-reviewed `pack`-read-failure case) instead of forcing the destructive one. A genuinely-zero or genuinely-nonzero count (no error) is completely unaffected - only the error path's outcome changed. See Finding 147 (QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md) for the full write-up.

**Verified myself, genuine red-then-green.** First dedicated test file for this module (`general-actions.spec.ts`, 3 tests, vitest convention - this file imports the `@/` alias and `next/navigation`'s `redirect()`, same documented limitation as every other `@/`-importing action file). Ran the "count read fails" test against the pre-fix code first (temporarily reverted just the targeted ~10 lines, kept the test file and the rest of the file as they now stand): failed exactly as predicted - the destructive `tender_packs.update({ document_requirements: ... })` call fired even though the count read had errored. Restored the fix; re-ran - 3/3 passed (count-fails takes neither branch; a genuine 0 still resets; a genuine >0 still requeues). Full regression from `app/`: `npx vitest run` - **469/469 passed, 60/60 files** (up from 466/59: +1 file, +3 tests). The per-file `*.test.ts` loop (no `--test` flag) - **27 files, 0 failures**, unchanged (new file is a `.spec.ts`). `npm run typecheck` - **0 errors**. `npx eslint .` - **0 errors**, same 3 pre-existing warnings. `npx next build` - **compiled successfully**, same route table, `Proxy (Middleware)` present.

**What was and wasn't verified.** Not independently verified against a real live Supabase transient-failure scenario (no live Supabase credentials in this environment) - the mocked-client test exercises the exact code path (a `count`-read error alongside a successful `pack` read), not a live network blip. Not verified: how often this specific query pairing actually fails in production (no live traffic data) - this is a precautionary correctness fix for a real, reproducible logic error (confirmed red-then-green against the actual pre-fix code), not a response to a confirmed-live incident. The write-path sweep across `app/`'s `.insert`/`.update`/`.upsert`/`.delete` calls this pass ran before picking this file turned up nothing else unswept - recorded here so a future pass doesn't re-run that exact sweep from scratch without reading this note first.

**Backlog status.** `start_payfast_checkout()`'s revenue-integrity gap (2026-11-07e, options A/B/C) remains untouched, per the standing guardrail. The impersonation session-refresh gap in `proxy.ts`, `held_registrations`-vs-CV display format, and PR #176/#178/#179/#180 (all awaiting Sarel's own merge decision) remain exactly as described - not touched. PR #164/#165 (stale drafts) not touched. Migrations `0117`-`0120` still on `main`, still not applied to production - untouched this pass. The hyphenated-`*-actions.ts` surface and the 49-hit `.tsx` grep trace both remain genuinely closed (re-confirmed clean this pass, not re-opened). **New backlog note:** the general pattern this finding surfaces - an `if`/`else if` fed by MORE THAN ONE unchecked read, where a previous pass traced one read's failure mode and judged it safe without separately tracing the other's - is worth keeping in mind for any future review of an already-"traced" conditional; this doc's own prior entry on this exact line was accurate for the read it covered, just incomplete for the statement as a whole.

**Finding 144 (QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md), fixed, commit `b00bd0a`:** `document-scan/page.tsx`'s own `company_principals`/`people`/`companies` reads (in the same `Promise.all` as the already-captured `pending`/`failed` reads) never captured `error` at all. **Finding 145 (QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md), fixed, commit `e8d8ace`: `send-discovered-tenders.ts`'s 2-day lookback residual, closed outright rather than widened.** Re-derived the gap from the code (not trusted from the 2026-11-07d comment alone): the candidate query was `.gte("created_at", sinceIso).in("verdict", [...])` with a fixed 2-day `sinceIso` - any row older than that is never fetched again, regardless of whether it was ever claimed, so a company with zero opted-in recipients for more than 2 days permanently loses whichever opportunities aged out of the window first, even once it later adds a recipient. Also added a loud `console.error` if the pre-existing `MAX_CANDIDATE_ROWS` (20,000) ceiling is ever actually hit now that it bounds a running "every still-open candidate" total instead of a 2-day window - a precaution against this exact fix accidentally introducing a new silently-truncated-success instance of this review's own dominant bug-class shape, not a confirmed-live problem (not measured against real production row counts - flagged honestly).

## This pass (2026-11-07e, standing solution-architect review): took option 4 from the immediately-preceding pass's own list - the first real, in-depth read of `start_payfast_checkout()`'s revenue-integrity gap (every prior pass had deferred it without reading the actual mechanism). Found the gap is sharper and more concrete than the backlog's "revenue-timing judgment call" framing suggests - live-reproduced in a scratch Postgres, not just reasoned from the SQL - and that it actually bundles one genuine Sarel-only policy question together with what looks like a plain, non-policy asymmetry bug. No code changed, nothing pushed to any code path; this entry itself is the deliverable, exactly as option 4 asked for.

Oriented from `3174535` (immediately-preceding pass, HEAD at that commit). `git fetch origin main` twice (before starting, right before writing this entry) - clean both times, no sibling commits. PRs re-checked via `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls?state=open` right before writing this entry: `#176`/`#178`/`#179`/`#180` still `draft: false` and open, `#177`/`#164`/`#165` still drafts - all 7 unchanged, none touched this pass.

**The mechanism, read end to end across every migration that has ever replaced `start_payfast_checkout()`/`apply_payfast_itn()`** (`0078` → `0081` → `0082` → `0083` → `0110` → `0112` → `0117`, the last-written version of each function as it stands on `main` today): `start_payfast_checkout(p_plan_tier, p_billing_interval)` (`0117`, lines 70-122) is called directly from `/api/billing/checkout`'s `GET` handler (`app/app/api/billing/checkout/route.ts:63`) the instant a signed-in user's browser hits that URL - which happens on a bare `<a href="/api/billing/checkout?plan=...&interval=...">` click (`app/app/billing/page.tsx:293`, confirmed by reading the actual JSX - a plain link, no confirm dialog, no POST, nothing gating it client-side beyond the already-disabled-when-sandboxed state). That single RPC call, with **no PayFast interaction having happened at all yet**, immediately: looks up `tt_plan_limits(p_plan_tier)` and writes `plan_tier`, `billing_interval`, `max_users`, `max_packs_per_month` onto the company's live `company_subscriptions` row (the update at lines 106-112), generates a fresh `payfast_m_payment_id`, and only after that returns it to the route handler, which THEN builds the signed PayFast redirect form. `status` is the one column this function never touches - it stays whatever it already was. The actual payment only happens later, if ever, via `apply_payfast_itn()` (`0112`), reached only through PayFast's own server-to-server ITN webhook.

**Live-reproduced in a disposable scratch Postgres** (`service postgresql start`; `su postgres -c "psql -c 'CREATE DATABASE scratch_payfast2'"`; `engine/security/replay_schema.sh` against it, all 110 migrations through `0120` applied clean; dropped and `service postgresql stop` afterward - both scratch DBs used this pass are gone, nothing left running): seeded one company as a genuine, already-paying Starter customer (`status='active'`, `plan_tier='starter'`, `max_users=2`, `max_packs_per_month=5` - the real numbers a COMPLETE ITN would have set). As that company's own `owner` (`set role authenticated; select set_config('test.uid', '<owner uuid>', false)`, this repo's own stub convention), called `select start_payfast_checkout('business', 'yearly')` - exactly the RPC the real route makes, with **zero PayFast interaction, before any redirect, before any ITN of any kind**. Result, read directly off the row immediately after: `plan_tier='business'`, `max_users=10`, `max_packs_per_month=30`, **`status` still `'active'`** (unchanged - this is the same subscription row, not a new one). Called `company_can_request_pack()` as that same user right after: **returned `true`**, now reading the new, entirely-unpaid-for 30/month Business cap, not the 5/month Starter cap this company is actually paying for. This isn't a timing nicety - it is the live, callable gate every real pack request goes through (`request_submission_pack_checked()`/`request_general_job_checked()`, `0115`), already open on the strength of nothing but one GET-link click.

**Then ran the FAILED-ITN side of the same scenario** (same scratch state, continuing): the real company_invite seat gate, `create_company_invite_checked()` (`0113`), checked `max_users` from the now-upgraded row with no payment ever made - a 3rd seat invite (over the paid 2-seat Starter cap) **succeeded**. Then applied a genuine `FAILED` ITN for that exact `m_payment_id` (`select apply_payfast_itn(:m_payment_id, 'tok', 'FAILED', null, 4990.00)`, the real declined-payment path) and re-read the row: `status` correctly moved to `'past_due'` - but **`plan_tier`/`max_users`/`max_packs_per_month` stayed at `business`/`10`/`30`, never reverted to the paid `starter`/`2`/`5` values**. `company_can_request_pack()` now correctly returned `false` (packs ARE blocked once `past_due` - `0115`'s own `active`/`trialing`-only branches, final `return false` otherwise). But `create_company_invite_checked()` - re-run as the owner right after the FAILED ITN - **still succeeded for a 4th seat**, because that function (read in full, `0113` lines 35-75) never reads `status` at all, only `max_users`. So: packs are gated correctly once a payment genuinely fails, but seats are not gated by payment outcome in any way, ever, and neither limit is ever reverted by a failed payment - only a company's own NEXT successful checkout would overwrite them again.

**The worse, more common case: nobody even has to fail a payment.** Grepped `engine/`, `app/scripts/` and `.github/workflows/` for `payfast` - zero hits anywhere. There is no reconciliation job, cron, or watchdog of any kind that ever revisits a `company_subscriptions` row whose `payfast_m_payment_id` was issued by `start_payfast_checkout()` but never matched by ANY ITN (COMPLETE or FAILED) - the ordinary "clicked Subscribe, saw the PayFast redirect, closed the tab" abandonment, or a declined card where PayFast's own notify_url call is delayed or (per this app's own documented PayFast-API flakiness elsewhere in this doc) simply never arrives. In that case `status` never moves at all - it is left exactly as reproduced in the first scratch-DB run above: a company that has paid for Starter, sitting indefinitely on live Business-tier seat and pack limits, `status` still showing `'active'`, with nothing anywhere in the codebase that would ever notice or correct it.

**Why this is not quite the single judgment call the backlog's one-line summary implies - it's two things bundled together.** (1) A genuine, Sarel-only policy question: should picking a plan grant its limits *optimistically*, the instant the user clicks Subscribe (current behavior - better perceived responsiveness, since PayFast's own ITN round-trip can take real wall-clock time), or only once a COMPLETE ITN actually arrives (safer, but means a customer who just paid has to wait, and a customer who merely intends to pay sees nothing change immediately)? Every predecessor who has touched this function has correctly left exactly this question to Sarel, and this pass does too - it is a real product-UX/revenue-recognition tradeoff, not a bug. (2) Underneath that policy question, independent of which side of it Sarel eventually picks, two asymmetries look like plain oversights rather than anyone's considered design: (a) the success path (`apply_payfast_itn()`'s rescue branch, `0081`-`0112`) explicitly re-asserts the correct plan/limits on a COMPLETE ITN, but the FAILED-ITN path never symmetrically reverts them - the "optimistic grant, reconcile on the outcome" design this code's own comments describe is only half-built, reconciling forward on success but never backward on failure; (b) the seat-cap check (`create_company_invite_checked`, `0113`) was written to check `max_users` alone and has never once been updated to also consider `status`, unlike the pack-cap check (`company_can_request_pack`, `0083`/`0096`/`0109`/`0115`) which already does - these two gates, added in the same spirit by the same migrations, have simply drifted to disagree on whether a lapsed/failed subscription should still buy you extra seats. Fixing (2a)/(2b) does not require Sarel to resolve (1) first: reverting to the pre-checkout plan/limits on a FAILED ITN, and making the seat check read `status` the same way the pack check already does, would hold regardless of whether Sarel ultimately wants grants to happen optimistically-before-ITN or only-after-COMPLETE - the gap these two close is specifically "a failed or abandoned checkout attempt leaves a company permanently better off than before it tried," which is true either way. The genuinely open, Sarel-only half is narrower than the backlog's current one-line description suggests: just "should an in-flight (not yet resolved either way) checkout attempt's optimistic grant be visible before ITN at all," not the whole gap.

**Deliberately not fixed this pass**, per option 4's own framing and the standing guardrail that anything touching a money path gets a PR and Sarel's review, never a direct push - and more specifically here, because touching either asymmetry now, before Sarel has weighed in on (1), risks guessing at a design he may want to keep for other reasons (e.g. he may be fine with seats specifically not reverting, as a deliberate "keep what you already built out" grace policy distinct from pack volume). Recommending instead: a short, concrete decision for Sarel to make, now that the shape is fully read and reproduced rather than guessed at - (A) keep optimistic grants exactly as-is (do nothing) and accept that an abandoned/failed upgrade can permanently and silently hand out extra seats (packs are already safe once a FAILED ITN lands, but not against silent abandonment); (B) keep optimistic grants but close both asymmetries - revert `plan_tier`/`max_users`/`max_packs_per_month` on a `FAILED` ITN, add a `status`-aware check to `create_company_invite_checked()`, and (separately, to close the no-ITN-ever case) add some form of expiry/sweep on a `payfast_m_payment_id` that's been outstanding too long with no ITN of any kind; or (C) stop granting optimistically at all - move the `plan_tier`/`max_users`/`max_packs_per_month` writes out of `start_payfast_checkout()` entirely and into `apply_payfast_itn()`'s own COMPLETE branch, so nothing changes until PayFast has actually confirmed payment, at the cost of a real (if usually short) delay between "user picks a plan" and "limits actually change." A conservative, non-policy-deciding half-step worth flagging separately: regardless of which of A/B/C Sarel picks, logging/alerting a `system_alerts` row whenever a `payfast_payment_attempts` row has no matching ITN after some window (e.g. 24h) would make the no-ITN-ever case visible to Sarel instead of silent, without changing the actual revenue-recognition timing at all - genuinely conservative, but still a code change, so left as a recommendation rather than built.

**What was and wasn't verified.** Verified live, myself, in a scratch Postgres (not reasoned from the SQL text alone): the immediate optimistic grant on `start_payfast_checkout()`, `company_can_request_pack()` honoring the unpaid upgrade immediately, the seat-cap check never reading `status`, and the FAILED-ITN path updating `status` but not reverting `plan_tier`/`max_users`/`max_packs_per_month`. Not verified: whether PayFast billing is actually switched on in the live production environment right now (`isBillingSandboxed()`, `lib/payfast.ts`, reads `NEXT_PUBLIC_PAYFAST_SANDBOX`/`payfastMode()` - this session has no access to the live environment's actual env-var values, so whether this is reachable by a real customer today, as opposed to only in sandbox mode, is asserted by nobody here and should be checked against the live Vercel/Supabase env before treating this as an active, exploitable-today gap rather than a reachable-once-billing-goes-live one). Also not verified: real PayFast abandonment/delay rates in production (no live PayFast traffic data available in this environment) - the "nobody has to fail a payment, just abandon" framing is a structural claim (no reconciliation job exists, confirmed by grep), not a claim about how often it has actually happened.

**Backlog status.** `start_payfast_checkout()`'s revenue-integrity gap remains open, exactly as before - this pass did not resolve it (deliberately, per its own framing) but replaces the backlog's vague one-line description with the sharper, live-reproduced write-up above, split into the one real Sarel-only question (A/B/C above) and the two narrower, probably-not-policy asymmetries (FAILED-ITN non-reversion; seat-cap's missing status check) that look fixable either way he decides. The other standing judgment-call items (the impersonation session-refresh gap in `proxy.ts`, `held_registrations`-vs-CV display format, `send-discovered-tenders.ts`'s own 2-day lookback residual, PR #176/#178/#179/#180 all awaiting Sarel's own merge decision, PR #177 still a draft) remain exactly as described - not touched this pass. The ~9 untraced `.tsx` hits from the 49-hit grep and the 33-hyphenated-file surface also remain untouched. Migrations `0117`-`0120` still on `main`, still not applied to production - unrelated to this pass's own analysis, which concerns `0078`-`0117`'s already-applied-everywhere-but-production-may-or-may-not-have-them-all logic, not anything newly added by the pending batch.

To verify independently: re-run this pass's own scratch-Postgres script shape - seed a company active/starter/2/5, call `start_payfast_checkout('business','yearly')` as that company's owner with no further action, and read `company_subscriptions`/`company_can_request_pack()` immediately after (expect business/10/30 limits, status still active, pack gate already open); then call `apply_payfast_itn()` with `'FAILED'` for that same `m_payment_id` and re-read (expect status past_due, limits still business/10/30); then call `create_company_invite_checked()` as the owner (expect it to still succeed, reading only `max_users`). Or read `app/supabase/migrations/0117_billing_employee_role_gap.sql` lines 70-122 (`start_payfast_checkout`), `0112_payfast_itn_amount_verification.sql` lines 39-130 (`apply_payfast_itn`), `0115_pack_quota_regression_and_request_race.sql` lines 89-123 (`company_can_request_pack`) and `0113_create_invite_seat_check_race.sql` lines 35-79 (`create_company_invite_checked`) side by side and confirm the last of those four never references `status`/`v_status` anywhere in its body, unlike the other three.

**The bug, re-derived from the code, not trusted from the backlog's own one-line summary.** Both `send-compliance-digest.ts` (Tier 2, compliance-expiry) and `send-discovered-tenders.ts` (Tier 1, new-discovered-tenders) claimed each candidate's `claim_notification()` token - a one-time-ever, per-item idempotency claim, same RPC `send-returnables-digest.ts`/`send-scout-alerts.ts` use - BEFORE looking up that company's `operationalRecipients()`. For `send-discovered-tenders.ts` this was worse than a simple ordering slip: the claim loop ran over EVERY candidate row across EVERY company, before the rows were even grouped by company, so a zero-recipient company's items were claimed as a side effect of processing a completely different company's batch in the same loop. Either way, a company with zero opted-in recipients at the exact moment either script ran had every one of that run's compliance items / discovered tenders permanently marked "already notified" with nothing ever actually sent - and no `notification_logs` row either, since no send was ever attempted - indistinguishable from "already handled" to any future run, even once that company later opts a member in.

**Why this isn't actually the judgment call the 2026-11-06 pass left it as.** That pass's own entry (line ~1089 of this doc, `091e884`) reasoned it couldn't tell whether the "claiming early is deliberate" rationale a predecessor gave for these two scripts (`e34d59c`'s own sibling entry, 2026-10-30: "claiming early is deliberate... even if that batch's send later fails") was meant to cover the zero-recipients sub-case too, and chose not to override that predecessor's call without discussing it first. Reading the actual rationale again: it's about a batch whose SEND is attempted and fails (a transient network blip, a bad render) - a case where claiming early avoids re-claiming the same item on a retry. Zero recipients is a different event: no send is ever attempted at all. Tracing the failure-mode consequence directly (what happens if the claim-then-group order is changed to group-then-check-recipients-then-claim): nothing about the "avoid a duplicate claim across runs" protection changes - the claim is still atomic per-row, still happens exactly once, just later in the control flow, scoped to one company's own batch, and only once that company is known to have somewhere to send it. There is no real tradeoff this reordering gives up; the earlier pass's hesitation was about not wanting to unilaterally overrule a predecessor's judgment on a question that, read carefully, that predecessor's own stated reasoning doesn't actually cover.

**Fixed, both files, same shape as the 3 already-established sibling fixes** (`send-deadline-reminders.ts`/`send-operational-alerts.ts`, 2026-11-06; `send-returnables-digest.ts`, 2026-10-30): recipients resolved and checked before the claim, not after.
- `send-compliance-digest.ts`: moved the `operationalRecipients()` call before the claim loop; skip (no claim attempted) when a company has zero recipients.
- `send-discovered-tenders.ts`: bigger restructuring, as the 2026-11-06 pass anticipated it would need - grouped ALL candidate rows by company BEFORE any claim is attempted (previously claimed first, across every company, THEN grouped), then only claims a company's own rows once that company's recipients are confirmed non-empty.
- Both: extracted the per-company body into an exported, directly-testable function (`processComplianceDigestForCompany()` / `processDiscoveredTenderCompany()`), the same convention `send-deadline-reminders.ts` already established 2026-11-06 (no `app/scripts/*.ts` file had testable logic before that pass split one out), each guarded behind the identical `import.meta.url === \`file://${process.argv[1]}\`` check so importing the function for a test doesn't also fire a real (doomed) network call - verified this guard changes nothing about real invocation by running both scripts directly with no env vars set and confirming the identical pre-fix "must both be set" exit-1 message.

**One residual edge, honestly not fully closed, documented in the file's own header comment rather than claimed away.** `send-discovered-tenders.ts` reads only the last 2 days (`sinceIso`) on the assumption every row gets claimed-or-skipped daily. A company with zero recipients for MORE than 2 consecutive days will still lose whichever opportunities aged out of that window before a recipient ever appeared - genuinely unclaimed the whole time, but no longer in the query's own `gte("created_at", sinceIso)` range to be picked up. This is a real improvement (permanently-lost-immediately -> lost-only-if-the-gap-exceeds-2-days), not a full close; widening the window or querying unclaimed rows directly (instead of a fixed lookback) would close it, left for a future pass. `send-compliance-digest.ts` has no equivalent residual: `complianceDigestCandidatesForCompany()` re-derives candidates from live expiry dates every run, not a creation-date window, so an unclaimed item at the 30-day threshold is still a candidate at 29/28/.../15 days (just no longer AT the 30-day threshold specifically - the 14- and 7-day thresholds remain fully reachable).

Post-fix: `npx vitest run scripts/send-compliance-digest.spec.ts scripts/send-discovered-tenders.spec.ts` - **8/8 passed**. Red state, done for real: temporarily reintroduced JUST the claim-before-recipients ordering in both files (kept the function signature/export intact, so the test file itself was untouched - this isn't a "function doesn't exist yet" tautology) and re-ran - **exactly the 2 targeted "never claims claim_notification for a company with zero opted-in recipients" tests failed**, with the predicted diff (`skippedNoRecipients: 0` received vs `1` expected), while the other 6 tests (unrelated behavior - real-recipient ordering, already-claimed dedupe, dry-run display) stayed green, confirming the tests actually exercise this specific bug and aren't a tautology. The separate `node --experimental-strip-types` per-file loop over every `*.test.ts` (the exact method this doc's own guardrail specifies, no `--test` flag) - **27 files, 0 failures**, unaffected since neither touched file is a `*.test.ts`. `npm run typecheck` (whole project, via `next typegen && tsc --noEmit`) - **0 errors**. `npx eslint` on all 4 touched/new files - clean (one unused-param warning in the new discovered-tenders spec, fixed immediately, re-ran clean). `node --experimental-strip-types --check` on both edited scripts - compiles clean.
