## This pass (2026-11-07c, standing solution-architect review): took option 1 from the immediately-preceding pass's own list - actually fixed `etenders_national.fetch_releases()`'s silent-partial-failure-on-total-failure gap, checked-not-firing twice (2026-11-07, 2026-11-07b) and explicitly flagged both times as deserving its own dedicated change rather than a bolt-on. Fixed with a genuine red-then-green test, pushed directly to `main` (small/safe/additive - no RLS/gate/money-path change, same risk tier as the two preceding passes' own direct pushes).

Oriented from `95ee11c` (immediately-preceding pass, HEAD at that commit). `git fetch origin main` twice (before starting, right before pushing) - clean both times, no sibling commits landed during this pass.

**The fix.** `fetch_releases()` (`engine/discovery/etenders_national.py`) paged the OCDS API; on any page fetch failure (after `fetch_page()`'s own 3 retries), it printed a `WARNING` to stdout and returned whatever had already been collected. Correct and intentional when at least one page had already succeeded (the already-documented, live-confirmed real HTTP-500 wall around page 5-6) - that part is untouched. But when the VERY FIRST page attempt failed and zero releases were ever collected, the function returned `[]` - byte-for-byte identical to a genuine "no releases in this window" result, to every caller that only ever reads the return value (never the stdout print). Changed `fetch_releases()` to track whether a page fetch actually failed; if it did AND no releases were collected before that failure, it now raises `RuntimeError` naming the total-failure shape explicitly, instead of returning `[]` silently. The partial-success-after-some-pages case, and the genuine-zero-releases-no-error case, are both unchanged - verified by test, not just reasoned.

**Why this closes the gap for real callers, traced, not assumed.** `gov_sources.fetch_all()`'s own `etenders_portal`-failed fallback branch (line 419-424) already wraps the call in `try/except Exception as e: errors["etenders_ocds"] = str(e)` - this now actually populates on a total failure, which `watch_new_tenders.py`'s own `system_alerts.record()` gate (already gated on `res.get("errors")`, line 474-486) will now actually see and fire on. Checked the other 3 real callers of `etenders_national.fetch_releases()` in the repo (`grep -rn "etenders_national" engine --include=*.py`, read each one, not just grepped): (1) `gov_sources.py:220` - wrapped, as above; (2) `watch_new_tenders.py:463` and (3) `daily_digest.py:276` - both the manual-only `--sources ocds`/`sources="ocds"` branch (production default is `"all"`, which never reaches this code path directly - confirmed by each file's own `argparse`/function-signature default), unwrapped, so a total failure there now surfaces as a loud crash on a manual invocation instead of a silent "0 releases found" - strictly better for a human running it by hand, not a regression of any production path; (4) `watch_tender_updates.py`'s `OcdsDays.releases()` (line 150-159) - already wraps `self.fetch_day(day)` in `try/except Exception`, logs via `system_alerts.record(..., "error", ...)` and caches `[]` for that day, with its own comment "one bad day must not end the run." **This one is the clearest confirmation the fix was correct, not just safe**: that code was already written assuming `fetch_releases()` would raise on a real failure - it could never have actually caught anything from a total page-1 failure before this fix, because the old `fetch_releases()` swallowed the error internally before `OcdsDays.releases()`'s own `try` ever saw it. This fix makes that already-existing, already-correct exception handling actually do its job for the first time.

**Verified myself, genuine red-then-green.** Wrote `engine/discovery/test_etenders_national.py` (no dedicated test file existed for this module before - confirmed by `ls engine/discovery/ | grep test`, matches the prior passes' own note). 4 tests: total-failure-on-page-1 raises with the right message; partial-success-after-page-N-fails still returns the partial list unraised (the documented wall case, explicitly protected against regressing); a genuine empty-no-error result still returns `[]` unraised; a normal full 2-page success is unaffected. `python3 engine/discovery/test_etenders_national.py` post-fix: **ALL PASSED, exit 0**. Red state, done for real, not assumed: `git stash push -- engine/discovery/etenders_national.py` (reverting ONLY the source fix, keeping the new test file in place) and re-ran the exact same test file against the pre-fix code - **2 of 4 failed** exactly as expected (`raises RuntimeError...` and `the raised error names the total-failure shape...`, both FAIL, the other two still passed since they test the untouched paths) - confirmed the test actually exercises the bug, not a tautology. `git stash pop` restored the fix; re-ran - **ALL PASSED** again, exit 0. Also ran `python3 engine/discovery/test_gov_sources.py` (every existing test, unrelated to this fix, still **ALL PASSED**) and the full per-file loop over every `engine/**/test_*.py` (`find engine -name "test_*.py"`, ~60+ files) - **0 failures**, confirming no regression anywhere else in the engine. `python3 engine/discovery/test_tender_updates.py` specifically re-checked given the `OcdsDays` finding above - **ALL PASSED**. `py_compile` on both edited/new files - compiles clean. Did not run the TS/JS QA suite (`npm run typecheck`/vitest/`next build`) - this pass touched zero TypeScript/JavaScript files, only one Python module and its new dedicated test file.

**Backlog status.** 1 real, structurally-confirmed silent-failure gap (checked-not-firing-in-production twice by two prior passes, now actually fixed with its own red/green) pushed directly to `main`. Not a confirmed-live production break the way the Resend bug was - this closes a gap that has not yet fired, the same honest distinction the last two passes drew for their own OCDS-related findings. The 6 standing judgment-call items (`start_payfast_checkout()`'s revenue-integrity gap, the impersonation session-refresh gap in `proxy.ts`, `held_registrations`-vs-CV display format, the zero-recipients batched-send sub-case, whether `send_pack_ready_email.py`'s own User-Agent fix fires clean in its real always-on-worker environment, PR #176/#177/#178/#179/#180 all awaiting Sarel's own merge decision) remain exactly as described - not touched this pass. The ~9 untraced `.tsx` hits from the 49-hit grep and the 33-hyphenated-file surface also remain untouched. Migrations `0117`-`0120` still on `main`, still not applied to production. ## This pass (2026-11-07b, standing solution-architect review): took option 1 from the immediately-preceding pass's own list - checked whether `etenders_national.fetch_releases()`'s silent-partial-failure-on-total-page-failure gap (flagged but not fixed last pass) has ever actually fired in a live `daily-discovery` run. Answer: it has not, over the workflow's entire life (15 runs total, 2026-10-23 to 2026-11-06) - but tracing *how* it's reachable in production sharpens the finding into something more precise than the prior pass's framing, and that sharper version is still open. No code changed this pass; nothing pushed.

Oriented from `050f469` (immediately-preceding pass, HEAD at that commit). `git fetch origin main` twice (before starting, right before writing this entry) - clean both times, no sibling commits. PRs re-checked via `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls?state=open`: `#176`/`#178`/`#179`/`#180` still `draft: false` and open, `#177` still `draft: true`, `#164`/`#165` still stale drafts - all 7 unchanged, none touched this pass.

**Correction to the prior pass's own framing, found while tracing the real call path.** The prior pass's entry describes `fetch_releases()` as reached via `watch_new_tenders.py`'s `--sources ocds` branch, calling it "the live national-tender-discovery feed, not a side script" - true only for a manual `--sources ocds` invocation. Read `.github/workflows/daily-discovery.yml`'s actual `run:` line (`python3 engine/discovery/watch_new_tenders.py --out discovery_report.json`, no `--sources` flag at all) and `watch_new_tenders.py`'s own `argparse` default (`--sources` defaults to `"all"`, line 427) - the real production default takes the `else` branch (line 465 on), which calls `gov_sources.releases_for_watch()`, not `etenders_national.fetch_releases()` directly. `gov_sources.ALL_SOURCES` (line 72-74) does NOT include `"etenders_ocds"` - so in the default/production path, `fetch_releases()` is reached ONLY through one specific fallback: `gov_sources.fetch_all()` line 419-424, `if "etenders_portal" in sources and not by_source.get("etenders_portal")` - i.e. only when the primary eTenders-portal read (`etenders_portal.fetch_releases()`) fails outright for the whole run. It is not, as the prior entry implies, on every run's main path.

**That makes it a fallback-of-a-fallback, and the compound shape is worse than the single-layer gap previously named.** If the portal read ever does fail and this OCDS fallback fires, and `fetch_releases()`'s own paging *also* hits the already-documented, already-live-confirmed upstream wall (this same file's `fetch_releases()` docstring, confirmed live 2026-10-16: the OCDS API itself breaks with HTTP 500 around page 5-6, ~500-600 records in, "regardless of date range"), the inner failure is caught and swallowed entirely inside `fetch_releases()` (prints a `WARNING`, returns the partial list, never raises) - so the outer `try/except` around the fallback call in `fetch_all()` (line 421-424) never sees an exception, `errors["etenders_ocds"]` is never populated, and `watch_new_tenders.py`'s own `system_alerts.record()` call (line 483-486, gated on `res.get("errors")`) never fires. The run would report success with a silently-truncated release set (whatever fraction of the 14-day window the OCDS API served before its own page-5/6 wall) and nothing anywhere would show it happened - the exact dominant bug-class shape this doc tracks, just two fallback-layers deep instead of one.

**Checked whether this compound path has ever actually fired - it hasn't, over the workflow's whole life.** `gh run list --workflow=daily-discovery.yml --limit 50` returns exactly 15 runs total (the workflow was only created 2026-10-22, per its own header comment - there is no earlier history to miss). Pulled `gh run view <id> --log` for all 15 and grepped every one for `"falling back to the OCDS feed"` (the fallback's own trigger line) and `"stopped at page"` (`fetch_releases()`'s own partial-failure print): zero matches in any of the 15 logs - the primary `etenders_portal` source has not failed outright on a single run in this workflow's history, so the OCDS fallback (and therefore `fetch_releases()`) has never been invoked at all in production, let alone hit its own page-5/6 wall while there. The 14 `success`-concluded runs each show a `"NNNN release(s) in range"` line (1271-1482 releases/day, 2026-10-23 through 2026-11-06) with no `etenders_ocds` entry in `by_source`. The 1 `failure`-concluded run (`40074828465`, 2026-10-24) is the already-documented, already-fixed `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'lxml'` top-level crash (ci file itself explains this, and the pinned `pip install lxml==6.1.3` step fixed it the same day) - confirmed by re-reading that run's own log directly, nothing to do with OCDS. Per-source failures DID occur in this window (`lephalale` failed on 11 of the 14 successful runs with two distinct, already-known causes - a changed PDF table structure and an SSL EOF error - and `sanral` failed once, 2026-10-31, a timeout) - both are `gov_sources.py`'s own already-working per-source isolation (logged, run continues, no OCDS involvement), not this gap.

**Honest characterization, same distinction the last two passes drew for their own findings.** This is checked-not-currently-firing, not fixed - same category as last pass's own OCDS User-Agent hardening (precautionary, not a confirmed-live break) and structurally parallel to how the Resend bug *was* confirmed live via exactly this method (`gh run view --log` across real runs). The difference here: the Resend check found the bug firing on every single relevant run; this check, done the same way, found the reachable-path precondition (`etenders_portal` failing outright) has itself never occurred, so the deeper gap riding on it has had no chance to fire either. Did not fix it this pass - deliberately, per the review loop's own scope discipline (checking first, as option 1 asked, before deciding whether a fix is warranted) and because any fix here (e.g. making `fetch_releases()` raise instead of swallow on a page failure, or having `fetch_all()`'s fallback branch itself check for a suspiciously-short OCDS result) touches the same function the immediately-preceding pass already modified for the User-Agent header, and deserves its own dedicated pass with its own red/green rather than being bolted on as an afterthought here.

**Backlog status.** No code changed, nothing pushed this pass. The newly-flagged gap from last pass is now checked and sharpened (not fixed): confirmed-reachable-only-via-fallback, confirmed never fired in the workflow's full 15-run history, still open for whoever next wants to harden `fetch_releases()`/`fetch_all()`'s fallback branch against the same "partial success reported as full success" shape. The 6 standing judgment-call items (`start_payfast_checkout()`'s revenue-integrity gap, the impersonation session-refresh gap in `proxy.ts`, `held_registrations`-vs-CV display format, the zero-recipients batched-send sub-case, whether `send_pack_ready_email.py`'s own User-Agent fix fires clean in its real always-on-worker environment, PR #176/#177/#178/#179/#180 all awaiting Sarel's own merge decision) remain exactly as described - not touched. The ~9 untraced `.tsx` hits from the 49-hit grep and the 33-hyphenated-file surface also remain untouched this pass. Migrations `0117`-`0120` still on `main`, still not applied to production.

**Read every one of the ~50 call sites' own headers, not just grepped for the string "User-Agent."** Split them into two real categories: (1) external, third-party, WAF-plausible targets - `list_tenders.py`, `source_http.py`, `detail.py`, `award_outcomes.py` (`_get`/`portal_page`), `tender_enrichment.py`, `download_discovered_documents.py`, `watch_tender_updates.py`, `assess_tender.py`, `process_general_jobs.py`'s `_http_get`, `etenders_national.py`'s own `fetch_site_page` - every single one of these ALREADY carries an explicit `User-Agent` (`Mozilla/5.0 (tender-tool discovery; contact: Sarel)` or an equivalent descriptive string), confirmed by reading each, not assumed from the grep; (2) internal calls to this project's own Supabase instance (REST/RPC/Storage: `check_system_alerts.py`, `system_alerts.py`, `company_profiles.py`, `cv/process_cv_jobs.py`, `cv/extract_cv_fields.py`, `pack/process_pack_jobs.py`, `general/process_general_jobs.py`'s internal call, `narrative/process_narrative_jobs.py`, `notify/record_heartbeat.py`, `compliance/watch_deadlines.py`, `discovery/opportunity_requirements.py`'s storage download, `seed_demo_company.py`, `seed_supabase_company.py`, `write_admin_harness_results.py`) - none of these set a `User-Agent` either, but reasoned (not just assumed) that this is a different risk category: if Supabase's own API gateway blocked on a bare Python-urllib signature the way Resend's edge WAF does, essentially the entire background engine would already be dead on every run, which contradicts the system's own daily operation and this doc's own many passes' worth of successful test runs against it. Not independently load-tested against a live Supabase WAF rule (no safe, non-destructive way to isolate that the way the Resend bogus-key trick did) - flagged as reasoned-safe, not proven-safe the same way the Resend root-cause was.

**The one real gap found: `engine/discovery/etenders_national.py`'s `fetch_page()`.** Called `urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=30)` directly on a bare URL string - no `Request` object, no headers at all, the exact same "Python-urllib/3.x" default signature that triggered Resend's block - against National Treasury's public OCDS API (`https://ocds-api.etenders.gov.za/api/OCDSReleases`). This is the real production discovery path: `watch_new_tenders.py`'s `--sources ocds` branch calls `etenders_national.fetch_releases()` → `fetch_page()` directly, the live national-tender-discovery feed, not a side script.

**Live-tested both ways against the real endpoint, not assumed from the shape.** Wrote a standalone repro (bare `urlopen(url)`, no headers, same as the pre-fix code) against `https://ocds-api.etenders.gov.za/api/OCDSReleases` with a real 7-day date window: **HTTP 200, 5 releases returned** - confirmed, this request shape is NOT currently blocked by anything on this endpoint. This is the key difference from the Resend finding: that one was reproduced as a live, currently-failing 403; this one is reproduced as a live, currently-succeeding 200. So the honest characterization is precautionary hardening against a failure mode already proven real in this exact codebase (a government API's WAF posture can change without notice, and nothing about this endpoint is contractually guaranteed to stay tolerant of a bare UA), not a second confirmed-live production bug.

**Fixed anyway, small/safe/additive, direct push.** Added an explicit `User-Agent: "TenderTool-Discovery/1.0 (+https://tenderready.app)"` to `fetch_page()`'s own request, matching this same file's `fetch_site_page()` (already explicit) and the repo-wide convention every other external call already follows - so this file no longer has one function that's the odd one out. ## This pass (2026-11-06/07, standing solution-architect review): took the standing backlog's "whether RESEND_API_KEY is still valid in live GitHub Actions secrets" judgment-call item for the first time (option 3 from the immediately-preceding pass's own list) - answered it definitively (yes, the key is valid) but found a different, real, currently-live bug behind the question: `send_digest_emails.py`'s and `send_pack_ready_email.py`'s own raw `urllib` POSTs to Resend carry no `User-Agent` header, which Resend's edge WAF has been blocking with `HTTP 403 error code: 1010` on every real send attempt for at least 4 consecutive days (2026-11-03 through 2026-11-06) - Sarel's own daily digest email has not been delivered in that window, invisible to `gh run list`/the workflow's own "success" status. Fixed both files, pushed directly to `main` (`0369f50`). **This pass's own work was interrupted mid-task by a container restart TWICE** (per the coordinator's own messages) - once after the fix was written and live-verified but before it was committed, and again while this very System-Status.md entry was still being drafted (code fix already complete and merged onto current `main` by that point, only this write-up was in flight). Picked back up both times, re-verified everything fresh from a clean state before trusting any of the pre-restart work (re-read every diff, re-ran both test files for real exit codes, re-did a genuine live red-then-green against the real Resend endpoint for both modules independently, re-fetched `origin/main` each time and fast-forward-merged the one sibling-session commit that had landed in the meantime) - per the coordinator's own instruction, twice over, not to trust the pre-interruption reasoning at face value just because it was already written down.

Oriented from `963b779` (immediately-preceding pass). `git fetch origin main`, checked twice (once before starting the fix, once again after the interruption, right before committing): the first check was clean; the second found one real sibling-session commit in flight, `e34d59c` (`fix(sanral): Form B7's _num() never got the NaN/Infinity guard fill_financial_hours.py was fixed for` - `engine/sanral_b7.py`/`engine/test_sanral_b7.py`/`docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md`/`docs/specs/System-Status.md`, no overlap with this pass's own 2 files) - fast-forward-merged (`963b779..e34d59c`) before continuing, confirmed no conflict.

**How this was found.** Checked the three live, independently-schedulable Resend-sending GitHub Actions workflows that actually attempt real sends with real recipients, not just whether their jobs report "success" (a workflow can run clean while 100% of its own send attempts fail, if the script itself never raises past a send failure - exactly this backlog's own standing "zero-recipients batched-send sub-case" territory, which this finding sits right next to). `gh run view <id> --log` on the last 4-5 runs each of `daily-digest`, `founder-digest`, `compliance-alerts`, `returnables-digest`, `deadline-reminders`, `onboarding-nudges`, `operational-alerts`, `corrigendum-alerts`, `scout-alerts`: every one of the last several days' `daily-digest` runs (2026-11-03 through 2026-11-06) logged the identical line, `[system-alert] digest_send error: 1 of 1 daily digest email(s) failed to send: Resend rejected the send to 'sareljvr101@gmail.com': HTTP 403 error code: 1010` - a real, repeated, 100%-reproduction-rate send failure to Sarel's own inbox, not a zero-recipients no-op. The other digest/alert workflows mostly had nothing to send that day (confirmed from their own "0 send attempt(s)"/"0 sent, N skipped" log lines) except `founder-digest`, whose own send (`scripts/send-founder-digest.ts`, a different code path, the official `resend` npm package rather than raw `urllib`) logged `Founder daily digest (06 Nov 2026): sent.` - succeeding, with the exact same `RESEND_API_KEY`, on the same day `daily-digest` failed. That contrast is what pointed at the request shape, not the key, as the real variable.

**Root-caused, not just correlated - a live, direct reproduction against the real Resend API.** `grep -rn "User-Agent" engine/` shows every OTHER `urllib.request.Request` call anywhere in this codebase sets an explicit `User-Agent` - several specifically because a site's WAF blocked Python's bare default before (`engine/discovery/vaal_central_water.py`'s own header comment documents exactly this "WAF/User-Agent story" for a different site). `engine/notify/send_digest_emails.py`'s `send_one()` and `engine/notify/send_pack_ready_email.py`'s `_send_via_resend()` were the only 2 callers in the whole repo that construct a `urllib.request.Request` against an external API with no `User-Agent` at all (confirmed: `grep -rln "api.resend.com" app/lib app/scripts engine` returns exactly these 2 Python modules plus their own test files - every TypeScript sender goes through `app/lib/resendEmail.ts`'s official `resend` npm package instead, which sets its own non-default User-Agent). Confirmed live, this environment's proxy reaches `api.resend.com` directly (plain `curl` to it returns `401`, not blocked): a bare `urllib.request.Request` POST to `https://api.resend.com/emails` with a deliberately bogus API key (to isolate the edge from Resend's own auth layer) and no `User-Agent` came back `HTTPError 403 b'error code: 1010\n'` - byte-for-byte the same failure the production logs show. Adding literally any real `User-Agent` string to the identical bogus-key request made it reach Resend's own application layer instead, returning a proper `{"message":"API key is invalid","name":"validation_error","statusCode":401}` - proving the block is on the request's own shape (specifically, Python's default `Python-urllib/3.x` signature), not on `RESEND_API_KEY`'s validity. **This directly and completely answers the long-standing backlog question**: the key is fine - it was never reaching Resend's auth check at all.

**Fixed, 2 files, both re-verified fresh after the mid-task interruption.** Added an explicit `User-Agent` header (`TenderTool-DailyDigest/1.0 (+https://tenderready.app)` / `TenderTool-PackReady/1.0 (+https://tenderready.app)`) to both modules' Resend `urllib.request.Request` calls, each with a header comment explaining the finding and its own live reproduction, so a future pass re-reading either file doesn't have to re-derive this from scratch. `send_pack_ready_email.py`'s own path matters more than it might look: it's the instant "Bid Pack Compilation Complete" email (`engine/general/process_general_jobs.py`, called right after a pack job flips to "ready" - Sarel's own explicit decision that this not wait for a scheduled script, "teams are often working against tight courier/print deadlines"), claimed via a one-time `claim_notification()` token BEFORE the send is attempted - a blocked send here doesn't just delay that email, it permanently loses it (the job never runs again for the same job id). Not independently confirmed failing in a live GitHub Actions run the way `send_digest_emails.py` was (its own worker runs on an always-on container outside GitHub Actions per `bridge-worker-ci.yml`'s own comment, "the production worker is the always-on container" - no log access to that host from here), but the root cause is identical and was reproduced the same way, live, against the real endpoint, through this module's own `_send_via_resend()` function directly (not just a hand-rolled snippet) - same confidence as the confirmed-in-production fix, just not independently confirmed as already having bitten in practice.

**Verification, run myself, real exit codes, redone fresh post-interruption on the merged `main`.** `python3 engine/notify/test_send_digest_emails.py` - **0 failures** (its own printed count). `python3 engine/notify/test_send_pack_ready_email.py` - **0 failures**. Both test files monkeypatch `urlopen` directly rather than asserting on request headers, so neither could have caught this bug nor needed updating for the fix - confirmed by reading both files first, not assumed. `python3 -c "import py_compile; ..."` on both edited files - compiles clean. Did not run the full TS/JS QA suite (`npm run typecheck`/`eslint`/`vitest`/`next build`) - this pass touched zero TypeScript/JavaScript files, only 2 standalone Python modules with their own dedicated test files, run directly exactly as `bridge-worker-ci.yml` runs them.

**Genuine red-then-green, run myself, twice (once before the interruption, once again after, from a clean working tree, per the coordinator's own instruction not to trust the pre-interruption run at face value).** Called each module's own real send function (`send_digest_emails.send_one()`, `send_pack_ready_email._send_via_resend()`) directly against the live `https://api.resend.com/emails` endpoint with a deliberately bogus key - not a mock, not a unit test (neither file's own test suite exercises the real network, by design - "No network: urlopen is monkeypatched"). Pre-fix (`git stash` on just these 2 files): both returned `failed`, `HTTP 403 error code: 1010` / `'error code: 1010\n'` - the red state, confirmed. Post-fix (`git stash pop`): both returned `failed`, `HTTP 401 {"message":"API key is invalid",...}` - reaching Resend's real auth layer, the green state, confirmed. `failed` is the right outcome either way here (the key really is bogus) - what the red/green pair actually proves is which failure mode is hit, which is the entire point of this fix.

**Backlog status.** 1 real, currently-live-in-production finding (confirmed-failing-daily) + 1 same-root-cause finding in a second module (not independently confirmed failing live, reasoned safe to fix identically) - both fixed, pushed directly to `main` (small, safe, additive: a `User-Agent` header on an outbound HTTP call, no RLS/security-boundary or money-path change, same risk tier as this doc's many prior direct-push fixes). **The standing "is RESEND_API_KEY still valid" judgment-call item is now resolved, not just re-deferred**: yes, it's valid - remove it from the backlog list below. Did not continue the 49-hit TS read-grep's own remaining ~9 untraced `.tsx` hits, the 33-hyphenated-file surface, or a from-scratch-read batch this pass - this pass's whole budget went to the judgment-call angle instead, chosen specifically because (per the immediately-preceding pass's own framing) "this has been a standing open question for many passes with nobody actually checking it," and it turned out to have a real, live-production answer worth having. PR #176/#177/#178/#179/#180 re-checked just before this entry's own final push - note this corrects an earlier draft of this same sentence: the first attempt, `gh pr list --state open`, actually failed outright with a GraphQL-unavailable error (never returned real data, confirmed by re-reading this pass's own transcript before writing this), so the honest check is the one that followed, `gh api repos/SarelJvR2024/tender-tool/pulls?state=open`, which did succeed: all 5 (`#176`/`#177`/`#178`/`#179`/`#180`) still `open`, none merged, none closed, `#177`/`#164`/`#165` still the only drafts - none touched this pass. **For a future pass:** the ~9 untraced `.tsx` hits from the 49-hit grep, the 33-hyphenated-file surface, and a fresh from-scratch-read batch are all still exactly where the immediately-preceding pass left them; and it may be worth checking whether `send_pack_ready_email.py`'s own fix actually fires clean in its real always-on-worker environment next time a pack goes "ready" (no visibility into that host's logs from here) - flagged, not confirmed.

## This pass (2026-11-06, standing solution-architect review): picked up the two oldest, longest-untouched threads the immediately-preceding pass left open (the original standing `"const { data"` read-grep, now 49 raw hits, up from 43 - re-derived from scratch rather than trusted) and found a genuinely new, gate-adjacent instance of the dominant bug class in `computeTenderReadiness()` - a shared pure function that BOTH the live Submit-button UI gate AND PR #178's own still-unmerged server-side Fix-item gate call. Fixed on `main`, opened as PR #180 (not pushed directly - this touches the Pack Review hard-stop gate machinery); also flagged the interaction with PR #178 as a PR comment there, without editing #178 itself. A second, smaller instance of the same bug class fixed in `ImpersonationBanner.tsx`, same PR.

**Why this angle.** The immediately-preceding pass's own entry left three options open and asked for the choice to be weighed, not defaulted. Chose the two oldest standing grep threads (over a third from-scratch-read batch, or a different angle like `engine/` or a judgment-call item) because: (1) every prior from-scratch-read pass and grep-refinement pass has reliably found real bugs when it actually traced candidates to their consequence rather than stopping at "looks safe" - this is a proven-productive method, not a stale one; (2) the 43-hit grep specifically had an explicit, repeated "~30 of 43 untraced" note sitting unaddressed across at least 4 more recent passes (`5727cff`, `829dbb9`, `968feaa`, `6424df6` - none of them touched it), making it the single most clearly neglected angle in the whole doc, by the doc's own repeated admission; (3) unlike the 33-hyphenated-file surface (which has since had substantial follow-up from the bare-write and array/tuple-destructure blind-spot sweeps touching many of the same 33 files from different lenses), the 43-hit grep's own specific lens (plain pages/components/libs, not `*-actions.ts`) has had no follow-up at all since the one pass that first ran it.

**Re-derived the grep from scratch, not trusted.** `grep -rn "const { data" --include="*.tsx" --include="*.ts" app/app | grep -v "actions.ts" | grep -v "\.spec\." | grep -v "\.test\." | grep -v "error"` now returns **49** raw hits (not 43 - the codebase has grown since that count was last taken; flagged here as data, not assumed stale). Of these: ~13 are the already-established-safe `const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser()` pattern (always followed by a fail-closed `if (!user) redirect(...)`); ~6 are grep false-positives (comment lines mentioning `"const { data"` as text, left by prior passes' own header comments documenting the array/tuple blind spot); 5 are private-bucket `createSignedUrls`/`createSignedUrl` calls (traced in full below, confirmed safe); the rest were traced individually.

**Traced the 5 signed-URL calls to their real consequence, not assumed from the shape** (`company/registrations/page.tsx:59`, `company/properties/page.tsx:42`, `company/principals/page.tsx:54`, `admin/page.tsx:209`, `experience/[id]/page.tsx:110`) - all four vault-document pages share the identical pattern: `const { data: signed } = await supabase.storage...createSignedUrls(...); for (const s of signed ?? []) ...`. Read every downstream consumer (`HeldRow`/`DocumentLine` in `registrations/page.tsx`/`principals/page.tsx`) - on a failed batch, `urls[path]` is falsy and the UI falls back to showing the filename as **plain text instead of a link**, never to "No copy uploaded" - the compliance status itself (`expiryStatus()`/`path` presence) is computed entirely independently of `urls`, so a failed signed-URL fetch can only break a download link, never flip a compliance read. Confirmed safe, not fixed. Also traced `admin/layout.tsx:23`'s `is_platform_admin()` RPC gate (every `/admin/*` page's own access control) - `if (!isAdmin) notFound()` is fail-closed by construction: a failed RPC read makes `isAdmin` falsy, denying access, never granting it. Confirmed safe, not fixed.

**The real finding: `tender-readiness.ts`'s `computeTenderReadiness()` - traced from `pack-review-data.ts:116/134/232/236/297`'s own untraced hits, three levels deep to where it actually bites.** `pack-review-data.ts` (`loadPackReviewSnapshot()`, the "what will go into this SANRAL pack" preview) wraps each of its 6 sections in its own try/catch, and a failed read inside one (`company`, `key_positions`, `form_answers`, `signature`, `documents`, `form_b7`) already correctly renders as `{ error: "Couldn't load this section: ...", items: [] }` rather than fabricating data - that part is fine. The bug is one level up, in `tender-readiness.ts`'s own `computeTenderReadiness(sections)`, the shared pure function (used by BOTH SANRAL's `pack-review-data.ts` and the general family's `general-pack-review-data.ts`) that flattens those sections into the Verify/Provide/Fix split: its own header comment explicitly argued `section.error` sections should "contribute nothing... silently treating a read failure as '0 items, fully ready' would be worse than leaving it out of the count" - but leaving a failed section's items out of `fix`/`totalCount` has the EXACT SAME effect, at every call site, as if that section really did have 0 Fix items: `fix.length` and `score` can't tell "genuinely nothing to fix" apart from "a section holding a real Fix item just failed to load this render." The existing test file (`tender-readiness.test.ts`, pre-fix) literally codified this as intended behavior (`"a section that failed to load contributes nothing to the count"`, asserting `score: 100`).

**Where this actually bites.** `submission-pack.tsx:169` (SANRAL) and `general-workspace.tsx:259` (general family) both compute their own Submit-button `disabledReason` as `fixCount > 0 ? "Fix N items..." : ...` straight off this function - so a transient read failure in any one Pack Review section could make the button render as enabled/not-blocked when a real, disqualifying Fix item exists but just didn't load this render. Checked `requestSubmissionPack()` (`actions.ts`) on current `main` to see what's actually enforced server-side today: `unfilledPositions` (independently re-verified by the engine, already confirmed safe in a prior pass), `missingTemplates`, `b7.blocker`, the already-queued dedupe, and the pack-review-confirmation gate - but **nothing that re-checks `computeTenderReadiness(...).fix` at all**. That's exactly the gap PR #178 (open, unmerged, "the Fix-item server-side gate") is meant to close - and its own diff adds that check by calling this exact same `computeTenderReadiness()` function in both `actions.ts` and `general-actions.ts`. So today this is "only" a client-rendered-attribute cosmetic gap (a direct POST already bypasses the UI gate regardless, a separate thing PR #178 itself names); but once #178 merges, its new server-side check would inherit this identical blind spot, silently, unless it's also addressed. Also checked `pipeline/page.tsx:331/337`'s own "Pack Ready" board badge (`packHealthStatusFromReadiness(score, fix.length)`) - same shape, cosmetic-only (a dashboard card, not a gate), but a visible false-"ready" signal on Sarel's own Bids board.

**Fixed, on `main`, opened as PR #180 (not pushed directly - gate-adjacent).** `computeTenderReadiness()` now also returns `hasUnreadSection: boolean`. `submission-pack.tsx`/`general-workspace.tsx`'s own `disabledReason` now fails closed ("Couldn't check compliance readiness just now - refresh and try again") when `hasUnreadSection` is true - the pre-existing `packReviewSnapshot.mapped === false`/`!generalReviewSnapshot.mapped` fallback (already its own separate, already-PR'd-for gap) was deliberately left untouched, to keep this PR's diff scoped to the genuinely new finding and not duplicate #178's own change. `packHealthStatusFromReadiness()` (`pipelineCardHelpers.ts`) takes a new optional third `hasUnreadSection` param, returning `"in_progress"` instead of `"ready"` when true even at a 100% score; `pipeline/page.tsx`'s both call sites updated to pass it through. **Left a PR comment on #178** (not an edit to it) explaining the interaction, so whoever reviews #178 for merge knows to pull in #180's fix (or an equivalent check) first or shortly after.

**A second, smaller instance of the same bug class, same PR: `ImpersonationBanner.tsx`.** Found while sweeping the same grep list (`ImpersonationBanner.tsx:33`). A failed `impersonation_audit_logs` read fell through to the exact same `if (!row) return null` branch as a genuinely-ended/stale impersonation session - silently hiding the one reminder this banner exists to give (guardrail 2, its own header comment: "an admin forgetting which account they're acting as"), exactly while a real, still-open impersonation session needs it most. The underlying impersonation session itself is unaffected (enforced by the cookie/RLS, not by whether this banner renders) - this is a safety-reminder gap, not a permission bypass - but it's the same root shape. Fixed: now shows a cautious "Admin Support Mode may still be active - couldn't confirm details just now" banner (with the Exit button still present) on a read error, instead of silently showing nothing. No target name/email available to show on this path (not in the cookie, and the failed read is what would have supplied them) - acceptable, the point is the reminder and the exit path, not the detail.

**Verification, run myself, real exit codes.** `npm run typecheck` - **0 errors**. `npx eslint .` - **0 errors**, same 3 pre-existing warnings (caught and fixed one new one along the way - an unescaped apostrophe in the new `ImpersonationBanner.tsx` copy, `react/no-unescaped-entities` - before this entry was written, not after). `npx vitest run` - **453/453 passed, 56/56 test files** (up from 450/56: +3 new `pipelineCardHelpers.spec.ts` assertions). The corrected per-file `*.test.ts` loop (no `--test` flag) - **27 files, 303 tests, 0 failures** (up from 301/27: +2 new `tender-readiness.test.ts` assertions). `npx next build` - **compiled successfully**, same route table, `Proxy (Middleware)` present.

## This pass (2026-11-06, standing solution-architect review): took the immediately-preceding pass's own "stop refining the grep, read files from scratch" suggestion literally - picked 5 representative Server Action/data-loading files never previously reviewed by name, read each genuinely end-to-end with no grep filter at all, and it surfaced a real (if low-severity) instance of the false-all-clear shape in 1 of the 5 that EVERY prior grep pass would have missed structurally, not just by an exclusion-rule gap - fixed with a behavior change; the other 4 came back genuinely clean. Also confirms, as data, that the from-scratch-read approach is worth continuing over one more grep-pattern refinement.

Oriented from `5727cff` (immediately-preceding pass's own push, `829dbb9`). `git fetch origin main` found zero sibling-session commits, both before starting and again right before this entry's own push - pushed as a clean fast-forward (`5727cff..6424df6`). Re-checked PR #176/#177/#178/#179 (and #164/#165) myself via `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls?state=open`: all six unchanged from the prior pass's own record - `#179`/`#178`/`#176` `draft: false`, `#177` `draft: true`, `#164`/`#165` both still draft, stale since 2026-10-26. None touched, commented on, or merged this pass.

**Why this angle, and how the 5 files were picked.** The immediately-preceding pass's own entry explicitly named the risk: four consecutive passes each found a new grep EXCLUSION-RULE gap (camelCase guard files, hyphenated `*-actions.ts` files, bare writes, array/tuple destructures) rather than ever asking whether the grep's whole target shape - "find a `data`/`rows` destructure with no `error:` alongside it" - was itself too narrow a model of the bug class. Took that literally: picked files that had genuinely never been named in this doc before (confirmed by grepping every `.ts` filename in `app/app`/`app/lib` against the whole of `System-Status.md` and keeping only 0-mention or peripheral-mention hits), favouring small, varied files over another big Server Action: `app/app/company/digestActions.ts` (32 lines, 0 mentions), `app/app/_components/search-tenders.ts` (34 lines, 0 mentions), `app/app/tenders/[id]/bid-task-status.ts` (75 lines, 0 mentions), `app/app/tenders/[id]/update-actions.ts` (43 lines, mentioned twice before but only inside a grep-output file list, never itself read), `app/app/_components/document-intake/uploadBatch.ts` (94 lines, mentioned 3 times before but only for file-validation/header-comment context, never read for this specific bug shape).

**The finding: `app/app/_components/search-tenders.ts`'s `searchTenders()` - real, low-severity, fixed with a behavior change, and structurally invisible to every version of the TS-sweep's grep.** This one DID capture its error (`const { data, error } = await supabase.from("tenders")...`, `if (error) { console.error(...); return []; }`) - every grep this sweep has ever run (looking for a MISSING `error:` capture) would walk straight past it as already-safe. But the function's own return value on that captured-error branch was a bare `[]`, byte-identical to the genuine "no tender matches this query" result one line below (`return data ?? [];` when `data` is an empty array). Its one caller, `CommandPalette.tsx` (the Cmd/Ctrl+K "jump to a tender by contract number" search), rendered the exact same `<CommandEmpty>Nothing found.</CommandEmpty>` for both - a transient read failure told the user their tender doesn't exist, not that the search itself broke. This is a genuinely distinct dimension of the same root bug class this whole doc has been tracking: not "the error was never captured" (the thing every grep pass has looked for) but "the error was captured and logged, then discarded by collapsing it into the same return shape as a genuine empty result" - no literal-substring grep for `"const { data"` or a missing `error:` token could ever have found this, because there's nothing missing to grep for. Severity is low (a command-palette search convenience, not a compliance gate, hard stop or money path - the realistic consequence is a confused user retyping a contract number, not a disqualification risk or a lost write), consistent with this doc's own established severity calibration for a UI-only false-empty state.

**Fixed.** `searchTenders()` now returns `{ results, error }` instead of a bare array; `CommandPalette.tsx` tracks a `searchFailed` state (reset on close and derived-away, same pattern as the existing `displayedResults` staleness guard, once the query drops back under 2 characters) and shows "Tender search failed - try again." instead of "Nothing found." when the read itself failed. New `app/app/_components/search-tenders.spec.ts` (4 tests), using this repo's own established `vi.mock("@/lib/supabase/server", ...)` convention (copied from `company/actions.spec.ts`) since this file calls `createClient()` internally rather than taking it as a parameter.

**The other 4 files, read in full, genuinely clean:**
- `app/app/company/digestActions.ts` - `setDailyDigestOptIn()`'s one RPC call already captures `error` and redirects with a visible error message on failure; the happy-path `redirect()` after it is unreached code on the error branch (Next.js's `redirect()` throws internally), the same convention used throughout this codebase. No gap.
- `app/app/tenders/[id]/bid-task-status.ts` - pure synchronous classification logic (`classifyComplianceItem()`), no Supabase call, no I/O of any kind. Out of scope for this bug class entirely; read anyway per the directive (no filter), confirmed genuinely nothing to find.
- `app/app/tenders/[id]/update-actions.ts` - `acceptTenderUpdateDate()`'s one RPC call already captures `error` and redirects with a visible error message; same "redirect() throws, nothing after it runs" shape as `digestActions.ts`. No gap.
- `app/app/_components/document-intake/uploadBatch.ts` - per-file upload state machine (`markUploading`/`applyUploadResult`/`partitionBatch`); each file's own storage-upload error is captured, logged, and recorded in that file's own `{ status: "failed", error }` slot - never silently merged into another file's outcome or dropped. Already correctly handles the exact "one failure must not discard others" shape its own header comment documents. No gap.

**Verification, run myself, real exit codes.** `npm run typecheck` - **0 errors**. `npx eslint .` - **0 errors**, same 3 pre-existing warnings. `npx vitest run` - **450/450 passed, 56/56 test files** (up from 446/55: +4 tests, +1 file, exactly the new `search-tenders.spec.ts`). The corrected per-file `*.test.ts` loop (no `--test` flag) - **27 files, 301 tests, 0 failures, standing baseline exactly unchanged** (no `.test.ts` file touched - the new coverage went into a `.spec.ts` file). `npx next build` - **compiled successfully**, same route table, `Proxy (Middleware)` present.

**Genuine red-then-green, run myself.** `git stash push -- app/app/_components/search-tenders.ts` (keeping the new spec file in place), reran: 2 of the 4 new tests failed exactly as predicted (`expected undefined to deeply equal [...]` - destructuring `{ results, error }` off the pre-fix bare-array return gives `undefined` for both fields), the other 2 (query-too-short, genuine-no-match) still passed since their expected shape happened to coincide. `git stash pop` restored the fix; all 4 passed again, confirmed.

**Does this confirm the hypothesis?** Yes, with an honest caveat on magnitude. A from-scratch read of 5 small/medium files (representative size for this codebase's Server Action layer) found 1 real, previously-undiscoverable-by-grep instance of the bug class in roughly 20 minutes of reading - a similar hit rate to several of the recent grep-refinement passes, but the KIND of finding is qualitatively different: it is in the grep's blind spot by construction (captured-but-discarded error), not by an exclusion-rule accident, meaning no amount of further grep-pattern refinement on the existing `"const { data"`/missing-`error:` model could ever have found it. That said, the severity this time is genuinely low (UI convenience, not a gate/money/RLS finding) - unlike several recent grep-pass findings (`loadDocumentExpiryOverview()`, `getNotifications()`, `syncWonProjectToTeam()`) which were compliance-adjacent and behaviorally dangerous. One data point is not enough to conclude from-scratch reading strictly dominates grep refinement for THIS codebase's remaining surface, but it is enough to say the grep's fundamental target shape (missing error capture) is provably narrower than the full bug class (error capture discarded into an ambiguous return value), and a future pass should treat "error captured but not meaningfully propagated to the caller" as its own distinct thing to look for - genuinely ungreppable by any literal-substring method tried so far, since the signal is in what the function DOES with a value it already has, not in what syntax is present or absent.

**Backlog status.** 1 real finding fixed with a behavior change, pushed directly to `main` (`6424df6`, no PR) - low severity, additive, no RLS/security-boundary or money-path change, same risk tier as this doc's many prior direct-push fixes. The original standing 43-hit read-grep and the 33-hyphenated-file surface remain untouched this pass (this pass's whole budget went to the from-scratch-read angle instead, per the directive). The 6 standing judgment-call items (`start_payfast_checkout()`'s revenue-integrity gap, the impersonation session-refresh gap in `proxy.ts`, `held_registrations`-vs-CV display format, the zero-recipients batched-send sub-case, the live `RESEND_API_KEY` validity question, PR #176/#177/#178/#179 all awaiting Sarel's own merge decision) remain exactly as described - not touched, not resolved. Migrations `0117`-`0120` still on `main`, still not applied to production - untouched this pass. **For a future pass:** either continue the from-scratch-read approach on a fresh batch of never-named files (this pass only covered 5 of the ~150-file `app/app`/`app/lib` surface - plenty left), go back to the two oldest untouched grep threads, or pick a different angle entirely (a fresh `engine/` Python subsystem read, or revisiting a standing judgment-call item) - this pass's own data point is suggestive but not conclusive enough to mandate one over the other.

## Prior pass (2026-11-06, standing solution-architect review): a FOURTH systematic blind spot in the TS-sweep's own grep - array/tuple-destructured `Promise.all()` reads never matched the sweep's literal `"const { data"` grep either (a `[` sits between `const` and `{`, or the whole tuple sits on its own line, or several `{ data: x }` members share one long single-line destructure with only ONE `const` at the very start) - found and fixed 24 instances across 15 files, including one genuine hard-stop-adjacent gate finding (traced safe) and two genuine silent-false-"all clear" UI bugs (fixed with real behavior changes, not just logging)

Oriented from `968feaa` (immediately-preceding pass, docs-only "clean sweep" entry, no code touched). `git fetch origin main` found that one sibling-session commit in flight when this pass started; re-fetched and fast-forward-merged it (`b2c1b23..968feaa`) before finishing, confirmed no overlap (it only appended to this doc), then pushed this pass's own work on top. PR #176/#177/#178/#179 (and #164/#165) re-checked via `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls` at the start of this pass: unchanged, all still open/draft exactly as the prior entry recorded. Not touched, not merged.

**How this was found.** Took the standing directive's own suggestion literally: picked a plausible "other shape the `const { data` grep could miss" and grepped for it directly rather than reasoning about it. `grep -rn "Promise.all" --include="*.ts" app/app app/lib | grep -v "\.spec\.\|\.test\."` surfaced every call site; checking each by hand against `grep -n "const { data"` on the same file showed the array-destructure form (`const [{ data: x }, { data: y }] = await Promise.all([...])`) never matches - the literal 13-character substring `"const { data"` requires `const` immediately followed by `{ data`, and a `[`, a line break, or several unrelated tokens (another destructured member, `readiness`, `notifications`, etc.) sitting between them all defeat it. This is a cousin of the 3rd blind spot the immediately-preceding-but-one pass found (bare writes with no destructuring) - same root cause (the grep's literal-substring method, not any particular exclusion rule, was too narrow), one more shape of it.

**Full list of the 24 fixed instances, by file:**
- `app/app/tenders/[id]/compliance-data.ts` (3 Promise.all groups, 15 reads total: the top 9-way `company/pack/requirementRows/financial/briefing/roleRows/tagRows/officeRows/letterRows` read, plus the conditional `prov/asg` and `ppl/prj/cvs/gen` reads) - **the one real gate-adjacent finding, traced carefully, concluded safe.** `loadTenderCompliance()` feeds `packReadiness()`, which `requestSubmissionPack()` (`actions.ts:139-142`) uses as a genuine server-side hard stop (`if (readiness.unfilledPositions.length > 0) fail(...)`) - and `request_submission_pack_checked()` (migration 0115) does NOT independently re-verify unfilled positions, it only checks the billing quota and inserts the job row with the client-supplied `readiness_snapshot` verbatim. So a failed `requirementRows` read COULD, in principle, make a required-but-unconfirmed position vanish from `positionRows` (if it also has no `tender_pack_assignments` row yet, e.g. on a first-ever pack request) and let `unfilledPositions` wrongly come back empty - the TS gate passing when it shouldn't. Read `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py` directly (~line 505) to check whether this is actually exploitable: it is NOT - the engine re-derives `required` straight from the uploaded Technical workbook's own SETUP sheet (`read_required_positions(Workbook(technical))`) and `unassigned` from a fresh `tender_pack_assignments` read, completely independent of the TS-side `readiness_snapshot`, and raises `ValueError` (job marked `'failed'` with a visible `error_message`, confirmed at `process_pack_jobs.py:751`) if any required position is still unconfirmed. Same defense-in-depth shape already documented for `confirmPositionPerson()`'s own writes in the immediately-preceding-but-two pass. A TS-side bypass here just means the job gets queued and then fails loudly at the engine instead of being caught a step earlier - self-correcting on retry, not a real disqualification-risk bypass. Logged (9 + 2 + 4 `console.error` lines), not gated. Also checked `b7-data.ts`'s own `loadB7State()` (feeds the identical kind of hard stop, `b7.blocker` at `actions.ts:154`) for the same reason - same conclusion, same engine-level `sanral_b7.applicability()` re-derivation from the real workbook, logged there too.
- `app/app/tenders/[id]/actions.ts` (`syncWonProjectToTeam()`, lines ~561-610) - **the one other real finding fixed with a behavior change.** The `[{ data: assignmentRows }, { data: tenderRow }, { data: reqRows }]` read had no error captured at all. `assignmentRows` is what `confirmed` (the list of positions to sync into each person's `projects` row, feeding their next generated CV) is filtered from - a failed read silently made `confirmed = []`, skipped the whole upsert block, and the action still redirected to `#won-project` with no `error=` param, reporting success while nothing was actually synced. Fixed with the same `fail()` pattern this exact function already uses for every other read in it (`packErr`/`updErr`/`staleErr`/`syncErr`) - `asgErr` now fails loudly; `tenderErr`/`reqErr` (display text only) and a separate `existingSynced` read (stale-row cleanup only, safe direction) are logged, not gated.
- `app/lib/documentExpiry.ts` (`loadDocumentExpiryOverview()`) - **real finding, fixed with a behavior change.** All 4 reads (`companyRow/heldRows/typeRows/peopleRows`) had no error captured. Every caller used `rows.length === 0` to mean "nothing tracked, 100% compliant" - `dashboard/page.tsx`'s own `vaultCompliancePct = vaultRows.length === 0 ? 100 : ...` and `DocumentExpiryOverview.tsx`'s own "Every tracked document is valid - nothing needs attention right now." message both took a FAILED read (which also empties `rows`) for that exact same genuine-empty case. This is the dangerous direction the sweep looks for, not a logging gap: the one widget whose whole job (Sarel's own ask, "2 documents need attention before your next bid") is catching real compliance gaps could show a false "100% compliant"/"all valid" on a transient Supabase failure. Fixed by changing the return shape to `{ rows, error }` (same precedent as `fetchSavingsCounterSummary()`'s own earlier-today fix) and updating both callers: `dashboard/page.tsx` now shows "Couldn't check right now" instead of a percentage, never defaults to 100% on error; `DocumentExpiryOverview.tsx` shows a destructive "Couldn't check document expiry right now - try refreshing." banner instead of either message. []`/null defaults as "genuinely nothing expiring/closing soon". - `company/document-scan/actions.ts` - `confirmIdDocument()`/`confirmCvHandoff()`'s own principal/person lookups (lines 303, 354) fail closed. But `skipOnboardingDocument()` - a sibling of the file's own already-fixed `confirmVaultDocument()`/`confirmIdDocument()`/`discardOnboardingDocument()` - had NO check at all, not even `error`: **real finding, fixed** (see below).
- `company/properties/actions.ts` - the `docs`-before-delete read (storage leak only, safe) and the `existing`-before-replace read in `savePropertyDocument()` (decides update-vs-insert branch) were both traced. The second one looked concerning at first (a failed read mis-routes to the insert branch even when a row already exists) until checking `0050_principals_registrations_properties.sql:569` - `property_documents_one_per_type` is a real unique index on `(property_id, document_type)`, so a wrongly-taken insert branch is caught by the DB with a `23505`, not a silent duplicate. Confirmed safe (same "DB backstop catches it one call later" shape already established for `tenders/[id]/actions.ts:156` in the immediately-preceding pass).
- `company/principals/actions.ts`, `company/registrations/actions.ts`, `company/bank-accounts/actions.ts`, `company/team/actions.ts`, `admin/actions.ts`, `discovery/actions.ts`, `pipeline/actions.ts`, `invite/actions.ts`, `onboarding/actions.ts`, `_components/actions.ts` - read in full; every write already captures and checks `error`, every dedupe/ownership read already fails closed. No new finding in any of these.

**The grep-blind-spot finding, traced file by file (all fixed, logging-only except one):**
- **`company/document-scan/actions.ts`'s `skipOnboardingDocument()` - real finding, fixed with behavior change.** Pre-fix: `await supabase.from("onboarding_document_results").update({ review_status: "skipped" }).eq("id", result.id);` with nothing checked at all, then an unconditional `redirect(`${back}?saved=skipped`)`. A membership-revoked-mid-request zero-row match (the same RLS race already fixed on this row's sibling `discardOnboardingDocument()`, right below it in the same file) left the row stuck on `"pending_review"` - silently reappearing in the "to review" queue - while the UI reported the skip as having worked. Fixed with the identical `.select("id").maybeSingle()` + `error`/row check shape as `discardOnboardingDocument()`, with new test coverage (`skipOnboardingDocument - membership revoked mid-request` / `- real update still succeeds`) and a genuine red/green check: `git stash`'d just the fix and reran - the new test failed exactly as predicted (`expected '/company/document-scan?saved=skipped' not to contain 'saved=skipped'`); `git stash pop` restored it, all 9 of this file's own tests green again.
- **`company/document-scan/actions.ts`'s `markApplied()` helper - traced, low severity, fixed logging-only.** Runs AFTER the real write (companies/experience_items/cv_uploads/company_principals update, plus the onboarding source file already removed by several callers) has already succeeded, so there is nothing left to roll back on its own failure. Consequence: the row stays stuck on `"pending_review"` (visible in the "to review" queue despite being actually filed), but a re-confirm attempt fails cleanly since the onboarding source file is already gone by then - confusing, not destructive.
- **`tenders/[id]/pack-inputs-actions.ts`'s `confirmPositionPerson()` - 3 unguarded writes, traced carefully (this one touches the key-person confirm gate, so checked against the real enforcement path, not just assumed safe), fixed logging-only.** The `tender_pack_assignments` upsert (sets `confirmed_person_id`, the field that matters) and both `tender_packs.status` flips (`'confirmed'`/`'suggested'`) all go unchecked. Traced whether a silent failure could let a stale/wrong confirmation reach pack generation: it can't - `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py:507` computes its own `unassigned` list straight from `tender_pack_assignments.confirmed_person_id`, re-read fresh at generation time, never from `tender_packs.status`; and `tender_packs.status` itself is display-only in this app (`app/lib/dashboardStats.ts`'s readiness check, the page.tsx badge - confirmed by grep, nothing server-side gates on it). A silently-failed upsert/flip here means "the click did nothing, DB state is unchanged" - self-correcting on the next genuine attempt, never a false-confirmed state surviving into the real gate. Logged, not behaviorally changed.
- **`tenders/[id]/general-actions.ts` - 2 unguarded writes, fixed logging-only.** The `tender_answers` clear-delete in `saveGeneralAnswers()` (a failed clear just leaves the old value on file instead of blank) and the `tender_packs.document_requirements`/`intake` reset in `removePrivateTenderDocument()` - this second one is the exact candidate the immediately-preceding pass already named and explicitly deferred ("not fixed - noted as a real but minor candidate for a future pass if this exact file gets picked up again") - picked up now via this pass's own new angle, logged as that pass anticipated.
- **`tenders/[id]/actions.ts` - 3 unguarded writes, fixed logging-only.** `ensureClosingMilestone()`/`ensureBriefingMilestone()`'s own idempotent auto-seed upserts (a failed seed just means a reminder task doesn't appear this page load; re-attempted on the next) and `reassignTenderTask()`/`advanceTaskStatus()`'s inline tap-to-update writes (same shape, UI-only consequence).
- **`lib/pipeline.ts`'s `advanceFoundToAssessing()` - fixed logging-only.** This function's own docstring already calls it "best-effort: a failure here must not block the pack request itself" - the failure was just previously invisible even to its own console.

**Fixed, 6 files, 1 commit (`507e351`)**: `app/app/company/document-scan/actions.ts` (`skipOnboardingDocument()` real fix + `markApplied()` logging), `app/app/company/document-scan/actions.spec.ts` (2 new tests), `app/app/tenders/[id]/actions.ts` (4 writes logged), `app/app/tenders/[id]/general-actions.ts` (2 writes logged), `app/app/tenders/[id]/pack-inputs-actions.ts` (3 writes logged), `app/lib/pipeline.ts` (1 write logged).

**Traced several of the remaining ~41 untraced hits to their real consumers, all the way through, not stopping at "returns null, looks safe":**

- **`tenders/[id]/reuse-past-submission.tsx` / `lib/pastSubmissionReuse.ts` - real finding, fixed, PR #179.** The widget itself (`reuse-past-submission.tsx`) hides "Start from a previous submission" once the CURRENT tender's own `pipeline_stage` is `submitted`/`briefing_shortlisted`/`won`/`lost` - but that's the only place this was ever checked. `buildReusePlan()` (the one function both the preview and `applyPastSubmission()` rebuild their plan from, per its own header comment, "from the database, not taken from the preview the browser saw") only ever validated the chosen SOURCE tender against `DONE_STAGES` - it never re-checked the TARGET. Fixed both; opened as PR #178, not pushed directly (this changes the real hard-stop on the core pack-generation pipeline)

Oriented from `12de22a` (immediately-preceding pass). `git fetch origin main` found zero sibling-session commits before this pass started. Treating `engine/narrative/`, `engine/cv/`, `engine/onboarding/` as genuinely checked now (not just "shallow"), though not exhaustively read past the files named above (`generate_cv.py`, `extract_cv_fields.py`, `build_general_pack.py`, `fill_flat_pdf.py`, `fill_sbd_docx.py`, `requirements.py`, `generate_narrative.py`, `build_docx.py`, `build_prompt.py`, `uniqueness.py` remain unread this pass).

**Pivoted to the TS-side sweep, re-grepped `const { data` with no nearby `error` capture from scratch** (same command as prior passes: `app/app/**/*.tsx`/`*.ts`, excluding `actions.ts`/`.spec.`/`.test.` files) - same 45 hits as the immediately-preceding pass's own count, confirming the grep itself hasn't drifted. Traced `app/tenders/[id]/compliance-data.ts:41`'s unprotected `tenders` row read (`loadTenderCompliance`'s own entry point - `const { data: tender } = ...; if (!tender) return null;`) all the way through its 4 real call sites (`compliance-report.tsx`, `disqualification-guard.tsx`, `submission-pack.tsx`, `pack-review-data.ts`) rather than stopping at "returns null, looks safe."

**The real finding, bigger than the read-failure framing it started from.** `submission-pack.tsx`'s and `general-workspace.tsx`'s own "Generate/Fill pack" buttons both compute `fixCount = snapshot.mapped ? computeTenderReadiness(snapshot.sections).fix.length : 0` and disable the button when `fixCount > 0` - this is prompt 9 part 2's own "Submit button: disabled while any Fix item is open" feature (app/AGENTS.md). Followed the button's own form `action` into `requestSubmissionPack()` (`actions.ts`) and `requestJob()`'s `generate_pack` branch (`general-actions.ts`), and from there into `request_submission_pack_checked()`/`request_general_job_checked()` (migration 0115, read in full): **neither Server Action nor either Postgres RPC ever re-checks `computeTenderReadiness(...).fix` at all** - only `unfilledPositions`, missing blank templates, Form B7, the pack-review confirmation, billing quota, and "already queued". The Fix-item gate is a `disabled` HTML attribute and nothing else. An HTML `disabled` attribute is purely client-rendered; it does not stop a direct POST to the Server Action (devtools, a saved/replayed form, any client that doesn't re-render the button's state) - so a tender with a real, disqualifying Fix item open (a mandatory compliance document never confirmed, an unconfirmed key person, etc.) could still have its submission pack requested and built, with nothing on the server ever having checked. This is the same dominant bug class this review loop has mined all week (a safeguard that exists in exactly one place and silently isn't the real gate), just found in the newer Fix/Provide/Verify gating feature rather than an old unprotected read.

**A second, narrower instance of the classic shape, found while fixing the first.** Both buttons' own `snapshot.mapped ? ... : 0` fallback treats "not mapped" as "zero Fix items" - but since `submission-pack.tsx` only ever mounts for a tender page.tsx has already confirmed is SANRAL-family, and `general-workspace.tsx` only reaches this line after its own earlier, separate read already confirmed a requirements manifest exists, `!mapped` at this specific point in either file can only mean *this* request's own fresh read of `loadTenderCompliance`/`loadGeneralPackReviewSnapshot` failed transiently - never a genuine "not applicable" case. On a transient blip, after a tender had already been reviewed once (`reviewed=true` persists from an earlier visit), the old code would silently re-enable the button with the Fix check never having actually run that render - "a failed read looks falsely ready," reached through the new Fix-gate instead of an old field.

**Fixed, 4 files** (not yet pushed to `main` - see below): `actions.ts`'s `requestSubmissionPack()` and `general-actions.ts`'s `requestJob()` (`generate_pack` branch) both now re-read the same cached Pack Review snapshot and fail closed (`fail()`/`redirect()` with the same "Fix N items first" wording the button already shows) when `fixCount > 0`, and fail closed with a "couldn't check readiness" message when `!mapped` too (never silently proceeding on an unreadable snapshot). `submission-pack.tsx` and `general-workspace.tsx` themselves: `!mapped` now produces its own distinct "Couldn't check compliance readiness - refresh and try again" disabled reason instead of being folded into "0 fix items". `general-workspace.tsx`'s own `badges.generalFixCount` (a separate, purely cosmetic tab-badge count, same already-accepted tier as every other count this review loop has left alone) deliberately keeps the old 0-on-unmapped number - only the button's own gate needed the stricter tri-state. Every previously-passing path (`mapped=true`) is unchanged byte-for-byte in all 4 files; the new branches are reachable only when `mapped` is false, which is unreachable on the happy path for either component by construction.

**Verification, run myself, real exit codes**: `npm run typecheck` (`next typegen && tsc --noEmit`) - **0 errors**. `npx eslint .` - **0 errors**, same 3 pre-existing warnings unchanged (`Logo.tsx` x2 `no-img-element`, `analytics/page.tsx` 1 unused `STAGE_META`). `npx vitest run` - **434/434 passed, 54/54 files**. The corrected per-file `*.test.ts` loop (no `--test` flag, looping `node --experimental-strip-types`) - **27 files, 301 tests, 0 failures**, standing baseline unchanged. `npx next build` - **compiled successfully**, same route table, `/tenders/[id]` still `◐` Partial Prerender, `Proxy (Middleware)` line present.

**No new automated test, and no red-then-green manual revert-and-confirm for this one** - flagging plainly rather than quietly skipping past it: both Server Action changes are thin compositions of already-tested logic (`computeTenderReadiness` has its own 5-case `tender-readiness.test.ts`; `loadPackReviewSnapshot`/`loadGeneralPackReviewSnapshot` are the exact same cached snapshots the already-shipped button gate reads) inside files that import `next/navigation` and the Supabase server client at module scope - the identical "unsafe to import directly into a `.test.ts` file" situation this doc's own history already documents for this exact file category (`general-workspace.tsx`, `pack-review-data.ts`, prompt 9 part 0's own entry above). Correctness here rests on the composed, already-tested functions plus the full QA suite above, same standard that entry set - not asserted as equivalent to an actual red/green cycle.

**Why opened as PR #178, not pushed directly to `main`.** This is a genuine behavior change to the real hard-stop gate on the core submission-pack generation pipeline, for both tender families at once - unlike this review loop's usual "additive, narrowly-gated, unreachable on any currently-passing path" dashboard/report fixes, a company currently relying (even unknowingly, e.g. if their own browser's JS failed to apply the disabled state, or if they genuinely have an open Fix item right now) on the previously-missing server-side check would be newly, correctly blocked by this fix where they weren't before. **The real finding, in the 2 large remaining files (`general-workspace.tsx`, `general-pack-review-data.ts` - both part of the general/non-SANRAL tender-workspace family).** Both files' own "Company experience evidence" check is gated `if (evidenceRules.length > 0 && company?.id)`, where `company` comes from a `companies` read earlier in each file with no error captured at all (destructured as bare `{ data: companyRow }`). Supabase client calls never throw on a query-level error - a failed read returns `{data: null, error: {...}}`, it does not raise - so a transient `companies` read failure makes `company?.id` falsy via the exact same code path as "this tender genuinely needs no experience evidence," with nothing to tell them apart. Traced the real consequence in each file rather than assuming it from the shape alone:
- **`general-pack-review-data.ts`**: this section is one of several whose items feed `tender-readiness.ts`'s `computeTenderReadiness()`, which in turn is `general-workspace.tsx`'s own `generalFixCount` - the ONLY thing gating `disabled={!!generalDisabledReason}` on the "Generate a new pack"/"Generate submission pack" button (checked the actual JSX call site, not inferred). `computeTenderReadiness()`'s own doc comment already states the intended safeguard explicitly: "A section whose own data failed to load (`section.error`) contributes nothing... silently treating a read failure as '0 items, fully ready' would be worse than leaving it out of the count" - but that safeguard only works for a section that sets `section.error` via its own `catch` block, and this section's `catch` is never reached here because nothing actually throws. The result is exactly the thing the comment says is worse than omitting the section: on a `companies` (or the separate `experience_matches` RPC, same no-throw shape) read failure, this section silently pushes ZERO items - not a `missing`/Fix item, not `section.error` - so a tender that genuinely still needs its qualifying-experience evidence confirmed could have that one remaining gap vanish from the count on a blip, letting `generalFixCount` read 0 and wrongly enable pack generation. Compared directly against the SANRAL sibling (`compliance-data.ts`'s B6 check in `tenderCompliance.ts`) to confirm this is a real divergence, not an intentional design: the SANRAL side already has an explicit `else if (!input.experienceAvailable)` branch that pushes an honest "The Experience Library couldn't be read for this check..." item with status `check` - the general-family side never got the equivalent branch.
- **`general-workspace.tsx`**: the same `company?.id`-gated `experience` read feeds only a display block ("Company experience this tender accepts") - confirmed this one does NOT feed `peopleGaps` (`peopleGaps = regGaps + roleGaps`, computed from a separate, correctly-fail-safe pair of counts), so this instance is display-only, not a gating bug. Its own sibling `experience?.error` branch already shows a warning for the OTHER failure mode (`findMatchingExperience()`'s own RPC error) - but `company?.id` being falsy makes `experience` itself `null`, which that existing branch can't catch, so the read failure silently renders as if the tender simply had no evidence requirement at all (no warning, no chip, same look as "nothing to show").

**Fixed, both files, same severity choice (`needs_input`/"Provide," not `missing`/"Fix," matching the SANRAL precedent's own severity rather than inventing a stricter one):** `general-pack-review-data.ts`'s experience section now pushes an explicit "Your company record couldn't be read for this check..." item when `company?.id` is falsy, and a separate "The Experience Library couldn't be read for this check..." item when `findMatchingExperience()` itself returns `{error}` (previously silently dropped too, independent of the `company?.id` issue) - both now visible instead of vanishing, and because they're `needs_input` (bucketed "Provide" by `reviewStatusToBidTask()`), they can never themselves disable pack generation on a mere blip, only make the real remaining gap visible again on a genuine one. `general-workspace.tsx`'s own `experience` variable now resolves to `{ items: [], error: "Your company record couldn't be read for this check." }` instead of `null` when `company?.id` is falsy, so the file's own pre-existing `experience?.error` warning branch now catches this case too instead of silently skipping it - no new branch needed, no change to any gating logic (confirmed `peopleGaps` untouched). The non-error, non-empty-`evidenceRules` path is unchanged byte-for-byte in both files - every new branch is reachable only on a value that is `null`/falsy on every currently-passing path.

**Verification - 2 files, same QA gate, run once on the complete working tree**: `npm run typecheck` (`next typegen && tsc --noEmit`, never raw `tsc --noEmit`) - **exit 0, 0 errors**. `npx eslint .` - **exit 0, 0 errors**, same 3 pre-existing warnings confirmed unchanged (`Logo.tsx` x2 `no-img-element`, `analytics/page.tsx` 1 unused `STAGE_META`). `npx vitest run` - **exit 0, 434/434 passed, 54/54 files** (no `.spec.ts` touched - neither file has one). **Corrected per-file method** (`find . -name "*.test.ts" -not -path "*/node_modules/*"`, looping `node --experimental-strip-types "$f"` with no `--test` flag and no glob, summing each file's own TAP `# tests N`/`# fail N` lines, run myself) - **27 files, 301 tests, 0 failures**, baseline reconfirmed (no `*.test.ts` touched - neither file has one). `npx next build` - **exit 0, compiled successfully**, same 62-route table (checked line-for-line against the pre-fix listing), `/tenders/[id]` still `◐` Partial Prerender (unchanged), `Proxy (Middleware)` line present and unchanged.

**Why committed directly to `main`, not a draft PR**: both fixes are additive-only (new, narrowly-gated branches that push an explicit item only on a value that's falsy/absent on every currently-passing path; the non-error path is untouched), touch exactly the one check each file already had, no schema/RLS/migration/Server Action involved, same risk tier as the `tenders/[id]/page.tsx` fix (`5d587d9`) this doc already pushed directly despite comparable severity, for the identical reasoning (narrow, provably-safe-by-inspection, no live-DB test harness available for either file - same situation this doc has documented repeatedly for Server Component page/workspace files).

The 4 secondary reads combine into one `secondaryLoadError` boolean gating a new additive banner above the existing cards ("Some of your CV details (uploads, generated CVs or project history) couldn't be loaded..."), same pattern as `6a6fc5b`/`c871d96`/etc. The non-error path is byte-for-byte unchanged - every computed value is identical whenever all reads succeed.

Read both end to end rather than assuming the shape was identical from the name alone.

- `proxy.ts`: `const { data: membership } = await supabase.from("company_members")...` with no error captured; `if (!membership && !path.startsWith("/onboarding"))` redirects to `/onboarding`. A transient read failure is indistinguishable from "this user genuinely has no company" - **on every guarded page load**, not just one page - and force-redirects an already-onboarded user away from whatever they actually asked for, onto Onboarding Screen 1 ("create your company"). Traced the real worst-case consequence rather than assuming it: migration `0116` (already live - it is NOT one of the 0117-0120 migrations still pending on production, confirmed by checking which migration numbers that pending list actually names) added `company_members_user_id_key unique (user_id)`, specifically because of an earlier finding that `create_company_and_join()` had no protection against a double-submit creating two companies for one user. That constraint means actually submitting Screen 1 here would fail safely with the function's own existing friendly "Could not create your company - try again" message, not create a duplicate company - so this is a confusing, wrong-destination UX bug on every transient blip, not a data-corrupting one. - `app/onboarding/page.tsx`: the identical unprotected read one hop downstream - `if (!membership)` renders Screen 1 with no way to tell a failed read from a genuine first-time user, so even without `proxy.ts`'s own redirect (a stale bookmark/link lands here directly too), an already-onboarded member hitting a transient blip sees "create your company" with no warning.
