**The finding, read end to end before touching anything.** Inside the page's `if (tenderPack)` block (reached once a tender has a pack - i.e. every tender actually being worked, not just browsed), 5 reads were destructured as just `{ data }` with no error captured: a `Promise.all()` of `tender_requirements`/`person_role_eligibility`/`tender_roles`, plus separate `tender_pack_assignments` and `generated_cvs` reads. A 6th, the page's own `people` roster read (`assignablePeopleRows`, used for the task-assignee and key-position-confirmation dropdowns), also lacked error capture. Two concrete, reachable consequences, re-confirmed by reading every downstream consumer rather than assumed from the pattern:
1. **Cosmetic-but-familiar instance**: `positions.length === 0` already rendered "No positions listed yet..." (the exact established false-empty-state claim) on a silent `tender_requirements`/`tender_pack_assignments` failure; `assignablePeople.length === 0 && positions.length > 0` rendered "No one is captured on the People page yet..." on a silent `people` failure - both in the "Key positions" section, both indistinguishable from the genuine case.
2. **New, higher-severity instance, specific to this page**: `openPositionsCount` (computed from `requirementRows`/`assignments`, both from the unprotected reads) feeds directly into `PrimaryPackActionLink`'s `ready` prop at line ~780 (`ready={!!tenderPack && (!tenderReadiness || tenderReadiness.thingsLeft === 0) && openPositionsCount === 0}`), which gates whether the "Generate submission pack" primary action is enabled. Traced the failure mode concretely: if `tender_requirements` fails (returns `null` -> `requirementRows = []`) while `tender_pack_assignments` either also fails or genuinely has no rows yet for a position that was never confirmed, the computed `positions` set can lose a real, still-open position entirely - `openPositionsCount` reads `0` on a tender that still has an unconfirmed key person, and the pack-generation action is wrongly enabled. This is not a display-only mis-render; it is a readiness/submission-gating value computed from an unprotected read, on the one page in the app whose job is deciding whether a bid is actually ready to go out.

**Fixed**: all 6 reads now capture their own `error`, each logged via `console.error` with a distinct, page-specific message (matching this file's and this doc's existing convention). The 5 position/CV-related reads combine into one `keyPositionsError` boolean; the `people` roster read gets its own `peopleLoadError` (kept separate since it also affects the already-existing "no one captured" message independently of positions failing). `keyPositionsError` now also gates `ready` directly (`ready={!!tenderPack && !keyPositionsError && ...}`, never just the derived count) and is checked first in `disabledReason` ("Couldn't load this tender's key positions - try refreshing before the pack can be generated."), so a failed read can never silently enable pack generation, only ever block it (the always-safe direction). The "Key positions" section's render gate was widened from `positions.length > 0 || isSanralPackFamily` to also include `|| keyPositionsError`, so the new error banner is reachable even for a general-family tender whose positions list would otherwise be empty and the whole section would previously have disappeared rather than shown anything. Both existing false-empty-state messages ("No positions listed yet", "No one is captured on the People page yet") are now gated on `!keyPositionsError`/`!peopleLoadError` respectively, with a new destructive-tone inline banner (same `bg-destructive/10 text-destructive` treatment this file already uses for `ErrorBanner`, inlined here since this is inside a section body, not the page-level banner slot) shown instead whenever the real cause is a failed read. The non-error path is unchanged byte-for-byte - `keyPositionsError`/`peopleLoadError` are both `false` whenever every read succeeds, which is the entire pre-existing passing-case behaviour for `positions`/`assignments`/`generatedCvs`/`openPositionsCount`/`ready`/`disabledReason`.

Both call sites (`app/dashboard/page.tsx`, `app/analytics/page.tsx` - confirmed via grep these are the ONLY two callers of either `fetchSavingsCounterSummary()` or `SavingsCounterCard`) updated to destructure `{ summary, error }` and pass both through. The non-error path is unchanged on both pages and in the card - `error` is `false`/absent on every currently-passing code path, so the new branch is unreachable whenever both reads succeed, which is the entire rest of this function and component's existing behaviour.

## This pass (2026-11-06, standing solution-architect review): `pricePoints()`'s PPR 2022 price-points formula had no floor at 0, so the public `/tools/bee-preference-points` lead-magnet calculator rendered negative "preference points" for any realistic high-price input

Oriented from `9582a87` (own immediately-preceding pass, independently re-verified by the orchestrating session before this pass started per its own instruction - not re-verified again here). `git fetch origin main` found zero sibling-session commits - `HEAD` was already `origin/main`. Open PRs re-checked via the GitHub REST API (`gh api repos/.../pulls?state=open`, since `gh pr list`'s GraphQL path is blocked in this session): exactly three, unchanged - `#164`/`#165` (draft, stale since 2026-10-26, untouched) and `#176` (open, not draft, not merged, still awaiting Sarel's own go-ahead - not reviewed, not commented on, not touched this pass).

**Angle chosen, and what came up dry first.** The directive's own first-choice angle - other `.github/workflows/*.yml` multi-step Python pipelines with the same "claim/write in an earlier step, gated on a later step's unconfirmed outcome" shape `9582a87` just fixed in `daily-digest.yml` - was checked across every workflow in `.github/workflows/` and came back exhausted, not just assumed clean: `daily-discovery.yml` is the only other workflow that splits a Python "build" step (`watch_new_tenders.py`, writes `discovered_opportunities`/`discovery_seen_releases`) from a later, separate send step (`send-discovered-tenders.ts`, Node) - but read end to end, that send script's own `claim_notification` RPC call happens entirely WITHIN itself, in the same step, never in the earlier Python step. If the Node step never runs at all (an `npm ci` failure, a crash before `claim_notification` is ever called), nothing is marked claimed, and the next day's run picks the same `discovered_opportunities` rows back up automatically (its own `sinceIso` bounds to "last 2 days", confirmed by reading `send-discovered-tenders.ts` directly) - correctly decoupled already, not the same bug. Every other notify workflow (`compliance-alerts`, `corrigendum-alerts`, `deadline-reminders`, `founder-digest`, `onboarding-nudges`, `operational-alerts`, `returnables-digest`, `scout-alerts`) runs its own claim-and-send in one single Node step, confirmed by grepping each workflow file for its `run:` lines - no second script, no cross-step gap possible. This vein is genuinely exhausted now, not just this pass's own guess - every multi-step pipeline in the repo was actually read, not inferred from the one instance already fixed.

Also spot-checked the API-route-vs-Server-Action auth-parity angle: `app/app/api/**/route.ts` is only 3 files total (`billing/checkout`, `billing/payfast/itn`, `unsubscribe`) - read all 3. `checkout` requires `supabase.auth.getUser()` and redirects to `/login` if absent, same as a Server Action would gate. `payfast/itn` and `unsubscribe` are deliberately session-less webhook/one-click endpoints (PayFast's own server, and RFC 8058 mail-client auto-POSTs respectively) with their own already-documented, already-reviewed bearer-token/signature-based checks in place of a session - not a gap, by design, already commented as such in the files themselves. Nothing to fix here; too small a surface for a dedicated finding.

**The finding, from the "ZAR rounding/financial-calculation" angle.** `app/lib/preferencePoints.ts`'s `pricePoints()` implements the PPR 2022 reg 4/reg 5 price-points formula, `Ps = system-max x (1 - (Pt - Pmin) / Pmin)`, and its own comment already shows awareness that the result needs capping on the HIGH side ("never above the system's max... capped rather than allowed to exceed the max point by a rounding fluke") - but the function only ever did `Math.min(raw, maxPricePoints)`, with no floor on the LOW side. The raw formula goes negative for any `tenderPriceZar` more than double `lowestAcceptablePriceZar` (e.g. Pmin = R1,000,000, Pt = R2,500,000 -> `80 * (1 - 1.5) = -40`) - a real, reachable input on the public `/tools/bee-preference-points` calculator: read `BeePreferencePointsClient.tsx` directly and confirmed there is no upper-bound validation on the "Your tendered price" field at all, and the result card renders `{result.data.pricePoints} / {result.data.maxPricePoints}` verbatim, so a user who simply typed a price more than 2x the lowest bidder's would see "-40 / 80" and a correspondingly negative `totalPoints / 100`. A negative "preference points" figure is not how the PPR 2022 scoring is ever practically applied or presented - SBD 6.1's own Preference Points Claim Form has no box for a negative score, and no SCM practice note or worked example (including this repo's own `docs/specs/Tender-Regulatory-Compliance-Review.md` §2.1, re-read before concluding this) treats an over-priced bid as anything other than 0 price points, not an increasingly negative one. This is a UI/UX correctness bug on a public lead-magnet tool, not a judgment call to leave open - fixed by clamping the same way the high side already is.

**Fixed**: `pricePoints()` now does `Math.min(Math.max(raw, 0), maxPricePoints)` - clamped to `[0, maxPricePoints]` instead of only capped above. `calculatePreferencePoints()`'s `totalPoints` (which sums `pricePoints` + `beeGoalsPoints`) is unaffected in shape, just never fed a negative `pricePoints` input any more. Comment rewritten to document both bounds and why the low side matters here specifically (a real, unvalidated input on this exact page).

**Verified red-then-green.** Added 2 new tests to `app/lib/preferencePoints.test.ts`: the exact `Pt = 2 x Pmin` zero boundary (0 both with and without the fix - confirms the fix doesn't change the boundary itself), and a `Pt > 2 x Pmin` case (`Pt = 2,500,000`, and a further `Pt = 10,000,000` to confirm it stays at 0, not increasingly negative) asserting `pricePoints` returns exactly `0`. **Red confirmed directly**: `git stash push -- app/lib/preferencePoints.ts` (reverting only the implementation, keeping the new tests) and reran - `12 tests, 11 pass, 1 fail`, the failing one showing exactly the predicted pre-fix value (`AssertionError: -40 !== 0` at the `Pt = 2,500,000` case). `git stash pop` restored the fix, reran: **12/12 passed** (the file's own test count went from 10 to 12; the 2 new ones are additions, not replacements - every pre-existing case, including the Pt=Pmin/10%-above/rounding/throws/BEE-table/full-breakdown cases, is untouched and still green).

**Full suite, run after restoring the fix (not before)**: `npx tsc --noEmit` from `app/` - **0 errors**. `npx eslint .` - **0 errors**, same 3 pre-existing warnings this doc's own baseline already documents (`_components/Logo.tsx` x2 `no-img-element`, `analytics/page.tsx` 1 unused var), confirmed unchanged. `npx vitest run` - **427/427 passed, 52/52 files**, unchanged (no `.spec.ts` file touched). `node --experimental-strip-types --test` over all 27 `*.test.ts` files in `app/` - **240/240 passed** (238 baseline + the 2 new `preferencePoints.test.ts` cases; every other file's own count unchanged). `npx next build` - **compiled successfully**, same route shapes as `9582a87`'s own baseline including `/tools/bee-preference-points` and `/toolkit/bee-preference-points` (run out of caution since this lib file feeds that page, even though no page/route file itself was touched). Also re-ran `lib/sanralScoring.test.ts` + `lib/tenderCompliance.test.ts` directly (adjacent scoring logic, neither touched) - **13/13 passed**, confirming no regression nearby. No Python file touched this pass - no `py_compile`/`pytest` run needed.

**Why committed directly to `main`, not a draft PR**: pure function change in one file plus its own test file, no schema/RLS/migration/workflow touched, strictly a correctness fix in one direction (clamping an already-known-to-need-clamping formula at the other end it was missing), and the kind of small/well-verified fix the standing guardrails call for committing directly rather than opening a PR.

**Context for whoever picks this up next.** Migrations `0117`-`0120` still on `main`, still not applied to production - untouched this pass. PR `#176` still open, awaiting Sarel's own go-ahead - not touched. The 4 standing judgment-call items (`start_payfast_checkout()`'s revenue-before-ITN gap, the impersonation session-refresh gap, `held_registrations`-vs-CV display format, the zero-recipients batched-send sub-case) remain exactly as described - not touched, not resolved. The two veins flagged as exhausted (membership-revoked-mid-request, `AI-Call-Quality-Standard.md`) were correctly left alone this pass. The frontend empty-state/error-boundary systematic sweep flagged as still-open by 2 passes ago was **not touched this pass either** (a genuinely different angle was picked instead, per the directive's own menu of options) - still a real next-pass candidate. ## This pass (2026-11-06, standing solution-architect review): a fresh angle - the "claim the one-time digested-mark before confirming the send" bug class, already fixed for every OTHER notification type in this codebase (pack_ready, deadline reminders, operational alerts, returnables/compliance/discovered-tenders/scout-alert digests), had two unswept instances left in `engine/notify/daily_digest.py` - and they were the worst-case shape of this whole bug class, since "claim" and "send" here aren't two lines in one function but two DIFFERENT SCRIPTS in two DIFFERENT GitHub Actions steps. Fixed by moving the marking write to `send_digest_emails.py`, gated on a confirmed `sent` status; also corrected a now-demonstrably-false claim in the workflow's own header comment. 4 new tests, red-then-green confirmed. Committed and pushed directly to `main` - no PR (no schema/RLS/migration touched, same established fix pattern as every prior instance of this exact bug class, all of which were also committed directly).

Oriented from `4049d82` (own immediately-preceding pass, independently re-verified by the orchestrating session before this pass started per its own instruction - not re-verified again here). `git fetch origin main` found zero sibling-session commits, checked both before starting and again immediately before this commit - `HEAD` was already `origin/main` both times. Open PRs re-checked via the GitHub REST API (`gh api repos/.../pulls?state=open`, since `gh pr list`'s GraphQL path is blocked in this session): exactly three, unchanged - `#164`/`#165` (draft, stale since 2026-10-26) and `#176` (open, not draft, not merged, still awaiting Sarel's own go-ahead - not reviewed, not commented on, not touched this pass).

**Angle chosen**: the directive flagged both the "membership-revoked-mid-request" vein and the `AI-Call-Quality-Standard.md` cross-check as exhausted - explicitly not re-mined. Rather than the frontend empty-state/error-boundary angle (also offered, genuinely open, but a broader, shallower sweep), picked a line-by-line read of `engine/notify/daily_digest.py`/`send_digest_emails.py` end to end, looking specifically for the SAME "claimed a one-time token before the send was confirmed" shape the `fdeab92`/prior passes already found and fixed everywhere else in this codebase (the TS cron scripts, the pack-ready email) - checking whether that sweep, which the `fdeab92` pass's own entry explicitly scoped to `claim_notification`/`record_deadline_reminder_sent`/`record_operational_alert_sent` callers, had actually reached every real instance.

**The finding.** `daily_digest.py --mode live`'s `main()` called `discovery_downgrades.mark_digested()` and `watch_tender_updates.mark_digested()` - both real `PATCH` writes against `discovered_opportunities.downgrade_digested_at` and `tender_update_notifications.digested_at` - unconditionally, the moment a digest was merely BUILT (an item present in at least one person's assembled digest JSON), never gated on whether that digest was ever actually delivered. The real send is `send_digest_emails.py`, a SEPARATE script reading the `--out` JSON this one writes, run as its OWN later step in `.github/workflows/daily-digest.yml` with its OWN separate secrets (only `RESEND_API_KEY`/`DIGEST_FROM_ADDRESS` - confirmed by reading the workflow file, `send_digest_emails.py` has never had Supabase credentials in production at all). This is the identical bug class `fdeab92`'s pass fixed 4 instances of (and `send-returnables-digest.ts` before that) - but a WORSE-CASE shape of it: every other instance claimed its one-time token and attempted the send in the same function, so the gap was a few lines/milliseconds wide; here the "claim" (build step, writes to Supabase) and the real "send" (a wholly separate process, possibly minutes later, over its own network calls to Resend) are decoupled across a GitHub Actions step boundary. Concretely, before this fix, ANY of the following silently and permanently lost that day's re-assessed-tender-downgrade/tender-update content, with zero retry, ever: the "Send via Resend" step crashing, timing out, or being cancelled after the build step already succeeded; a Resend outage or bad/expired `RESEND_API_KEY` (which currently degrades gracefully, per that script's own design, by sending nothing and exiting 0 - a documented "safe" path that was nonetheless marking everything digested regardless); or even just ONE person's e-mail failing transiently (`send_one()`'s own `"failed"` status, which already exists and is exercised in this file's own tests) - that specific person's `tender_updates`/`reassessed_tenders` content for that day was marked delivered and never carried again, even though their inbox never received it. Confirmed by reading `daily_digest.py`'s `main()` (the two `mark_digested()` call sites, both gated only on "did this item appear in a built digest", never on send outcome) and `send_digest_emails.py` end to end (confirmed zero Supabase imports/env-var reads anywhere in it before this pass) and the workflow file (confirmed the "Send via Resend" step's `env:` block only ever had the two Resend secrets). Also caught, incidentally: the workflow's own header comment claimed "daily_digest.py's own --mode live is read-only against Supabase... this workflow cannot write or delete anything in the real database" - demonstrably false even before this pass's own finding (that step already writes `deadline_reminders_seen`/`digest_readiness_seen` seen-store rows every run via `watch_deadlines.save_seen_db()`/`save_readiness_seen_db()`), corrected alongside the real fix rather than left to mislead a future reader.

**Fixed**, moving the responsibility to where the actual send outcome is known rather than adding a check in place (the two scripts' separation means there's nowhere in `daily_digest.py` itself where "confirmed sent" could ever be known):

## This pass (2026-11-06, standing solution-architect review): the "membership-revoked-mid-request" meta-sweep's own "exhausted across the 8 named files" claim (`3aa470a`) held for the WRITE that each file's own fix targeted, but missed a second, later write inside one of those already-"fixed" functions - `app/app/company/registrations/actions.ts`'s own `saveHeldRegistration()`, fixed for its row-update write by `23b43b4`. Found and fixed the gap, verified red-then-green with 2 new tests, committed and pushed directly to `main`.

Oriented from `b764cf2` (own immediately-preceding pass, independently re-verified by the orchestrating session before this pass started - not re-verified again here, per instruction). `git fetch origin main` found zero sibling-session commits, both before starting and again immediately before this commit - `HEAD` was already `origin/main` both times. Open PRs re-checked via the GitHub REST API (`gh api repos/.../pulls?state=open`, since `gh pr list`'s GraphQL path is blocked in this session): exactly three, as expected - `#164`/`#165` (both draft, stale, untouched since 2026-10-26) and `#176` (open, NOT draft, NOT merged - left exactly as is, re-checked again after this pass's own push, still unchanged).

**The quick spot-check the directive asked for, done first**: re-grepped every `app/app/**/actions.ts` for `.update(`/`.delete(` not already chained with a `.select(...).maybeSingle()`/`.single()` gate. Most hits were either already-covered (just not matched by the crude single-line grep, because the `.select()` sits on a later line of the same chain) or genuinely low-severity (a plain UI-state `.update()` with no file/destructive consequence and no existing check at all, e.g. `tenders/[id]/actions.ts`'s `reassignTenderTask()`/`advanceTaskStatus()` - inline tap-to-update task fields, no error check, no destructive write, judged not worth fixing on the same proportionality basis prior passes have used for similar no-consequence cases). One hit stood out: `company/registrations/actions.ts` line 86, inside `saveHeldRegistration()` - a file this bug class's meta-sweep explicitly lists as already fully covered.

**The actual finding - read `saveHeldRegistration()` end to end again rather than trusting "this file is done" from the file-level list.** The function has TWO separate writes to `held_registrations`, not one: (1) the row's own field update (`.update(row).eq("id", id)`), fixed by `23b43b4` with `.select("id").maybeSingle()` plus a real "no longer there" error path; and (2), only reached when a certificate file is attached, a SECOND, later update that records the just-uploaded file's path (`.update({storage_path, original_filename}).eq("id", heldId)`) - still checking only `error`, exactly the pre-`23b43b4` shape, never touched by that fix or by any later meta-sweep pass (both of which evidently read only as far as the first write in this function before moving on). The two writes have two independent timing windows: fixing (1) does nothing to protect (2) - a membership-revoked-mid-request race (another admin's `removeMember()`, 0114) landing specifically between the row write succeeding and this second write still hits RLS's own `using (is_company_member(company_id))` (0050), re-evaluated against the then-current row, and PostgREST returns the same `error: null`/zero-rows-affected 2xx this whole bug class is built on. Pre-fix, the code: uploads the new certificate to storage (succeeds, since storage RLS is a separate, already-correct check), then this second update silently no-ops, then - checking only `error`, which is null - goes on to delete `existing.storage_path`, the OLD file, which the row STILL actually references since the attach write never took effect. Net result, worse than a plain orphan: the row ends up pointing at a file that no longer exists at all, while the real new file sits permanently unreferenced in storage - and the page reports "Registration saved".

**Fixed** with the same established pattern used throughout this bug class - chained `.select("id").maybeSingle()` onto the attach write, gated on the returned row (not just `error`); on a zero-row match, the newly-uploaded (now-orphaned) file is removed and the action fails with a clear error, and - critically - the OLD file is left alone (never reached, since the gate `fail()`s before that line).

**Picked up the directive's own explicit continuation**: the prior pass's meta-sweep (re-reading every file that got a fix from this bug class, end to end, for call sites the original fix never reached) covered `company/properties/actions.ts`, `company/principals/actions.ts`, `company/registrations/actions.ts`, `experience/actions.ts` and the newly-discovered `company/bank-accounts/actions.ts` - but NOT `company/actions.ts` (only `uploadVaultDocument()` fixed, by `7345243`) or `company/document-scan/actions.ts` (only `confirmVaultDocument()`/`confirmIdDocument()` fixed, by `0a3ac73`). Read both end to end. Separately, re-assessed the prior pass's own explicitly-flagged, deliberately-unfixed residual - `people/actions.ts`'s `deletePerson()` - since the directive invited an independent second opinion on it, not just a rubber-stamp.

**The `deletePerson()` re-assessment is the significant correction here.** The prior pass's own words: "a microseconds-wide window between two consecutive awaited calls, no destructive consequence... the window is narrower by orders of magnitude than every instance actually fixed above." Reading the function end to end rather than taking that characterization on trust: it is backwards. `deletePerson()`'s real order was (1) confirm the person exists, (2) read every CV-upload/generated-CV/held-registration storage path this person owns (two parallel `select`s, two storage `list()` calls), (3) remove the CV/generated-CV files from the `cv-documents` bucket (checked by `error`), (4) remove the held-registration certificate files from the `company-documents` bucket (**not checked by anything at all** - the prior pass's own claim that "its own storage-file removals already correctly check their own error" was true for step 3 but not step 4, an oversight in that pass's own read), THEN (5) `supabase.from("people").delete().eq("id", id).eq("company_id", companyId)`, checked only by `error`. The real race window for step 5 is the ENTIRE span from step 1 to step 5 - every read, every listing, both storage removals - not "two consecutive awaited calls." And the consequence is not "none": if another admin's `removeMember()` (0114) revokes this user's own `company_members` row anywhere in that window, RLS's own `using (is_company_member(company_id))` (0001, re-evaluated against the OLD row) on the final delete silently matches zero rows - but by that point every one of this person's real CV files, generated CVs and registration certificates has ALREADY been permanently destroyed from storage, unconditionally, while the `people` row (and everything that would have cascaded with it) survives, now with every `storage_path` column on its cascading rows pointing at nothing. This is the same shape as every other instance this bug class has already fixed (destructive storage removal unconditional on a write that might not have matched), just with the write at the END of the function instead of in the middle of it - arguably the single widest window of any instance found in this entire bug class to date, not the narrowest.

**Fixed by reordering, not by adding a check in place**: the person row's own delete now runs FIRST (right after gathering every storage path - itself all read-only, so safe to do in any order), gated by `.select("id").maybeSingle()`, and ALL storage removal (both buckets) is deferred until that delete is confirmed to have actually matched a row. This fully closes the window rather than narrowing it - once the delete is confirmed, the two storage removals are now best-effort cleanup (logged on failure, not blocking the user-facing success) rather than a precondition for a user-facing "deleted" message, since the real, irreversible delete has by then genuinely happened.

**Two more real instances in the same file, found as part of the same end-to-end read**:
- `deleteProject()` checked **nothing at all** on its own delete - not even `error` (the exact "worst instance" shape `deleteExperience()` had before `7434ddb`'s own fix). No destructive consequence (projects carry no storage file), so this only needed an `error` check added, not the full rows-matched gate.
- `savePerson()`'s edit path (`id` present) was an unswept "plain update twin" - `supabase.from("people").update(row).eq("id", id)` checked only `error`, no destructive consequence, but a real silent-false-success, same category `saveProperty()`/`savePrincipal()` already got fixed for in `7434ddb`.

**`company/actions.ts`**: `updateCompanyProfile()` was the same kind of unswept plain-update twin - `supabase.from("companies").update(update).eq("id", companyId)` checked only `error`, sitting in the same file as this function's own already-fixed sibling `uploadVaultDocument()`, never itself read for this bug class until this pass.

**`company/document-scan/actions.ts`**: `discardOnboardingDocument()` had the FULL destructive shape - `supabase.from("onboarding_document_results").update({review_status: "discarded"}).eq("id", result.id)` checked **nothing at all**, then an unconditional `storage.remove([upload.storage_path])` regardless. A membership-revoked-mid-request race there destroyed the file while the result row stayed stuck on `review_status: "pending_review"` with nothing left to review - a genuine sibling of this same file's already-fixed `confirmVaultDocument()`/`confirmIdDocument()`, never swept before this pass.

**Lower-severity siblings in the same two files, noted but deliberately NOT fixed this pass** (no destructive consequence in any of these - a proportionality judgment call, consistent with how prior passes have handled this exact tier): `people/actions.ts`'s `retryCvExtraction()`, `discardCvExtraction()` and `deleteSignatoryScope()` (each checks `error` but not rows-matched, or vice versa, no file involved); `document-scan/actions.ts`'s `skipOnboardingDocument()` and `retryOnboardingUpload()` (same shape, no file involved), and that file's shared `markApplied()` helper (used by all 4 `confirm*` functions, zero error checking at all, but it only ever runs AFTER the real destructive write/cleanup in its caller has already succeeded and been confirmed - its own failure risks a stuck "pending_review" bookkeeping row, not data loss, since `pending_review` is also protected by `loadPendingResult()`'s own `review_status !== "pending_review"` guard against double-application). Flagging all of these explicitly rather than leaving them for a future pass to rediscover from scratch.

**Two suggested angles checked, both genuinely clean** (built a real scratch Postgres 16 instance via `engine/security/scratch_supabase_stub.sql` + `engine/security/replay_schema.sh`, all 110 migrations through `0120`, clean replay, no error):
1. *RESTRICTIVE policies with the same "revoke from public doesn't touch anon" blind spot.* That blind spot is specific to `revoke ... from function ... from public` on a GRANT; a RESTRICTIVE policy is a completely different mechanism (it narrows what a PERMISSIVE policy already allows, it doesn't grant anything itself), so there's no equivalent gap to find - confirmed by reading every RESTRICTIVE policy in the schema (`0032`, `0077`, `0117`, `0118`): every one is scoped `to authenticated`, same as every PERMISSIVE policy.
2. *Leftover table-level `anon` grants independent of RLS.* Queried `pg_policies` directly against the replayed schema: every single policy in the schema (exactly as `0120`'s own entry already found for functions) is scoped `to {authenticated}` - zero target `anon`/`public`. Queried `pg_class.relrowsecurity` for every one of the 67 real tables in `public`: **all 67 have RLS enabled**, none missing it (ruling out the much worse "no RLS at all, so the default-privilege table grant is the only thing governing the table" shape). Grepped every migration for a table-level `revoke ... from public` (as opposed to the function-level pattern 0120 fixed): found exactly 3 (`0022`, `0042`, `0043`), and all 3 already correctly name `anon` directly (`revoke ... from authenticated, anon`), not the bare `from public` shape that has the blind spot - so this angle, unlike the function one, was never actually broken. Also checked the schema's two views (`company_ownership_breakdown`, `tender_engine_jobs`) for the classic "a view silently runs as its owner, bypassing the querying role's RLS" PG<15 gotcha - both already carry `security_invoker=true` (confirmed via `pg_class.reloptions`), so this is clean too. No code change from this part of the pass.

**The actual finding, a fresh angle entirely - the DELETE-path sibling of a fix never got made.** Looking for the next storage-file-deletion Server Action not yet covered by the "silent-false-success + destructive-storage-delete" bug class (23b43b4, 7345243, 0a3ac73's own chain), grepped every `app/app/**/actions.ts` for `storage.remove(`-adjacent code and found two files not yet checked (`app/tenders/new/actions.ts`, `app/people/actions.ts` - both read in full, both genuinely clean: all their `.update()`/`.delete()` calls either go through an RPC that raises a real error on an RLS mismatch, or are already gated by an up-front existence check with no later race window of consequence). But reading the ALREADY-FIXED files again, end to end rather than just at the fixed function, turned up the real gap: `company/properties/actions.ts`'s `savePropertyDocument()` was fixed by `7345243`, but its own sibling `deleteProperty()` - same file - reads the building's own documents' storage paths BEFORE deleting the `company_properties` row, then unconditionally removes those files from storage with no gate on whether the delete actually matched a row; same shape, same file, same pass's own fix just never reached it. The identical oversight recurred in 3 more files: `company/principals/actions.ts` (`uploadPrincipalDocument()` fixed by `0a3ac73`, `deletePrincipal()` - same file - never touched), `company/registrations/actions.ts` (`saveHeldRegistration()` fixed by `23b43b4` itself, `deleteHeldRegistration()` - same file - never touched), `experience/actions.ts` (`saveExperienceTags()` fixed by `0a3ac73`, `deleteExperience()` - same file - never touched, and worse: it didn't even check `error` on the delete at all). All 4 share the exact mechanics first documented in `7345243`'s own entry: PostgREST returns a 2xx with `error: null` and zero rows affected when RLS's own tenant-isolation `using` clause (re-evaluated against the OLD row) no longer matches - e.g. this user's own `company_members` row being removed by another admin's `removeMember()` (0114) between an earlier read in the same action and the delete - indistinguishable from a real delete by `error` alone. Pre-fix, each of the 4 goes on to destroy the row's real, still-referenced file(s) from storage regardless, while the page reports "removed" for a row that was never actually deleted.

Also found their plain UPDATE-path twins still missing the same check, never fixed because no prior pass's commit mentions them: `saveProperty()` (company/properties/actions.ts) and `savePrincipal()` (company/principals/actions.ts) both do `.update(row).eq("id", id)` with no `.select()` - no destructive consequence (no file read before them), but still a real silent-false-success ("saved" shown when nothing was written).

**A 5th file nobody had swept at all: `company/bank-accounts/actions.ts`.** Not in the list of files already covered by any prior pass. Both `saveBankAccount()`'s edit branch and `deleteBankAccount()` had the exact same `.update()`/`.delete()`-checks-only-`error` shape, gated by this table's own RLS (`using (tt_is_company_admin(company_id))` - owners/admins only, 0050). No storage file involved here (bank accounts have no attachment), so the consequence is "purely" the silent-false-success itself - an edit or a deletion silently does nothing while the page reports it saved/removed, if the signed-in user's own owner/admin role was changed or removed between page load and submit. **Reproduced directly against a real scratch Postgres 16 instance** before writing any fix (not assumed): created an admin `company_members` row, a `bank_accounts` row, then deleted the `company_members` row (simulating the exact race) and ran the identical `update ... where id = ...` PostgREST issues - result: `UPDATE 0`, no error, same confirmed shape as every prior pass's own repro.

**Fixed all 6 (4 files' delete siblings + their 2 plain-update twins, plus bank-accounts' own save+delete)** with the same established pattern: chain `.select("id").maybeSingle()` onto the write, gate any subsequent destructive storage removal on the returned `data` (not just `error`), and show "no longer there - refresh and try again" instead of a false "saved"/"removed" on a zero-row match:
- `app/app/company/properties/actions.ts` - `saveProperty()`, `deleteProperty()`
- `app/app/company/principals/actions.ts` - `savePrincipal()`, `deletePrincipal()`
- `app/app/company/registrations/actions.ts` - `deleteHeldRegistration()`
- `app/app/experience/actions.ts` - `deleteExperience()` (also added the missing `error` check it never had)
- `app/app/company/bank-accounts/actions.ts` - `saveBankAccount()`, `deleteBankAccount()`

**Verified, each with a new mocked Server Action test mirroring the established convention** (real exported action called unmodified, a sequential per-`.from()` response queue simulating PostgREST's real `{error: null, data: null}` zero-match behaviour) - 14 new tests across 5 spec files (4 existing files extended, 1 new file for bank-accounts, which had none): `app/app/company/properties/actions.spec.ts`, `app/app/company/principals/actions.spec.ts`, `app/app/company/registrations/actions.spec.ts`, `app/app/experience/actions.spec.ts`, `app/app/company/bank-accounts/actions.spec.ts` (new). Each pair (membership-revoked-mid-request / real-match-still-succeeds) reproduces the pre-fix bug red, then confirms green against the actual fixed code - not a reimplementation.

**Incidental finding while running the required full QA sweep**: `app/lib/dates.test.ts`'s `closingCountdown: more than 7 days away is not urgent` test is genuinely flaky (confirmed by running it standalone 3x: failed once, passed twice) - `closingCountdown()` itself is correct (deliberately floors to whole hours, never rounds up, so a closing-deadline countdown can't overstate time remaining); the test computes `future` as exactly `Date.now() + 10*24h` and asserts on it a moment later, so any nonzero elapsed time between those two lines pushes the real remaining duration fractionally under 10 days, flooring to "9 days 23 hours". The adjacent "days and hours both shown" test already pads itself by one extra minute for the identical reason; this one didn't. Fixed by padding it the same way. Confirmed stable across 5 repeated standalone runs after the fix, 0 failures.

**Verified with the full suite, from `app/`**: `npx tsc --noEmit` - **0 errors**. `npx eslint .` - **0 errors, 3 warnings** (the same pre-existing `Logo.tsx`/`analytics/page.tsx` warnings every recent entry documents, unchanged). `npx vitest run` - **403/403 passed, 51/51 files** (up from the `0120`-pass baseline of 389/389, 50/50 - the 14 new tests above plus 1 new spec file, zero regressions elsewhere). The separate `node --experimental-strip-types --test` suite over every `*.test.ts` file - **238/238 passed, 27/27 files** (same file/test count as the baseline - the `dates.test.ts` fix only changed one existing test's own setup, added none - re-ran it specifically 5x standalone post-fix with 0 failures, confirming the flake is actually closed, not just not-hit-this-run).

**Backlog: 19, unchanged** - this pass's own findings are fixed outright (narrowly scoped `app/` TypeScript + one test fixture, each verified red-then-green), not added as new numbered items. None of the 4 standing judgment-call items were touched. No new migration - this pass touched no SQL at all, so the "4 pending migrations awaiting Sarel's own application to production" count is unchanged.

Committed and pushed directly to `main` (small, well-verified, strictly-additive correctness fixes to Server Actions plus one test-fixture fix - no RLS/grant/schema change, no PR needed per the standing guardrail):

Not fixed this pass: the window is narrower by orders of magnitude than every instance actually fixed above (those span an entire page-load-to-form-submit interaction; this one spans two consecutive awaited calls), so the cost/benefit didn't justify scope-creeping into a 6th file this pass. ## This pass (2026-11-06, standing solution-architect review): continued `fdf51d7`'s own "other anon-granted SECURITY DEFINER functions" suggestion - found the explicit-grant angle already fully covered, but a different, broader mechanism behind it was not: ~46 functions' `revoke all ... from public` (the near-universal pattern across 0003-0115) never actually removed `anon`'s own execute privilege, because this project's roles are provisioned the real-Supabase way (a direct, named-role default-privilege grant to `anon`/`authenticated`/`service_role`, separate from and untouched by revoking the generic `public` pseudo-role); fixed with a new migration revoking `anon` explicitly for all of them, verified red-then-green against a real scratch Postgres 16 instance for the privilege change AND a functional sample, confirmed zero regression for `authenticated` (grant-level and business-logic-level), pushed to `main` as a new migration awaiting Sarel's own application to production, same batch as `0117`-`0119`

**Context for whoever picks this up next, restated, unchanged**: migrations `0117`-`0119` were already on `main` but not yet applied to production; this pass adds a fourth, `0120`, to that same pending batch (SQL-only, also not yet applied). PR `#176` is still open, independently verified, still awaiting Sarel's own explicit go-ahead - not touched, not re-reviewed, not changed in scope by this pass. The 4 standing judgment-call items (`start_payfast_checkout()`'s revenue-before-ITN gap, the impersonation session-refresh gap in `app/proxy.ts`, `held_registrations`-vs-CV display format, the zero-recipients batched-send sub-case) remain exactly as described in prior entries - not touched, not resolved. `start_payfast_checkout()` specifically is discussed below (it DID match this pass's own bug pattern) and was deliberately left out of the fix so this grant-table cleanup can't be read as touching that open judgment call.

Oriented from `fdf51d7` (own immediately-preceding pass, independently re-verified by the orchestrating session before this pass started - not re-verified again here, per instruction). `git fetch origin main && git merge --ff-only` confirmed clean both before starting and again immediately before this commit - `HEAD` was still a direct ancestor of `origin/main` with zero divergence, no sibling-session work landed mid-pass. Open PRs re-checked via `gh api repos/.../pulls?state=open`: exactly three - `#164`/`#165` (draft, stale, untouched) and `#176` (open, not draft, not merged, left exactly as is).

**Angle chosen**: the orchestrator's own directive explicitly named this as "a promising, not-yet-fully-swept variant" of `fdf51d7`'s angle - other `SECURITY DEFINER` functions that are `anon`-granted without a genuine `anon` caller. Grepping migrations for literal `grant execute ... to anon` found only the 11 lines already known and accounted for in `fdf51d7`'s own entry (`apply_payfast_itn`, `signups_enabled`, `claim_notification`, `record_notification_sent`, `lifecycle_unsubscribe_token_for`, `unsubscribe_lifecycle_email`, `record_deadline_reminder_sent` x2, `invite_preview` - the 4 already fixed by `0119` plus the 4 already-confirmed-genuine callers, `lifecycle_unsubscribe_token_for` already `service_role`-only since `0108`) - that literal angle really is exhausted, exactly as the directive guessed it might be.

Rather than stop there, re-read the question as "which functions actually END UP anon-executable in the live schema, by ANY mechanism" rather than "which migrations say the word `anon`" - because a SECURITY DEFINER function's privileges aren't fully described by what a migration's own `grant`/`revoke` lines say; Postgres's own default behaviour matters too. Built a real scratch Postgres 16 instance (reusing this session's own `engine/security/scratch_supabase_stub.sql`, a prior pass's own tenant-isolation-test harness, which deliberately replicates the real Supabase platform's own role/default-privilege setup, not a bare vanilla Postgres), replayed all 109 real migration files verbatim in order (clean, no manual fixture, no error), then queried `has_function_privilege('anon', <oid>, 'EXECUTE')` directly against the resulting catalog for every `security definer` function in `public` (56 total, minus pure trigger functions, which PostgREST can never expose as an RPC call regardless of grants).

**The finding**: 52 non-trigger `security definer` functions came back `anon`-executable in the real, current schema (pre-`0120`) - not 8 (the literal-`anon`-grep count), not the ~11 either. Root cause, confirmed by reading `engine/security/scratch_supabase_stub.sql`'s own header (itself documenting a prior pass's own hard-won 2026-10-17/18 lesson) and then reproducing it directly: this project's Postgres roles carry `alter default privileges in schema public grant all on functions to anon, authenticated, service_role` - a DIRECT, NAMED-role grant to `anon` applied automatically to every function at creation time, completely separate from and untouched by the generic `public`-pseudo-role default every vanilla Postgres function also gets. The near-universal migration convention (`revoke all on function X from public; grant execute on function X to authenticated;`, used in essentially every migration from `0003` onward) only ever undoes the SECOND, generic grant - it has never actually removed `anon`'s own direct one. The handful of migrations that DO work correctly (`0055`, `0089`, `0094`/`0095`, `0099`, `0108`, and now `0119`) all happen to spell it `revoke all ... from public, anon` (or a separate explicit `revoke ... from anon`) - confirmed by grepping for the literal string `from anon` across every migration and finding exactly those files, nothing else.

**Not a live, exploitable vulnerability on its own** (checked individually, not assumed, via `pg_get_functiondef()` read for every one of the 52, then verified by direct `set role anon` calls against the scratch database): 4 are the genuine, already-known anon callers (`apply_payfast_itn`, `invite_preview`, `signups_enabled`, `unsubscribe_lifecycle_email` - untouched); `start_payfast_checkout` also matched the bug pattern but was deliberately excluded from the fix below, specifically so this cleanup can't be read as touching its own still-open revenue-integrity judgment call; of the remaining 47, 3 (`tt_pack_company`, `tt_person_in_company`, `tt_tender_visible_to`, 0043) are bare id-to-id relationship booleans never used inside an anon-facing RLS policy (grepped every `create policy` in the schema - every one of the 157 is scoped `to authenticated`, zero target `anon`/`public`), so a direct anon call only confirms "does this id pair exist" with no sensitive payload - the same low-severity calibration Findings 109/110 already used for a sibling case. The other 44 each carry their own internal `auth.uid()`-derived gate (`is_company_member()`/`is_platform_admin()`/`is_employee_in_company()`, an explicit `if not is_platform_admin() then raise exception ... 42501` guard, or an equivalent WHERE-clause filter) that already independently blocks a real `anon` caller today, confirmed directly: `set role anon; select is_platform_admin()` returned `f` (not an error), `select * from platform_admin_companies()` returned 0 rows, `select bank_account_summaries(<any id>)` returned 0 rows - every one already silently inert for `anon`, by the function's own logic, with the grant table never actually being the thing stopping it. This is why the fix below is framed as hardening/defense-in-depth, not a vulnerability patch: it closes a door whose lock was already holding, so nothing a real caller does changes, but a future change that ever weakens one of those internal checks without anyone re-auditing the (misleadingly-already-"revoked") grant table would otherwise land live immediately instead of being caught.

Two functions - `is_company_member()` (0001) and `tt_is_company_admin()` (0050) - turned out to have an even more basic gap than the rest: neither had EVER carried any `revoke`/`grant` statement at all (both pre-date the `revoke all from public` convention), so each still also carried the plain generic `public`-pseudo-role default on top of the named `anon` grant (confirmed via `unnest(proacl)` showing a bare `=X/<owner>` ACL entry - the tell for an un-revoked `public` grant). Both are pure `auth.uid()`-gated booleans (always `false` for `anon`, which has no `auth.uid()` at all) - inert either way - but fixed with `revoke all ... from public, anon` instead of a plain `revoke execute ... from anon`, closing both gaps at once.

**Reproduced directly against the real scratch Postgres 16 instance, red-then-green** (dropped and rebuilt the `auth`/`storage`/`public` schemas from a clean slate first, to rule out stale state from an earlier attempt in the same run): **RED** - pre-`0120`, 52 functions anon-executable (counted via the same query above); `set role anon; select is_platform_admin()` and `select * from platform_admin_companies()` both executed with no `insufficient_privilege`/`permission denied` error (returning `f` / 0 rows respectively - confirming the grant was real, even though the business logic already masked its effect). Applied the real `0120` migration file itself (not a hand-copied fragment) - **GREEN** - anon-executable count dropped to exactly 5 (the 4 genuine callers + the deliberately-excluded `start_payfast_checkout`); the identical `set role anon` calls for `is_platform_admin()`, `platform_admin_companies()`, and `is_company_member(...)` now all raise `permission denied for function ...` (Postgres's own phrasing for `insufficient_privilege`/42501); `set role authenticated` (with a dummy `test.uid` session var the stub reads) still returns the correct business-logic result for all three - `is_platform_admin()` → `f` for a non-admin, `platform_admin_set_setting(...)` → its own `'Only a Tender Tool platform admin can do this'` 42501 raise (unchanged, business-logic-level, not a new grant-level denial), `bank_account_summaries(...)` → 0 rows for a non-member (unchanged) - confirming zero behaviour change for the one role that actually uses these. Scratch database dropped, Postgres service stopped after - also found and dropped 9 unrelated leftover scratch databases from earlier passes that were never cleaned up (`cmdcenter_test`, `narrative_check2`, `narrative_replay_check`, `phase2_replay_check`, `tenant_iso_test`, `tender_tool_replay`/`2`/`3`, `upsert_test`) - a housekeeping fix, not a code change, noted here so a future pass doesn't mistake them for live fixtures.

**Fixed** with new migration `app/supabase/migrations/0120_security_definer_functions_anon_grant_table_cleanup.sql`: 46 `revoke execute ... from anon` statements (one per function, exact signatures taken verbatim from the scratch database's own `pg_get_function_identity_arguments()` output, not hand-typed) plus 2 `revoke all ... from public, anon` statements for the two functions that never had any revoke at all, plus an updated `comment on function is_platform_admin()`. SQL-only, no JS/TS/Python file touched - deliberately excludes `start_payfast_checkout` (judgment-call item, untouched) and the 4 genuine anon callers (`apply_payfast_itn`, `invite_preview`, `signups_enabled`, `unsubscribe_lifecycle_email` - all untouched, same exclusions `0119`'s own entry already used).

**Verified with the full suite** (no app code changed, so no regression possible, but run in full per the standing instruction regardless, from `app/`): `npx tsc --noEmit` - **0 errors**. `npx eslint .` - **0 errors, 3 warnings** (the same pre-existing `Logo.tsx`/`analytics/page.tsx` warnings every recent entry already documents, confirmed unchanged). `npx vitest run` - **389/389 passed, 50/50 files**, identical to the `fdf51d7` baseline. The separate `node --experimental-strip-types --test` suite over every `*.test.ts` file (27 files) - **238/238 passed**, identical baseline. The migration itself was separately, actually executed against real Postgres as described above, not just parsed.

**Security/grant-table-shaped, but explicitly a hardening/defense-in-depth fix, not a vulnerability patch** - re-stated for anyone skimming: every one of the 46 (really 47, counting `start_payfast_checkout` left alone on purpose) functions already had its own independent, working protection against a real `anon` caller; this migration only removes a redundant, misleadingly-labelled grant that the schema's own comments (`revoke all ... from public` right above a function explicitly commented "Platform-admin only") already show the author intended to remove and believed they had. No role or tenant boundary was loosened - strictly narrower than before, same shape as `0119`.

**Backlog: 19, unchanged** - this pass's own finding is fixed outright (SQL-only, narrowly scoped, verified against real Postgres), not added as a new numbered item. The "pending migrations awaiting Sarel's application to production" item now covers **4** migrations: `0117`, `0118`, `0119`, `0120` - same item, updated count. None of the 4 standing judgment-call items were touched; `start_payfast_checkout()`'s own revenue-integrity gap specifically was read again in the course of this pass (to confirm it matched the grant-table bug pattern) but its underlying payment-timing logic was not touched, and it was deliberately left OUT of this pass's own fix for that reason - restated, not resolved.

Committed and pushed directly to `main` (SQL-only, strictly narrowing, well-verified - same standing convention as `0108`/`0119`):
- `app/supabase/migrations/0120_security_definer_functions_anon_grant_table_cleanup.sql` (new)
- `docs/specs/System-Status.md`

`git status --short` confirmed clean before and after (only the new migration file and this doc).

To verify independently: apply `engine/security/scratch_supabase_stub.sql` to a fresh Postgres 16 database, replay every file in `app/supabase/migrations/` in filename order through `0119` (current `main`, pre-`0120`), then run `select count(*) from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid=p.pronamespace where n.nspname='public' and p.prosecdef and p.prorettype != 'trigger'::regtype and has_function_privilege('anon', p.oid, 'EXECUTE');` - expect `52`. Apply `0120`, re-run the identical query - expect `5` (`apply_payfast_itn`, `invite_preview`, `signups_enabled`, `start_payfast_checkout`, `unsubscribe_lifecycle_email`).

## This pass (2026-11-06, standing solution-architect review): a fresh angle - security-adjacent but NOT PR `#176`'s class - the notification engine's own `claim_notification()`/`record_notification_sent()`/`record_deadline_reminder_sent()`/`record_operational_alert_sent()` were all callable by the truly-anonymous `anon` role (the app's public key, shipped in every client bundle), letting anyone pre-claim a one-time-ever notification token and permanently, silently suppress a real future send - most concretely, `scripts/send-founder-digest.ts`'s own date-only idempotency key makes the founder's own daily digest fully guessable and 100% pre-claimable with no login at all; fixed with a new migration revoking `anon` (keeping `authenticated`, the one genuine webapp caller), verified red-then-green against a real scratch Postgres 16 instance, pushed to `main` as a new migration awaiting Sarel's own application to production, same as `0117`/`0118`

**Context for whoever picks this up next, restated, unchanged**: migrations `0117`/`0118` (employee-RLS fixes) are both on `main` but **still NOT applied to the live production database**; this pass adds a third, `0119`, to that same pending batch (see below - also SQL-only, also not yet applied). PR `#176` (the 12-function `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC employee-RLS-bypass class) is **still open, independently verified, still awaiting Sarel's own explicit go-ahead to merge** - this pass's own finding is a genuinely different vulnerability shape (anonymous-write/denial-of-service via premature token exhaustion, not an employee-vs-owner RLS bypass within a company) and does not touch, comment on, or change #176's scope in any way. The 3 standing judgment-call items (`start_payfast_checkout()`'s revenue-before-ITN gap, the impersonation session-refresh gap in `app/proxy.ts`, `held_registrations`-vs-CV display format) remain exactly as described in prior entries - not touched, not resolved. The `send-compliance-digest.ts`/`send-discovered-tenders.ts`/`send-scout-alerts.ts` zero-recipients sub-case flagged by an earlier pass is also untouched this pass - not overridden, left for Sarel or a future pass with room to restructure that batching.

Oriented from `3135a7b` (own immediately-preceding pass, independently re-verified by the orchestrating session before this pass started - not re-verified again here, per instruction). `git fetch origin main && git merge --ff-only` confirmed clean both before starting and again immediately before this commit - no sibling-session work landed mid-pass. Open PRs re-checked via the GitHub REST API (`gh api repos/.../pulls?state=open`, since `gh pr list`'s GraphQL path is blocked in this session): exactly three, as expected - `#164`/`#165` (both draft, stale, untouched) and `#176` (open, NOT draft, NOT merged, left exactly as is - re-checked again after this pass's own push, still unchanged).

**Angle chosen**: the directive's own suggestion to look at "RLS policies on any table created/altered by a migration you haven't checked yet" - but reading every table's own RLS-enablement and policy count across all 108 migrations (scripted, not sampled) found RLS enabled everywhere with no gaps; the handful of tables with zero `create policy` statements (`notification_claims`, `lifecycle_unsubscribe_tokens`, `payfast_payment_attempts`, `platform_admins`, `platform_settings`, `sent_deadline_reminders`, `sent_operational_alerts`, `tender_watch_state`) are all deliberately, explicitly documented as "enabled with zero policies so PostgREST still closes it to anon/authenticated by default" - real, intentional "service-role/SECURITY-DEFINER-function-only" tables, not a gap. That led directly to the `grant execute on function ... to anon, authenticated` statements guarding those same SECURITY DEFINER functions, which this doc's own 2026-10-31 security-audit thread (Findings 109/110, migration `0108`) had already combed once - but under a specifically different question ("does this leak another tenant's data to a caller who doesn't own it"). That same entry explicitly names the 4 functions this pass fixes and explicitly declines to flag them: *"The idempotency/logging functions granted to `anon` (`claim_notification`, `record_notification_sent`, `record_deadline_reminder_sent`, `record_operational_alert_sent`) are insert-only with no sensitive read, so an ownership check doesn't apply the same way - noted, not flagged as a new item."* Read that reasoning again against a different question - not "what can `anon` **read**" but "what can `anon` **write**, and does that write alone cause real, irreversible harm" - since `notification_claims`' own primary key is a permanent, non-renewable, one-time-ever resource (0093's own header, and this doc's own repeatedly-fixed "claim a one-time-ever token too early" bug class both depend on exactly that).

**The finding**: all 4 functions are `security definer`, all 4 were granted `execute` to `anon` **and** `authenticated` (0079/0080/0092/0093) - `anon` being PostgREST's role for a request carrying nothing but the app's own public key, which is not a secret (shipped in every client bundle by design - the same framing migration `0108`'s own header comment already uses for the sibling `lifecycle_unsubscribe_token_for()` bug it fixed). An anonymous caller doesn't need to read anything back to do real damage here: successfully **writing** a claim before the real sender ever tries to permanently and silently burns that exact future notification, by this engine's own by-design semantics ("already sent, do nothing" - this doc's whole "claim a one-time-ever token too early" bug class already establishes this is a real, serious consequence when the app's own code does it to itself; the same consequence is strictly worse when a stranger does it on purpose). Most concretely and completely reachable: `scripts/send-founder-digest.ts`'s idempotency key is `` `founder-digest-${sastDateKey}` `` - a plain ISO date string, zero UUID/secret material, 100% guessable for any future date with no reconnaissance at all. The other 3 functions' keys are UUID-keyed (company_id/tender_id) - a smaller, not-zero window (an id leaked or guessed some other way), the identical fix either way.

**Confirmed no genuine `anon`-context caller exists for any of the 4**, so revoking `anon` breaks nothing real: grepped every call site across `app/` and `engine/`. ## This pass (2026-11-06, standing solution-architect review): the "claim a one-time-ever notification token too early" bug class - already fixed once for `send-returnables-digest.ts` on 2026-10-30 - turned up in 4 more call sites across 2 scripts, missed because the prior sweep grepped only for `claim_notification` callers and these use sibling RPCs (`record_deadline_reminder_sent`, `record_operational_alert_sent`); fixed all 4, with new regression tests, red-then-green

**Context for whoever picks this up next, restated, unchanged**: migrations `0117`/`0118` (employee-RLS fixes) are both on `main` but **still NOT applied to the live production database**; PR `#176` (the 12-function `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC employee-RLS-bypass class) is **still open, independently verified, still awaiting Sarel's own explicit go-ahead to merge**. This pass's own task was explicitly told to stay off both of those (the orchestrator's own open review queue, not something for this pass to add to) - **`0117`/`0118` remain pending Sarel's application to production; PR `#176` remains open, unmerged, and untouched by this pass** - not reviewed, not commented on, not merged.

Oriented from `091e884` (own immediately-preceding pass). `git fetch origin main && git merge --ff-only` confirmed clean - already at `091e884`, no new commits from any sibling session, no collision (re-checked again immediately before this entry's own commit - still clean). Open PRs re-checked via the GitHub REST API (`gh api repos/.../pulls?state=open`, since `gh pr list`'s GraphQL path is blocked in this session): exactly three, as expected - `#164`/`#165` (both draft, stale, untouched) and `#176` (open, NOT draft, NOT merged - left exactly as is).

**Angle chosen**: the directive's own suggestion to look for this exact bug class (unguarded write + an irreversible consequence that proceeds regardless) OUTSIDE `app/app/**/actions.ts`, with a genuinely different trigger condition than the already-exhausted RLS membership race. Read every `app/lib/*.ts` helper actually called from a Server Action for a storage-delete-after-unchecked-update shape first (none - the one real `.update(` outside `actions.ts`, `lib/pipeline.ts`'s `advanceFoundToAssessing()`, is an explicitly-documented best-effort call with no downstream consequence either way). Then read every `app/scripts/send-*.ts` cron sender under the service-role key, since RLS doesn't apply there at all - a different mechanism would have to produce the same shape. Found one: every notification-claim RPC in this engine (`claim_notification`, `record_deadline_reminder_sent`, `record_operational_alert_sent`) is an explicit one-time-ever token (migration `0093`'s own header comment, `record_deadline_reminder_sent`'s unique constraint) - claiming it and then never actually sending (for ANY reason) permanently and silently loses that exact notification, even once the reason it couldn't send is later resolved.

**This is not a new bug class** - `send-returnables-digest.ts` was fixed for exactly this shape on 2026-10-30 (claiming before `operationalRecipients()`/render, both of which can fail), and that pass explicitly swept "every other caller of `claim_notification`" looking for the same thing, correctly leaving `send-compliance-digest.ts`/`send-discovered-tenders.ts`/`send-scout-alerts.ts` alone as a documented, batched-send tradeoff (see below for why I didn't re-open that specific call). **But that sweep's own search term - `claim_notification` - never would have found `scripts/send-deadline-reminders.ts` or `scripts/send-operational-alerts.ts`**: both claim through a different, sibling one-time-claim RPC (`record_deadline_reminder_sent`, `record_operational_alert_sent` - the same "insert with a unique constraint, catch the violation" shape, just not literally named `claim_notification`), so a literal grep for that one name skips them entirely. Read both files in full regardless of that prior "not touched" note, since the directive's own angle doesn't stop at a function name.

**The finding - 4 instances, all genuinely reachable, none batched (so none of the prior pass's "claim-many-before-a-batched-send" reasoning applies)**:
- `scripts/send-deadline-reminders.ts`'s main loop: claimed `record_deadline_reminder_sent` BEFORE calling `criticalBidRecipients()` and checking `recipients.length === 0` (the existing `skippedNoMembers` counter proves this branch is genuinely hit in practice, not theoretical). A company with zero registered members at the exact moment this cron runs permanently loses that tender's one 3-day/24-hour closing-deadline reminder for good, even after a member is added before the tender actually closes.
- `scripts/send-operational-alerts.ts`'s `runPrintCutoff()`, `runBriefingReminders()`, `runClarificationWindow()` - all three claim `record_operational_alert_sent` BEFORE `operationalRecipients()` (via the shared `claim()` helper, called first in every one of the three loops). Identical consequence for the 48-hour print/transit cutoff, the briefing countdown, and the clarification-window-expiry alert respectively - each a one-shot-per-threshold token, same as `record_deadline_reminder_sent`.
- (Checked in `runPrintCutoff()` while reading it: a second `if (!deadline) continue;` sits after the claim too, but `printSignDeadline()` is called with the exact same inputs `printCutoffCandidates()` already used to compute `hoursLeft` via the identical `hoursUntilPrintSignDeadline()` - which calls `printSignDeadline()` internally and returns null exactly when it's null - so a candidate that already passed `printCutoffCandidates()`'s own filter can never hit this branch. Confirmed by reading both functions side by side, not fixed - genuinely unreachable dead code, not a live bug.)

**Did NOT re-open `send-compliance-digest.ts`/`send-discovered-tenders.ts`/`send-scout-alerts.ts`** (the three the 2026-10-30 pass explicitly checked and left alone). `send-scout-alerts.ts` checks its one recipient (`ADMIN_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL`) before any claim at all - genuinely fine, re-confirmed by reading it again. The other two DO have the identical "claim per item before the per-company recipients check" shape - re-confirmed by reading both again line by line - but I'm leaving the prior pass's documented "deliberate batched-send tradeoff" verdict as it stands rather than overriding it myself: unlike the two non-batched scripts above, fixing these two properly means restructuring the claim to happen AFTER grouping-by-company (claim each item in a company's own batch only once that company's recipient list is known to be non-empty), which is a materially bigger, batching-semantics-sensitive change than a two-line reorder, and a predecessor already looked at this exact question and reasoned about it explicitly. **Flagged honestly rather than silently dropped**: the stated rationale ("claiming early is deliberate... even if that batch's send later fails") describes a send that is attempted and fails, which is a different event from zero recipients meaning no send is ever attempted at all (no `notification_logs` row either way) - I think the zero-recipients sub-case specifically doesn't actually need the early claim the batching tradeoff justifies, but I'm not confident enough to override a predecessor's explicit, reasoned call on a non-security judgment question without discussing it, and it isn't the kind of unambiguous, mechanically-missed bug (wrong grep term) the other 4 instances are. Left for Sarel's own judgment call or a future pass with more room to restructure the batching carefully - not added to the numbered backlog (same "flagged inline" convention this doc already uses for similarly thin, contestable leads), not fixed.

**Reproduced directly against the real exported functions, red-then-green, not assumed**: both files' core per-candidate logic wasn't previously testable (no export, `main()` invoked unconditionally at module load) - the established project convention, confirmed by reading this doc's own 2026-10-30 entry, is that no `app/scripts/*.ts` file has ever had dedicated test coverage ("a standalone script needing a live Supabase client is heavier to unit-test"). Rather than accept that gap again for a bug this clear-cut and this mechanical to reproduce, split each file's per-candidate loop into an exported, directly-testable function (`processDeadlineReminderCandidates()` in `send-deadline-reminders.ts`; `runPrintCutoff()`/`runBriefingReminders()`/`runClarificationWindow()` in `send-operational-alerts.ts` were already separate functions, just not exported) and guarded each file's top-level `main()` call behind `import.meta.url === \`file://${process.argv[1]}\`` so importing the function for a test no longer also fires a real (doomed, since test env vars aren't real credentials) network call and `process.exit(1)` - verified this guard doesn't change the real CLI behaviour by running both scripts directly with no env vars set and confirming the identical "must both be set" exit-1 message as before. New `app/scripts/send-deadline-reminders.spec.ts` (3 tests) and `app/scripts/send-operational-alerts.spec.ts` (6 tests) use the same sequential/keyed-response Supabase mock technique the `actions.ts` passes already established, adapted for `.rpc()` calls by name and a minimal thenable/chainable `.from()` stub. **Not security/RLS-shaped** - these scripts run under the Supabase SERVICE ROLE key, so RLS plays no role in this bug at all; the trigger is purely "zero opted-in/registered recipients at the moment the cron fires" (a company mid-onboarding, or one where every member has opted out), exactly the different, non-RLS trigger condition the directive's own angle asked for. If the race hits (same `remove_member_checked()` mechanism, on "companies: members can update" or "company_principals: tenant isolation"), the just-copied destination file is orphaned AND the source file is destroyed outright - and since `markApplied()`'s own trailing update hits the identical race, the `onboarding_document_results` row is left stuck on `review_status = "pending_review"`, which implies to the UI that the source file is still there to act on. **Reproduced directly against the real exported functions**, not assumed, using the established sequential-response-mock technique (`23b43b4`'s own convention, extended this pass with a `storage.from().download()` mock for `copyBetweenBuckets()`'s own real network read): for all three files, with the relevant table's own update queued to return `{data: null, error: null}` (RLS's own real zero-row-match response) - confirmed in every case the action redirected with a false "saved"/"filed" URL pre-fix, and that the destructive storage removal happened regardless. Then, simulating the exact race (`DELETE FROM company_members ...` between the row's creation and the upsert, same mechanism as every other instance in this doc), ran the identical `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (company_id, document_type) DO UPDATE SET ...` statement PostgREST's `.upsert(row, {onConflict: "company_id,document_type"})` issues. **Result: a real, loud error** - `ERROR: 42501: new row violates row-level security policy for table "company_document_templates"`, raised at `ExecWithCheckOptions` (Postgres's own `WITH CHECK` enforcement, not a silent zero-row success).
