## This pass (2026-11-06, standing solution-architect review): extended `23b43b4`'s own bug class to two more files - `app/company/actions.ts`'s `uploadVaultDocument()` and `app/company/properties/actions.ts`'s `savePropertyDocument()` both silently reported success AND destructively deleted the still-referenced previous file on a membership-revoked-mid-request race; both fixed, each verified red-then-green with a new mocked Server Action test, pushed to `main`

**Context for whoever picks this up next, restated, unchanged**: migrations `0117`/`0118` (employee-RLS fixes) are both on `main` but **still NOT applied to the live production database**; PR `#176` (the 12-function `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC employee-RLS-bypass class) is **still open, independently verified, still awaiting Sarel's own explicit go-ahead to merge**. This pass's own task was explicitly told to stay off both of those (the orchestrator's own open review queue, not something for this pass to add to) - **`0117`/`0118` remain pending Sarel's application to production; PR `#176` remains open, unmerged, and untouched by this pass** - not reviewed, not commented on, not merged. `app/app/admin/actions.ts` also remains deliberately uninvestigated past where an earlier pass left it (security-adjacent to `#176`'s own class) - not picked up this pass either.

Oriented from `23b43b4` (own immediately-preceding pass: the `saveHeldRegistration()` orphan-upload fix). `git fetch origin main && git merge --ff-only` confirmed clean - already at `23b43b4`, no new commits from any sibling session, no collision. Open PRs re-checked via the GitHub REST API (`gh api repos/.../pulls`, since `gh pr list`'s GraphQL path is blocked in this session): exactly three, as expected - `#164`/`#165` (both draft, untouched) and `#176` (open, NOT draft, NOT merged - left exactly as is; re-checked again after this pass's own push, still unchanged).

**Picked the directive's own "any other Server Action with an `.update(...).eq(\"id\", ...)` pattern that doesn't check for a zero-row match before continuing to do something consequential" angle directly**, rather than re-litigating the 3 already-flagged files (`deleteHeldRegistration()`, `savePrincipal()`, `saveProperty()` - each re-confirmed by the prior pass to genuinely lack a file-upload/resource-leak consequence, not re-checked again here since nothing about them has changed). Grepped every `app/app/**/actions.ts` for `.update(...).eq("id", ...)` call sites (22 files) and read each hit's surrounding code for the specific shape that made `23b43b4` real: an update checked only by `error`, with a file-storage write (upload and/or delete) downstream of it in the same action.

**The finding - two genuinely fresh instances of the same bug class, both worse than `23b43b4`'s own**: both are in document-upload actions with a "swap the old file for the new one" step, and in both, the final storage cleanup of the *previous* file has no gate on the update having actually matched a row:
- `app/company/actions.ts`'s `uploadVaultDocument()` (vault compliance documents - COID, CIDB, SARS TCS PIN, PI insurance, ISO 9001, bank letter, B-BBEE proof): reads the company's current document path, uploads the new file to storage, then `supabase.from("companies").update({[column]: storagePath}).eq("id", companyId)` checking only `error`, then **unconditionally** `if (previousPath) remove([previousPath])`. "companies: members can update" (0001) is `for update ... using (is_company_member(id))` - re-evaluated against the OLD row, USING only. The realistic trigger: another admin calling `removeMember()` (`remove_member_checked()`, 0114, a real, already-shipped RPC that deletes another user's `company_members` row) on this same signed-in user while their vault-upload form is mid-submit. Confirmed, not assumed, by reading `remove_member_checked()` directly - it's a real deletion, not a soft toggle.
- `app/company/properties/actions.ts`'s `savePropertyDocument()` (per-building lease documents - title deed, owner mandate, zoning/fire/electrical CoC, SAPOA grading, etc., 0050): identical shape - `existing` document row read, new file uploaded, then `supabase.from("property_documents").update(row).eq("id", existing.id)` checking only `error`, then unconditional previous-file removal. "property_documents: tenant isolation" (0050) is the same `using (is_company_member(company_id))`, USING-only-on-the-old-row shape. This is a genuinely different function from `saveProperty()` (the building's own row, line 47 of the same file) - the one the prior pass already read and correctly judged to lack this consequence (it has no inline file upload); `savePropertyDocument()` (line 111) is the file-upload sibling the prior pass's own note didn't cover. Noted but deliberately NOT pursued further: `property_documents`/`company_properties` also carry a `0077` *restrictive* "employee has no access" policy (`is_employee_in_company`) - the same migration series as the open `0117`/`0118`/`#176` employee-RLS work. Confirmed this fix's own trigger (a company_members row disappearing via `removeMember()`) is unrelated to that restrictive policy or to any bypass of it - the bug is the same plain tenant-isolation USING-clause race as `23b43b4`'s and `uploadVaultDocument()`'s, not anything about employee access - but called out explicitly here in case a future pass sees it differently.

**Consequence - worse than `23b43b4`'s own finding**: that fix's bug only orphaned a newly-uploaded file. Here, because the *previous*-file removal is unconditional rather than gated on the update's own success, a zero-row-match update leaves the newly uploaded file orphaned **AND** actively deletes the previous file from storage - a file the row still references (the update never actually changed it) - destroying the company's/building's own still-valid, previously-saved document while the UI reports "Document saved".

**Reproduced directly against the real exported functions**, not assumed, using the sequential-response-mock technique `23b43b4` introduced (no reimplementation of either function's logic): for `uploadVaultDocument()`, pre-fix, with the `companies` update queued to return `{data: null, error: null}` (RLS's own real zero-row-match response) - confirmed the action redirected with `saved=doc` (false success), the new upload was never cleaned up, and the previous file WAS removed (`removeCalls` held exactly the old path, not the new one). For `savePropertyDocument()`, same mock shape against the real `property_documents` update - same three-part confirmation: false `saved=doc`, new upload left in `removeCalls`-untouched state, previous file removed anyway. Both reproductions exercise the real, unmodified exported action (`app/app/company/actions.ts`'s `uploadVaultDocument`, `app/app/company/properties/actions.ts`'s `savePropertyDocument`), not a reimplementation.

**Fixed** with the minimal correct change in both files, mirroring `23b43b4`'s own pattern: chained `.select("id").maybeSingle()` onto the update and check the returned data (not just `error`) before the previous-file removal can be reached - `uploadVaultDocument()` now checks `error || !updated`; `savePropertyDocument()`'s update/insert ternary was restructured into an `if (existing) {...} else {...}` (needed since only the update branch gets the new `.select()`/zero-row check; the insert branch's own RLS `with check` already raises a real error on a genuine violation, it doesn't silently no-op the way the update's `using`-only clause does) with the same `data`-null check added only to the update branch.

**Verified red-then-green for both, with two new test files** (`app/app/company/actions.spec.ts`, `app/app/company/properties/actions.spec.ts` - neither file had any test coverage before this pass): each has one test asserting the membership-revoked-mid-request race fails cleanly (no `saved=doc`, redirects with `?error=`, new upload cleaned up, previous file preserved) and one asserting a real, genuinely-matching update still saves and swaps the previous file out correctly (confirms the mock harness exercises the success path, not just the failure one). Ran both against the pre-fix file first (captured the fix as a patch, `git checkout --` the file, wrote and ran the test, then reapplied the patch) - **both failed exactly as predicted** (`uploadVaultDocument()`: redirected `saved=doc`, `removeCalls` held only the old path, not the new one; `savePropertyDocument()`: same, `saved=doc#prop-prop-1`). Reapplied each fix and reran: **both 2/2 passed**. Full `npx vitest run` from `app/`: **370/370 passed, 44/44 files** (366/42 baseline + this pass's 2 new files, 4 new tests - no regression anywhere). All 27 `*.test.ts` files (the separate `node --experimental-strip-types`-run suite) re-run directly - 0 failures, unaffected (none touch either changed file). `npx tsc --noEmit` (whole project) - 0 errors. `npx eslint` on all 4 touched/new files - clean. `git diff --stat`: `app/app/company/actions.ts` (+15/-2), `app/app/company/properties/actions.ts` (+18/-5), plus the two new spec files.

Not security/RLS-shaped - same reasoning `23b43b4` already established for this exact bug class: RLS is working exactly as designed in both cases (correctly refusing a write once the caller is no longer a member of the company the row belongs to); the bug is purely the app-level code not noticing that correctly-enforced refusal before doing something irreversible (deleting a file) on the strength of a false "it worked" read. WHERE id = ...` and moved on - the file's actual write-path correctness was never itself the subject). Read `app/company/registrations/actions.ts` (146 lines - held registrations/licences/accreditations, migration 0050) end to end against its real caller (`app/company/registrations/page.tsx`'s `HeldForm`/`HeldRow`), the same method the last two passes used successfully on Server Actions.

**The finding**: `saveHeldRegistration()`'s edit path (`id` present) does `supabase.from("held_registrations").update(row).eq("id", id)` and only checks `error`. Migration `0050`'s own `held_registrations` RLS policy is `for all ... using (is_company_member(company_id)) with check (is_company_member(company_id))` - for an `UPDATE`, Postgres evaluates `using` against the pre-update row. If `id` belongs to a row RLS doesn't match on the `using` side (because it was deleted by another tab/device in the moments between the page rendering the edit form and this submit - the only realistic way a stale id reaches this action, since the id always comes from a hidden field populated from the company's own just-fetched rows, not from anywhere a foreign company's id could get in), PostgREST's real behaviour is a 2xx response with **zero rows affected and `error: null`** - completely indistinguishable from "it matched and was updated" by looking at `error` alone. Pre-fix, the code: (1) treats this exactly like a real save and redirects with `?saved=1`, a false "Registration saved" message; (2) if a certificate file was attached, carries on regardless - the next `select("storage_path").eq("id", heldId).maybeSingle()` also returns `null` (same RLS block on the now-nonexistent row), so the existing-file cleanup check is skipped, and the code uploads the file to storage anyway at `${companyId}/registrations/${heldId}/...`; the follow-up `update({storage_path, original_filename}).eq("id", heldId)` call that's supposed to record the new path **also** silently matches zero rows (`error: null` again) - so the upload's own error-handling cleanup (`if (upErr) { ...fail... }`) never triggers, and the file is left permanently orphaned in storage with no database row ever referencing it. Confirmed `principals/actions.ts`'s own `uploadPrincipalDocument()` already guards exactly this shape correctly (`select(...).maybeSingle()` first, `if (!existing) fail(...)` before ever uploading) - this file just didn't carry the same guard onto its own edit-then-upload path.

**Reproduced directly against the real exported function**, not assumed: this repo has no existing convention for mocking `supabase-js`/Next's Server Action plumbing in a test, so wrote a small, self-contained sequential-response mock (`app/company/registrations/actions.spec.ts`, new file) that simulates PostgREST's real "zero-row match -> `{error: null, data: null}}`" behaviour precisely, mocks `@/lib/supabase/server`'s `createClient`, `next/navigation`'s `redirect` (made to throw, same as the real one, caught by the test) and `next/cache`'s `revalidatePath`, then imports and calls the real, unmodified `saveHeldRegistration()` - not a reimplementation of its logic. Against the pre-fix file: a zero-row-match update redirected with `?saved=1` (should have been an error) and, with a file attached, called `storage.upload()` regardless (should never have been reached) - both **failed exactly as predicted**. A third test (a real, matching update) passed throughout, confirming the mock harness genuinely exercises the success path and the fix doesn't regress it.

**Fixed** with the minimal correct change: chained `.select("id").maybeSingle()` onto the edit-path update and check the returned `data`, not just `error` - `if (!data) fail("That registration is no longer there - it may have been removed. Refresh and try again.", "#add")`, placed before the file-upload block so a zero-row match can never reach it. `deleteHeldRegistration()` has the same underlying shape (a delete that matches zero rows also reports `?saved=removed` either way) but with no resource-leak consequence - it's already-gone either way and nothing is uploaded afterwards - so, per the directive's own "don't force it" instruction, left unfixed and just noted here; same for the identical unguarded-update pattern in `app/company/principals/actions.ts`'s `savePrincipal()` and `app/company/properties/actions.ts`'s `saveProperty()` (both read in full while comparing against this fix's shape - neither uploads a file inline on the same action, so neither has this bug's actual consequence, just the same latent "false success message on a stale/deleted row" shape) - flagged here as a class worth a future pass's attention if it's ever seen to bite for real, not forced into a multi-file refactor for one file's genuine, consequential bug.

**Verified red-then-green**: ran the new spec against the pre-fix file first (`git stash` wasn't needed - the test was written and run before the fix was applied) - **2 of 3 tests failed exactly as predicted** (`saved=1` where an error was expected; `uploadCalls` length 1 where 0 was expected), the third (real-match) test already passed. Applied the fix and reran: **3/3 passed**. Full `npx vitest run` from `app/`: **366/366 passed, 42/42 files** (363/41 baseline + this pass's 1 new file, 3 new tests - no regression anywhere). All 27 `*.test.ts` files (the separate `node --experimental-strip-types`-run suite) re-run directly - 0 failures, unaffected (none of them touch `registrations/actions.ts`). `npx tsc --noEmit` (whole project) - 0 errors. `npx eslint app/company/registrations/actions.ts app/company/registrations/actions.spec.ts` - clean. `git diff --stat`: `app/app/company/registrations/actions.ts` (+7/-1), plus the new `app/app/company/registrations/actions.spec.ts` (+203).

Not security/RLS-shaped - RLS is working exactly as designed here (correctly refusing the write on a row the caller's company no longer has access to); the bug is purely the app-level code not noticing that correctly-enforced refusal and claiming success instead. No role or tenant boundary was touched by this fix. No new security/RLS-shaped finding was stumbled into along the way to defer either.

**Backlog: 19, unchanged** - no judgment-call item touched. This pass's own finding was new, standalone, non-security - fixed outright, not added to the backlog. **2. Picked a fresh, non-security angle**: grepped this doc's own history for mention counts of every `app/lib/*.ts` file (same method recent passes have used) to find genuinely under-reviewed ones. Several files had 0 mentions (`emailSubjects.ts`, `emailTemplatesTier0/2/3.ts`, `formatZAR.ts`, `siteUrl.ts`, `tenderTemplates.ts`, `utils.ts`). Read `tenderTemplates.ts` (SANRAL blank-template metadata) and its 3 real callers (`tender-templates.tsx`, `pack-inputs-actions.ts`'s `uploadTenderTemplate()`, `pack-review-data.ts`) in full first, specifically checking for the "two hand-kept lists that have to stay in sync" bug class the prior pass's own fix was built around (`lib/tenderTemplates.ts`'s own per-template `required: true/false` field, used by the upload-templates UI, vs. `compliance-data.ts`'s separately hand-written `PACK_REQUIRED_TEMPLATES` array, used by the actual pack-readiness/missing-templates gate) - the two lists are currently identical in effect (`technical_xlsm`/`a_forms`/`c111_form_of_offer`/`c123_contract_data` required in both, `financial_xlsm` optional in both), so there is no live bug here today, just the same latent drift risk the prior pass's fix pattern exists to prevent. Not forced into a fix (nothing is actually wrong right now, and deriving one hand-kept list from the other here is a real refactor across 2 files for a risk that hasn't materialised) - noted here in case a future pass sees the two lists actually disagree. `uploadTenderTemplate()`'s own validation order (template-type check, file-presence/size check, extension check, upload, then `record_tender_document()`) and its reliance on Next's `redirect()` throwing to short-circuit later lines (same pattern already used elsewhere in this codebase) both checked by hand and hold up.

**Moved to `formatZAR.ts`** (the canonical Rand formatter, Sarel's own 2026-10-24 Batch 6 brief - "the one place financial, tender value, and BOQ numbers get formatted") - read the whole file plus its existing `formatZAR.test.ts` (13 tests, all passing) end to end. Its `compact` option (`"R 1.5M"`/`"R 250k"` for KPI/summary badges) is implemented by `compactMagnitude()`: divide by 1,000 or 1,000,000, then `toFixed(1)` (dropped to `toFixed(0)` when the *raw*, un-rounded value is already a whole number) - checked specifically for a rounding-boundary bug, since `toFixed()` rounding combined with a hard `>=` threshold on the raw value is exactly the shape that produces an off-by-one at the boundary.

**The finding**: for any value in `[999_950, 999_999]`, `compactMagnitude()` takes the `>= 1_000` branch (correctly, since `abs < 1_000_000`), computes `k = abs / 1_000` (e.g. `999.95` to `999.999`), and `k.toFixed(1)` rounds that up to `"1000.0"` - so the function returns the literal string `"1000.0k"` instead of promoting to the next unit. **Reproduced directly against the real exported function**, no guessing: `node -e` calling the file's own (pre-fix) `compactMagnitude` logic for `999_950`/`999_999`/`999_999` all printed `"1000.0k"`; `999_949` (one rand below the boundary) correctly printed `"999.9k"`. The only real production call site today (`app/tenders/[id]/page.tsx`'s completed-project-value line, `formatZAR(Number(completionValue) * 1_000_000, { compact: true })`) can't currently hit this exact window in practice - `project_completion_value_rm` is `numeric(16,2)` (migration `0065`), so its value in Rand is always a multiple of R10,000, and the nearest reachable value below R1,000,000 is R990,000, well clear of the `[999_950, 999_999]` window - but `formatZAR.test.ts`'s own existing compact-mode tests (`1_500_000`, `2_000_000`, `250_000`, `1_500`) show this is written and tested as a general-purpose formatter for exactly this kind of KPI/summary display, not a single-caller helper; a narrower future input (a different KPI badge, a change to that column's precision) would hit it silently. Fixed as a real bug in shared, documented, tested logic, not deferred as unreachable-today - same reasoning the `scoreOutlookChips.ts` note two passes ago used to justify the opposite call (there, two independent narrow conditions had to coincide on data no real tender has ever produced; here, the only thing standing between the bug and a real user is one column's current numeric precision, which is a much thinner guarantee).

**Fixed** with the minimal correct change: `compactMagnitude()` now also promotes to the `M` branch when `Math.round((abs / 1_000) * 10) / 10 >= 1_000` - i.e. when the thousands figure, rounded to the same 1 decimal place the function already displays, would itself hit 1000 - not just when the raw value is already `>= 1_000_000`. The `M` branch's own existing formatting (raw-value wholeness check, `toFixed(0)`/`toFixed(1)`) is unchanged and untouched; the fix only changes which branch a boundary value takes, so `999_950` and `999_999` now correctly render `"1.0M"` (matching the already-existing "whole millions drop the decimal, fractional ones don't" rule - `0.99995` isn't whole, so it keeps the decimal, same as `1.5M`).

**Verified red-then-green, with new tests added to the existing `formatZAR.test.ts`**: added `"formatZAR: compact rounds up into the next magnitude instead of printing '1000.0k'"`, asserting `999_950` and `999_999` both render `"R 1.0M"` and `999_949` still renders `"R 999.9k"`. **Picked the directive's own "fresh Server Action correctness pass" angle**: grepped this doc's own history for mention counts of every `app/**/actions.ts` file by its own directory name (not just the generic string "actions.ts", which every entry matches loosely) to find genuinely under-reviewed ones. `app/app/pipeline/actions.ts` (1 mention) stood out - core business logic (moving a tender between kanban stages, recording bid economics, recording a won/lost outcome), never read end to end on its own before. Read `moveTenderStage()`, `saveTenderEconomics()`, and `recordOutcomeAndMoveStage()` in full, plus every real caller (`pipeline/page.tsx`'s `StageButton`/`TenderCard`, `pipeline/outcome-form.tsx`'s `OutcomeForm`) - not just the action file in isolation, since a Server Action's correctness here depends on which stages the UI actually offers it for.

`moveTenderStage()` and `saveTenderEconomics()` both held up on a careful read (validation via `parseRand`/`parsePercent`'s own documented `undefined`-for-blank-vs-`null`-for-unparseable contract, correctly distinguished at every call site - re-checked by hand rather than assumed, since a `=== null` vs `!= null` mixup here is exactly the kind of off-by-one this file's own density of blank/garbage-input branches invites). `recordOutcomeAndMoveStage()` itself is also correct in isolation. **The real bug was in which stages the UI wires these actions up for, not in the actions themselves.**

**The finding**: `lib/pipeline.ts`'s `NEXT_STAGES` (widened by migration `0105` to add `briefing_shortlisted` as a second, buyer-dependent path from `submitted` to an outcome, alongside going straight to `won`/`lost`) says `submitted -> ["briefing_shortlisted", "won", "lost"]` and `briefing_shortlisted -> ["won", "lost"]`. But `pipeline/page.tsx`'s `TenderCard` rendered its plain forward-action button bar under `card.stage !== "submitted" && (NEXT_STAGES[card.stage].length > 0 || back)` - i.e. for a card at `submitted`, the ENTIRE forward-button block was hidden, not just the two outcome targets within it. The only other path forward from `submitted` is `pipeline/outcome-form.tsx`'s `OutcomeForm`, whose two submit buttons only ever post `stage="won"` or `stage="lost"` - never `"briefing_shortlisted"`. **Net effect: no button anywhere in the product could ever move a tender from `submitted` to `briefing_shortlisted`.** Confirmed this wasn't a theoretical reading of dead code by checking every real writer of `tender_packs.pipeline_stage` in the whole codebase (`grep -rn "pipeline_stage" app engine` excluding tests/specs) - exactly two: `moveTenderStage()`'s upsert and `recordOutcomeAndMoveStage()`'s upsert, both in this same file, both driven only by what a form's hidden `stage` input is set to by the UI above. No RPC, trigger, or engine job sets it either (migration `0105`'s own header comment confirms `briefing_shortlisted` "only ever follows [submitted]" and is purely a UI-driven move, same as every other stage transition). `engine/seed_demo_company.py`'s own demo data never seeds a `briefing_shortlisted` example either - one more sign this stage had never actually been exercised by anything. **A real, shipped 0105 feature (one of Sarel's own named 7 pipeline columns, confirmed built in `app/AGENTS.md`'s own "Bids pipeline redesign" write-up) was functionally dead on arrival.**

**This directly bears on, and partially overturns, a 2026-11-02 pass's own explicit judgment call** (same doc, "one more targeted sweep for the missing-`briefing_shortlisted` bug class" entry): that pass traced the SAME `OutcomeForm` stage gate, noticed a `briefing_shortlisted` card gets plain Won/Lost buttons with no outcome form, and deliberately left it alone, reasoning "a `briefing_shortlisted` tender can still advance to `won`/`lost` via the plain stage-advance buttons... and `OutcomeForm` correctly reappears once it reaches `won`/`lost`... a legitimate product-flow nuance... not a correctness bug." That reasoning is only sound if a tender can actually reach `briefing_shortlisted` in the first place - and, per the finding above, none ever could, through any UI path that pass didn't check. Not relitigating that pass's own point (a `briefing_shortlisted` card CAN reach won/lost via a plain button once it's there, bypassing the outcome form at that one step - true, and still worth closing while fixing the rest) - extending it with the one check it didn't make.

**Fixed** with the minimal change that resolves both symptoms from their one shared root cause (two hand-kept stage lists that had to stay in sync and didn't), rather than patching each site separately: added `OUTCOME_STAGES` (`["won", "lost"]`) and `OUTCOME_FORM_STAGES` (every stage `NEXT_STAGES` can reach `won`/`lost` from, plus `won`/`lost` themselves - computed from `NEXT_STAGES` itself, not hand-listed a second time) to `lib/pipeline.ts`. `pipeline/page.tsx`'s forward-button bar now filters `won`/`lost` out of its own plain button list (`forwardStages`) instead of hiding the WHOLE bar for `submitted` - so `submitted` now offers a real "Mark briefing / shortlisted" button (its `ACTION_LABEL`/`EMPTY_COPY` entries already existed, unused, before this fix) alongside its outcome-form path, and `briefing_shortlisted` no longer offers plain Won/Lost buttons at all. `outcome-form.tsx`'s own gate now reads `OUTCOME_FORM_STAGES.includes(stage)` instead of hand-listing `submitted`/`won`/`lost`, so it now also renders (and auto-opens, matching `submitted`'s existing UX) on `briefing_shortlisted` - closing the exact gap the 2026-11-02 pass flagged but left alone.

**Verified red-then-green, with a real new test** (`lib/pipeline.spec.ts` - no React rendering test infrastructure exists in this codebase, confirmed by checking `package.json` for `testing-library`/`jsdom`/`happy-dom`, none present, so the fix is tested the same way this file's existing tests already do: as a structural invariant on the exported stage-list constants, not a rendered-DOM assertion): 3 new tests - `OUTCOME_FORM_STAGES` is exactly `submitted`/`briefing_shortlisted`/`won`/`lost`; it covers every stage `NEXT_STAGES` can reach `won`/`lost` from (the structural invariant that makes this exact bug class impossible to silently reintroduce by adding a new path to an outcome without also wiring `OutcomeForm` up to it); it excludes `found`/`assessing`/`building`. Reverted just `lib/pipeline.ts` (`git stash push -- lib/pipeline.ts`, keeping the new tests) and reran: **3 of 3 new tests failed exactly as predicted** (`OUTCOME_FORM_STAGES` undefined, since the export didn't exist pre-fix) - every other test in the file still passed. Restored the fix and reran: all 5 tests in the file passed, **0 failures**. Full `npx vitest run` from `app/`: **360/360 passed, 39/39 files** (357/39 baseline + this pass's 3 new tests in the existing `pipeline.spec.ts` - no new file needed, no regression anywhere). `npx tsc --noEmit` (whole project) - 0 errors. `npx eslint app/pipeline/page.tsx app/pipeline/outcome-form.tsx lib/pipeline.ts lib/pipeline.spec.ts` - clean. No `*.test.ts` file touches this area (confirmed by `find . -iname "*pipeline*" -iname "*.test.ts"` - none), so the separate node-run suite wasn't affected and didn't need rerunning. `git diff --stat`: `lib/pipeline.ts` (+28), `pipeline/page.tsx` (+8/-13, net smaller - the two separate forward-button blocks collapsed into one), `pipeline/outcome-form.tsx` (+12/-11), `lib/pipeline.spec.ts` (+26, 3 new tests in the existing file).

This module's own header comment states plainly why it exists (Sarel, 2026-10-22, verbatim): the generator "may NEVER generate the same or similar versions for two companies - then they might both get disqualified." Checked several other candidates first and ruled them out with a concrete reason (not forced): `lib/vaultDocuments.ts`'s `vaultDocumentMismatchWarning()` (filename-only, non-blocking warning, internally consistent); `lib/opportunityBuyerMatch.ts` (already checked clean by the 2026-11-04 pass below - not re-litigated); `lib/scoutAnomalyAlerts.ts`'s `scoutAnomalyCandidates()` (correct filter logic, already has its own dedicated spec file). Also did a full line-by-line read of the PayFast ITN route's OTHER logic per the directive's own suggestion (signature-stripping regex edge cases, the source-IP/server-confirmation checks, `apply_payfast_itn()`'s amount_gross comparison) - all of it holds up: `verifyItnSignature()`'s `signature=` strip regex correctly handles the field appearing first, middle, or (its only real position) last in the raw body; the amount check compares `numeric` to `numeric` with whole-Rand prices (1490/2990/4990/14900/29900/49900), so there's no floating-point rounding exposure to find. Nothing new there - not forced into a finding that wasn't real.

**The finding**, in `generate_with_uniqueness_check()` (`engine/narrative/generate_narrative.py`): the function generates a draft, checks it with `check_uniqueness()` against every OTHER company's ready document of the same kind for the same tender, and - if flagged - regenerates ONCE with a distinctness instruction. All correct so far. It THEN runs the mandatory 3-pass self-review loop (`run_review_passes()`, the `AI-Call-Quality-Standard.md` "never the first answer" loop Sarel asked for) on whichever draft that left it with, and returns `plain_text` built from the review loop's OWN final sections - but `similarity_score`/`similarity_flagged` were never recomputed after that point, so the values `process_narrative_jobs.py` actually writes to `narrative_documents` next to `generated_text` described a draft that no longer exists, not the text that was actually saved. The review loop's own prompt (per `build_prompt.py`'s `build_review_user_message()`) asks the model to re-check correctness/quality and ALWAYS returns full corrected text, even on a pass that reports "no issues found" - nothing in that prompt asks the model to preserve distinctiveness, so a clean review pass can legitimately rewrite a paragraph back toward generic/boilerplate phrasing, which is exactly the shape this module's own similarity check exists to catch. A header comment on the function already acknowledged NOT re-running the uniqueness check after review, framing it as "a deliberate ordering choice, not an oversight" to avoid the two checks "chasing" each other - true for not re-triggering another distinctness-retry-then-review cycle, but it also meant the STORED verdict could be stale for the actual saved document, which that comment didn't address.

**Reproduced for real** (`/tmp/.../scratchpad/repro_narrative/repro.py`, using the same `StubClient` convention `test_generate_narrative.py` already uses - no real Anthropic key touched): a genuinely distinct first draft ("Mahlangu Civils will deploy its own dedicated grader fleet and site agent") scored 0.42 against a competitor's ready text ("We propose a phased construction methodology with weekly site meetings and dedicated quality control") - correctly NOT flagged, no distinctness retry triggered. A review pass that reports "no issues found" but rewrites the paragraph to near-match the competitor's own wording then runs. Before the fix: the function returned `similarity_score: 0.42`, `similarity_flagged: False` - but the actual `plain_text` it returned (what gets saved as `generated_text`) scored **0.94** against the same competitor text when re-checked with the exact same `check_uniqueness()` call - genuinely over the 0.6 threshold, the precise "two companies' submissions read suspiciously alike" case this feature exists to catch, shipped with a false "all clear" flag.

**Fixed** with the minimal correct change: after `run_review_passes()` returns, `check_uniqueness()` is called a second time against the review loop's own final `plain_text`, and THAT score/flagged pair is what gets returned (and stored). No new LLM call, no second distinctness-retry-then-review cycle is added - the fix deliberately does not reintroduce the "chasing" risk the existing header comment correctly flagged; it only makes the stored verdict honest about the text that was actually saved, the same "a human decides, never silently assumed" discipline `quality_flagged` already applies to the review loop's own output elsewhere in this same function.

**Verified red-then-green, with a real new test**: new `test_similarity_is_recomputed_against_the_review_loop_s_own_output()` in `engine/narrative/test_generate_narrative.py`, using the exact reproduced scenario above. Reverted just `generate_narrative.py` (`git stash push -- generate_narrative.py`, keeping the new test) and reran: **2 of the new test's own checks failed exactly as predicted** (`similarity_flagged` read `False` when the test expects `True`; `similarity_score` read `0.46` when the test expects `> 0.6`) - every other test in the file still passed, 0 other regressions. Restored the fix and reran: all checks passed, **0 failures** across the whole file. Full `python3 engine/narrative/test_generate_narrative.py` - 0 failures (all 24 pre-existing checks plus the 5 new ones in the new test). `python3 engine/narrative/test_process_narrative_jobs.py`, `test_build_prompt.py`, `test_build_docx.py`, `test_uniqueness.py` - all unaffected, 0 failures each (no other module reuses `generate_with_uniqueness_check()` - confirmed by `grep -rln generate_with_uniqueness_check engine/`, only `generate_narrative.py` itself and its own two test files). `python3 -m py_compile` on both changed files - clean. `ruff check engine/narrative/generate_narrative.py engine/narrative/test_generate_narrative.py` - the same 7 pre-existing findings (all in untouched test-file lines, confirmed identical before and after this change via `git stash`) - 0 new findings introduced.

Not security/RLS-shaped (an internal engine heuristic feeding a company's own narrative document generation - no role or tenant boundary anywhere near this code; `other_texts` was already being fetched correctly, cross-tenant, by the service-role worker before this fix, exactly as the module's own design requires - this fix only corrects WHEN the comparison against it is made, not what it's allowed to read) - in scope for this pass, not deferred. Read `docs/specs/AI-Call-Quality-Standard.md` before touching this (per `CLAUDE.md`'s own instruction for any LLM-call-adjacent change) - confirmed the fix adds no new LLM call and doesn't alter the generate-then-3-pass-review loop's own shape in any way the standard governs; it only recomputes an existing, local, stdlib-only `difflib` comparison once more, after that loop finishes, against the text the loop actually produced.

## This pass (2026-11-06, standing solution-architect review): a full correctness read of the PayFast ITN route itself (not the already-deferred redelivery-idempotency question) found a genuine JS-Date "month overflow" bug in `nextPeriodEnd()` - and the identical bug class, independently, in `lib/properties.ts`'s `tooOld()` - fixed both, verified red-then-green, pushed to `main`

**Context for whoever picks this up next, restated, unchanged**: migrations `0117`/`0118` (employee-RLS fixes) are both on `main` but **still NOT applied to the live production database**; PR `#176` (the 12-function `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC employee-RLS-bypass class) is **still open, independently verified, still awaiting Sarel's own explicit go-ahead to merge**. This pass's own task was explicitly told to stay off both of those, off the pagination-cap bug class (now exhausted), and off `lib/cvExtraction.ts` (just fixed by the immediately preceding pass) - so it picked one of the directive's own named candidates instead: a full correctness read of the PayFast ITN route handler itself. **`0117`/`0118` remain pending Sarel's application to production; PR `#176` remains open, unmerged, and untouched by this pass** - not reviewed, not commented on, not merged.

Oriented from `34ef912` (own prior pass: `cvExtraction.ts`'s bare-year false positive). `git fetch origin main && git merge --ff-only` confirmed clean - already at `34ef912`, no new commits, no collision (re-checked again immediately before this entry - still clean). Open PRs re-checked via the GitHub REST API (`gh api repos/.../pulls?state=open`, since `gh pr list`'s GraphQL path is blocked in this session): exactly three, as expected - `#164`/`#165` (both draft, untouched since 2026-10-26, not touched) and `#176` (open, NOT draft, NOT merged - left exactly as is).

**Read this doc's own last several entries first, to avoid retreading ground.** The PayFast ITN handler's own prior coverage, confirmed from this doc's history before starting: signature (Finding 54, verified against PayFast's own official SDK test fixture); source IP + server confirmation (both read and confirmed correct); `amount_gross` verification (migration `0112` - `tt_plan_price_zar()` mirrors `lib/billing.ts`'s pricing exactly, confirmed side by side, no VAT mismatch either); the `current_period_end`-on-FAILED bug (migration `0110`); the webhook-redelivery idempotency gap (found, reproduced live against a scratch Postgres on 2026-10-25, deliberately left as Sarel's own judgment call since - needs a new `pf_payment_id`-keyed dedup table, not a one-line guard, and there's no live money or a real recurring customer this can affect yet). None of those were re-opened or re-litigated this pass - this pass did a *fresh* line-by-line read of the route handler's own logic (`app/api/billing/payfast/itn/route.ts`) that no prior pass had done end to end, rather than re-checking any of the above.

**The finding**: `nextPeriodEnd()` (the private helper the route used to compute the new `current_period_end` an ITN-triggered activation writes) counted a month/year forward with a bare `date.setMonth(date.getMonth() + 1)` / `date.setFullYear(date.getFullYear() + 1)`. Plain JS `Date` arithmetic "overflows" into the following month whenever the target month is shorter than the current day-of-month - e.g. Jan 31 has no Feb 31, so `setMonth` silently lands on Mar 3, not Feb 28. This is **not a rare edge case for a recurring monthly charge**: any customer whose billing date happens to fall on the 31st of January, March, May, August or October gets their "paid through" date (shown on `/admin/billing`, and the field that drives what `status`/`current_period_end` combination the admin sees) pushed 1-2 real days further out than a genuine calendar month, every single cycle that lands on one of those dates - not a one-off.

**Checking for the same bug class elsewhere, mechanically** (the same discipline prior "exhausted a bug class" passes used): `grep -rn "setMonth\|setFullYear" app --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx | grep -v node_modules` - exactly 3 matching lines in the whole app: 2 inside the route's own `nextPeriodEnd()` (the finding above) and 1 in `lib/properties.ts:98`'s `tooOld()` (the Company Properties page's "this compliance document is past the tender rule's own age limit" check, live-used by `app/company/properties/page.tsx`, confirmed by `grep -rn tooOld app`) - the **identical bug**: a 12-month-validity document (`pest_control_certificate`/`sapoa_grading`, both `maxAgeMonths: 12`) issued on a leap day (Feb 29) gets its expiry silently rolled to March 1 of the following (non-leap) year instead of landing on the real Feb 28 anniversary - reading as still valid one extra day past the tender rule's own cutoff. No other file in the codebase does bare month/year `Date` arithmetic at all - this bug class is now exhausted across the whole `app/` tree.

**Reproduced for real, not just reasoned from reading it** - standalone script run directly (copying each function's old logic verbatim): `nextPeriodEnd("monthly")` with the system clock set to `2026-01-31T10:00:00.000Z` returned `2026-03-03T10:00:00.000Z` (should be `2026-02-28`); set to `2026-03-31T10:00:00.000Z` returned `2026-05-01T10:00:00.000Z` (should be `2026-04-30`). `tooOld()`'s old logic, given `issued_on: "2024-02-29"` and `maxAgeMonths: 12`, computed a limit of `2025-03-01` (should be `2025-02-28`) - so on `2025-03-01` itself (the document's real one-year-and-one-day-old date) the old code said NOT too old, wrongly.

**Fixed** by routing both through `date-fns`'s `addMonths()` (already a `package.json` dependency, previously imported nowhere in `app/lib` - confirmed by `grep -rln 'from "date-fns"' lib app` returning nothing before this change) instead of reinventing the clamping logic: `addMonths()` correctly clamps to the last day of the target month when the original day doesn't exist there, which is the correct calendar-anniversary behaviour for both a billing period and a document-validity window. `nextPeriodEnd()` itself was moved out of the route handler into `lib/payfast.ts` as a plain exported function (a `route.ts` file in the App Router may only export HTTP method handlers - `GET`/`POST`/etc - so it couldn't be given real test coverage in place; confirmed no other `route.ts` in this codebase exports anything beyond its HTTP method before making this change, so this wasn't already a precedent to just follow). The route now imports it from there, alongside its other already-externalized PayFast logic (`verifyItnSignature`, `decodePlanInterval`, etc.) - consistent with that file's own existing "every testable PayFast rule lives here, the route only orchestrates" shape.

**Verified red-then-green, with real new test coverage**: `lib/payfast.spec.ts` gained 5 new cases for `nextPeriodEnd()` (using `vi.setSystemTime()` to control "now" precisely) - the two reproduced overflow cases (now correctly `2026-02-28`/`2026-04-30`), a leap-day yearly case (`2028-02-29` -> correctly `2029-02-28`, not `2029-03-01`), and two ordinary-date sanity checks (monthly and yearly) confirming no overcorrection. New `lib/properties.spec.ts` (this file had zero test coverage before this pass) gained 5 cases for `tooOld()` - the reproduced leap-day false-negative (now correctly flagged too-old the day after its real anniversary), the same leap-day case confirmed NOT too old exactly on the real anniversary, an ordinary non-overflow date, a document type with no age limit, and a missing issue date. Reverted each fix individually (`nextPeriodEnd()` back to the bare `setMonth`/`setFullYear`, `tooOld()` back to the bare `setMonth`, one at a time) and reran: in each case exactly the predicted case(s) failed with exactly the predicted wrong value (e.g. `expected '2026-03-03...' to be '2026-02-28...'`), every other case in that file still passed; restored both fixes and reran - all green again. Full `npx vitest run` from `app/`: **357/357 passed, 39/39 files** (347/38 baseline + this pass's 5+5 new tests across 1 extended + 1 brand-new file - no regression anywhere). Every `*.test.ts` file (the separate `node --experimental-strip-types`-run suite, 27 files) also re-run directly, unaffected - all pass, 0 failures. `npx tsc --noEmit` - 0 errors. `npx eslint lib/payfast.ts lib/payfast.spec.ts lib/properties.ts lib/properties.spec.ts app/api/billing/payfast/itn/route.ts` - clean. `git diff --stat`: `app/app/api/billing/payfast/itn/route.ts` (15 lines changed), `app/lib/payfast.ts` (+20), `app/lib/properties.ts` (+18/-3), plus the extended `app/lib/payfast.spec.ts` and the new `app/lib/properties.spec.ts`.

Not security/RLS-shaped (a client-displayed billing date and a client-displayed document-age warning, both already readable/writable by whoever could already reach them - no role or tenant boundary anywhere near either fix) - in scope for this pass, not deferred. No new security/RLS-shaped finding was made along the way to defer either - this was a correctness-only read from the start, per the directive's own framing of this option.

**Backlog: 19, unchanged** - no judgment-call item touched (`held_registrations`-vs-CV, `start_payfast_checkout()`'s revenue-before-ITN gap, the impersonation session-refresh gap, and the PayFast ITN webhook-redelivery idempotency design question all untouched, as directed/by design - this pass deliberately read the ITN route without reopening that last one). This pass's own finding (one bug class, two files) was new, standalone, non-security - fixed outright, not added to the backlog.

Not a bug.

Not a bug.

Not a bug.

Not a gap.

**The finding**, in `app/lib/cvExtraction.ts`'s `looksLikeExistingProject()` (zero mentions anywhere in this doc's history - genuinely never reviewed; used live by exactly one caller, `app/people/[id]/cv-review.tsx`, confirmed by `grep -rn looksLikeExistingProject app`): the CV-review page's own "is this proposed project probably already on file" pre-tick heuristic matched on ANY shared 4+ digit token, including a bare 4-digit token that is just a calendar year. A company that completes more than one project in the same year - the ordinary case, not an edge case - would have a genuinely NEW project from a freshly-uploaded CV wrongly flagged as a likely duplicate of an UNRELATED existing project that merely shares that year, purely because both client/contract lines contain, e.g., "2024" somewhere. The page's own header comment on this function says plainly it exists to "leave a likely duplicate unticked... never to hide it" - but a false positive here does exactly that: `cv-review.tsx`'s "Add this project" checkbox defaults UNTICKED whenever `dup` is true (`defaultChecked={proj.verified && !dup}`), so a reviewer who trusts the automatic flag (plausible - it's shown as a pre-answered judgement, "already on file?") and doesn't compare the two project lines by hand would silently never add a real, new project to the Experience Library from that CV.

**Reproduced for real, not just reasoned from reading it** - standalone script (`/tmp/repro_cv/looksLike.mjs`, the function copied verbatim): `looksLikeExistingProject("XYZ Municipality Water Treatment Plant Upgrade, 2024", ["ABC Municipality - Reservoir Project, completed 2024"])` returned `true` - two unrelated projects for different clients, flagged as a duplicate purely because both happen to mention 2024.

**Fixed** by excluding a token that is a bare 4-digit plausible calendar year (`1900`-`2099`, via a new `BARE_YEAR` regex) from the "numbers" list used for the match, while leaving every other signal unchanged: the whole-line exact match, and any digit token that is NOT a bare year (a real contract/project reference like "2024/15" or "GG2024-01" squashes to something longer than 4 characters and is untouched by this exclusion, so a genuine duplicate sharing a real reference number is still caught). Matches the function's own stated bias: a weak/ambiguous signal (a shared year alone) must resolve toward NOT flagging, since hiding a real new project is the worse direction, not occasionally re-showing an actual duplicate for the reviewer to tick off by hand.

**Verified red-then-green, with a real new test file** (`app/lib/cvExtraction.spec.ts` - this file had zero test coverage before this pass): 5 cases - the reproduced false positive (year-only collision, now correctly `false`), a real shared reference number embedding a year (still correctly `true`, confirming the fix doesn't overcorrect), an identical whole-line match (still `true`), a genuine non-year 4+ digit project number (still `true`), and two unrelated projects with no shared number at all (correctly `false`). Reverted the fix with the new test file kept (`git stash push -- lib/cvExtraction.ts`) and reran: the first case failed exactly as predicted (`expected true to be false`), every other case still passed; restored the fix and reran: all 5 passed. Full `npx vitest run` from `app/`: **347/347 passed, 38/38 files** (342/37 baseline + this pass's 5 new tests in 1 new file - no regression anywhere). `npx tsc --noEmit` - 0 errors. `npx eslint lib/cvExtraction.ts lib/cvExtraction.spec.ts` - clean. `git diff --stat`: exactly `app/lib/cvExtraction.ts` (18 insertions, 4 deletions) plus the new `app/lib/cvExtraction.spec.ts` file.

Not security/RLS-shaped (a client-side UI pre-tick default on a form the signed-in user already has full write access to - no role or tenant boundary anywhere near this code) - in scope for this pass, not deferred. No new security/RLS-shaped finding was made along the way to defer either.

**Backlog: 19, unchanged** - no judgment-call item touched (`held_registrations`-vs-CV, `start_payfast_checkout()`'s revenue-before-ITN gap, the impersonation session-refresh gap, and the separate PayFast ITN webhook-redelivery idempotency design question all untouched, as directed/by design). **The mechanical check method, reusable by a future pass without redoing this from scratch**:
1. `grep -n "\.select(" app/lib/*.ts` and the same across every `app/**/actions.ts` file (22 files at the time of this pass), plus `grep -rn '\.from("tenders")\|\.from("tender_requirements")' app --include=*.ts` as a targeted second pass once the shared/public tables emerged as the real risk factor (a filename-only grep misses callers in `app/**/data.ts`/`app/**/page.tsx` helper files that aren't named `actions.ts`).
2. For every match, read the surrounding code far enough to answer: (a) is there a `.range()` already, or a `count: "exact", head: true` (PostgREST then returns a count, not row payloads, and `lib/supabasePaging.ts`'s own header comment confirms `db-max-rows` only caps actual row payloads - these are never at risk, e.g. `company_principals`/`experience_items` in `lib/companyReadinessData.ts`), or an existing `fetchAllRows()` call (`lib/marketPricing.ts`, `lib/discoveryPagination.ts`, `lib/companyReadinessData.ts` itself)? If any of those, skip it. (b) What is the REAL scope of the query once RLS is applied - not just "is there an explicit `.eq("company_id", ...)`" (several queries have none and are still safely company-scoped, because RLS itself narrows them: `lib/notifications.ts`'s bell and `lib/documentExpiry.ts` both read `held_registrations`/`people`/`tenders` with no explicit company filter at all, but the signed-in user's own RLS context already narrows every one of them, `tenders` via its own `tender_packs!inner(...)` has-many embed, which is itself RLS-scoped to the caller's company).
3. The judgement call, same one already applied to `cv_uploads`: does the table's REAL scope for this query (not the table in the abstract) realistically accumulate past 1000 rows? Two shapes are genuinely at risk and worth re-checking on a future pass as the product grows: (i) a per-company table with **no retention** (every write is a new row, nothing is ever overwritten or deleted) - `cv_uploads` was this shape; `held_registrations`/`people`/`company_principals`/`experience_items`/`person_role_eligibility` were all individually checked this pass and are NOT this shape (edits are real `UPDATE`s in place via their own `actions.ts`, confirmed by reading each one, not assumed) - their own per-company row count stays naturally bounded to "how many registrations/staff/principals/CV-line-items a company genuinely has," not "how many times anyone has ever clicked save." (ii) a table that is **shared/cross-tenant by design**, where a single query's real row count is the SUM across every company or every buyer, not one company's own slice - this is the shape this pass's 5 findings all share, and it is structurally far more dangerous than (i) because the table was never meant to be company-scoped in the first place: `tenders`/`tender_requirements` (migration `0001`'s own header comment: "SHARED/PUBLIC...Shared across every company - not tenant-scoped", fed daily by a dozen+ discovery scrapers that THIS SESSION's own prior live-tests already found return 268 (`capetown_procurement.py`) and 292 (`kouga.py`) rows EACH from a single buyer) and, separately, any query against `tender_packs`/`tender_update_notifications`-shaped tables run under the SERVICE ROLE key in a `scripts/send-*.ts` cron sender (RLS is bypassed entirely there, so the query sums EVERY company's own rows together in one response, not just the caller's).

Past the cap, this would silently stop showing "this tender asks for SACNASP/SAGC/SACAP/..." badges on the People page for whichever open tenders sort past row 1000 - understating real demand for a registration, not a cosmetic miscount.

Past the cap, this would silently stop sending the "closing in 3 days / 24 hours" reminder for whichever tender/company pairs sort past row 1000 - a missed bid deadline, not a cosmetic gap.
3. **`scripts/send-returnables-digest.ts`** - the identical `tenders` x `tender_packs!inner(...)` shape, same SERVICE ROLE scope, feeding the "mandatory returnable missing 3-5 business days before closing" nudge.

Left unchanged.

But `randwater`'s own fix was a stale boolean assertion against a fixture whose real date had simply arrived - this test's own comment block (lines 316-324, added in the SAME 2026-10-23 QA pass as `test_kouga.py`'s frozen-clock fix) claimed the opposite: that it had ALREADY been given the same frozen-clock treatment ("Freezing the clock ... makes it correct forever, not just until that date"), so a plain "flip the hardcoded date" fix made no sense on its own evidence - if the freeze genuinely worked, today's real date should not matter at all. **Root cause, confirmed by reading the real code path, not the comment's claim about it**: `gov_sources.merge()` (line 353, `if hit is None and not r["is_closed"]:`) never recomputes `is_closed` itself - it only reads whatever value the release dict already carries. That value is set once, at construction time, inside `source_http.release()` (`base["is_closed"] = is_past(base["closing_date"])`, against the real wall clock unless patched) - which in this test happens inside `sanral_site()`, called while building the `site = [...]` list. For the one SANRAL row closing "2026-11-06T12:00:00+02:00", today's real wall clock (checked directly: `2026-11-06 12:30 UTC` = 14:30 SAST) is already past that closing time, so it was constructed with `is_closed=True` regardless of the later patch - which meant `merge()`'s own `not r["is_closed"]` gate was false, the "buyer's site says still open, fold into the portal's closed row" branch never ran, and the SANRAL row stayed its own standalone entry (`sanral:nra2026-0754-a`) instead of folding into `ocds-9t57fa-171042`. Genuinely the same underlying bug CLASS as Finding 62 (a near-term real date baked into a fixture, now arrived) - but the specific, already-attempted fix for it was itself wrong, which is the part worth a future pass not re-discovering from scratch.

**Fixed by moving the monkeypatch to wrap `site`'s own construction, not just the `merge()` call** - every `sanral_site()` call (hence every `source_http.release()` call that bakes in `is_closed`) now runs under the same frozen `now()` as `merge()` itself, so every `is_closed` value this test depends on is computed consistently under the fixture's own intended "now" rather than whatever the real wall clock happens to say on any given day. Corrected the comment's own factual claim about `merge()` recomputing `is_closed` while at it, so it doesn't mislead the next reader the way it misled the 2026-10-23 fix.

Traced the real consumer: `seed_supabase_opportunities.py` upserts `discovered_opportunities` keyed on `(company_id, ocid)` (`client.upsert(..., "company_id,ocid")`, one row at a time, not batched) - with two real, distinct tenders sharing one ocid, whichever one is written second in a run silently overwrites the other's row (closing date, title, is_closed, everything), with no error. Depending on write order (kouga's own listing is newest-first, so a re-advertisement is typically processed BEFORE its own older original), the live, still-open re-advertisement could end up clobbered by its own stale, already-closed predecessor - hiding a real, currently-open tender from every company's Discovery feed entirely. Not security-shaped (no role/tenant boundary involved, just a same-source identifier collision) - a correctness bug, in scope for this pass.
- Confirmed this is a genuine site data quirk, not a kouga.py parsing bug: fetched each pair's two detail URLs directly - both are real, separately-dated, separately-worded tender postings on kouga.gov.za itself, not a double-count of one card.

**Fixed, narrowly, in `kouga.py` only** (`_disambiguate_reused_refs()`, called once at the end of `fetch_releases()` after all pages are assembled): for any `contract_number` that appears more than once in a single fetch, every row sharing it gets its own URL slug appended to its ocid (`kouga:<ref>:<slug>`) instead of the bare `kouga:<ref>`. Every OTHER, non-colliding ref's ocid is left completely untouched - deliberately, so this doesn't retroactively change the identity of the ~287 tenders that were never ambiguous and would otherwise all look "new" to `watch_new_tenders.py`'s `(ocid-keyed)` seen-store on the next run. Did not touch the general `ocid` scheme, `gov_sources.py`'s own merge logic, or any other reader - confirmed `gov_sources.merge()` itself already correctly keeps same-source duplicate rows separate (`_find()`'s own "never fold two rows of the same source into each other" rule), so the collision was specifically and only at the `ocid` string level feeding the Supabase upsert, not a double-counting problem inside this codebase's merge step.

**Verified red-then-green, both live and with a permanent regression test**: live, confirmed 0 duplicate ocids across all 292 real rows post-fix (was 5 colliding pairs = 10 affected rows pre-fix), and confirmed every non-colliding row's ocid is byte-for-byte unchanged (`kouga:<ref>`, no suffix). Added `test_reused_ref_gets_distinct_ocids_not_a_collision()` to `engine/discovery/test_kouga.py` - a synthetic duplicate card (same real fixture, same Ref No "225/2026" used twice with a different URL/title/closing date, the exact real shape found live) asserting both rows are kept, now get distinct ocids, each still traceably prefixed `kouga:225/2026:`, and that every other ref's ocid is unaffected. Confirmed genuinely red first: temporarily disabled the new `_disambiguate_reused_refs()` call and re-ran - the new test's 2 collision assertions failed exactly as expected (`['kouga:225/2026', 'kouga:225/2026']`), re-enabled and confirmed green. Ran the full existing `test_kouga.py` suite (pre-existing 21 checks + 5 `fetch_releases()` end-to-end tests, all written by earlier passes) unchanged and still `ALL PASSED` - no regression in page-assembly, `max_pages`, the empty-page/safety-cap error paths, or `gov_sources.py` wiring (`SOURCE_LABELS`/`ALL_SOURCES`/`BUYER_FAMILY`). `ruff check engine/discovery/kouga.py engine/discovery/test_kouga.py`: same pre-existing findings as before this change (2 in `kouga.py` at its own lines 37/55, both pre-dating this pass; 6 pre-existing in `test_kouga.py` at its own header/line 285) - confirmed by diffing against the committed `HEAD` version of each file; zero new findings at any line this pass added. No TypeScript touched (pure Python, engine-side only) - `npx tsc`/ESLint not applicable.

**Separately ran `test_gov_sources.py` and `test_source_http.py` as a broader regression check** (not part of the directive's own ask, but a natural neighbor-check for a merge-adjacent fix): `test_source_http.py` clean. `test_gov_sources.py` has 2 pre-existing failures (`"open on SANRAL, Closed on portal..."`) - confirmed, by stashing this pass's own changes and re-running against unmodified `a23901e`, that these ALREADY fail on `main` before this pass touched anything; the test's own comment (line 319) names the cause - a hardcoded `2026-11-06` fixture date that is, as of today, no longer safely in the future, the same "hardcoded near-term real date eventually flips" bug class this doc's own history (Finding 62, the randwater fixture) has already named once before. **Not fixed this pass** (unrelated to `kouga.py`, the directive's own task, and not a kouga.py/live-test finding) - flagged here plainly for whichever future pass does its own test-suite hygiene sweep: `engine/discovery/test_gov_sources.py` line ~319's own hardcoded date needs the same frozen-clock treatment `test_kouga.py` already got for an identical reason (2026-10-23 QA pass, this same file's own comment block).

## This pass (2026-11-06, standing solution-architect review): did the SYSTEMATIC version of the employee-RLS check (directive after 0117+0118 found two in a row) - the mechanical table-level sweep came back genuinely clean, but checking real app-layer callers for its own candidates found a bigger, different sibling problem: 12 SECURITY DEFINER RPCs bypass employee RLS entirely. **Opened as PR #176, not pushed to main and not merged, per the standing guardrail on anything larger than a one-table fix.**

Oriented from `84c5093` (own prior pass: `company_tender_preferences` employee-RLS fix, 0118, pushed by the orchestrator after this session's own push was blocked). `git fetch`/`merge --ff-only` confirmed clean - already at `84c5093`, no new commits, no collision. Open PRs re-checked via the GitHub REST API (`gh api repos/.../pulls?state=open`): only `#164`/`#165` remain, both draft, both untouched since 2026-10-26 - not touched. Backlog cross-checked: 19 total, 3 genuinely open (`start_payfast_checkout()`'s own revenue-before-ITN gap, the impersonation session-refresh gap, `held_registrations`-vs-CV) - none acted on.

**Part A: the systematic table-level check, done mechanically rather than by eyeballing migration files.** Replayed all 108 migrations into a fresh scratch Postgres (`service postgresql start`; `su postgres -c "bash engine/security/replay_schema.sh -U postgres -d scratch_sweep"`) and ran this directly against `pg_policies` - the exact, reproducible enumeration the directive asked for:

```sql
select distinct tablename from pg_policies
where schemaname='public' and permissive='PERMISSIVE'
  and (qual ilike '%is_company_member%' or with_check ilike '%is_company_member%')
  and tablename not in (
    select distinct tablename from pg_policies where schemaname='public' and permissive='RESTRICTIVE'
  )
order by 1;
```

(Confirmed first, directly against `pg_proc`, that `is_company_member`/`is_employee_in_company` are the only two functions any policy's `qual`/`with_check` ever calls for a company-membership check, and that no policy spells the same check out inline against `company_members` instead of calling the function - so this query is a complete enumeration, not a partial one keyed to one function name by luck.)

Result: exactly 3 tables - `savings_counted_steps`, `tender_documents`, `tender_requirements`. Each checked individually, not assumed clean:
- `savings_counted_steps`: already investigated by the 0118 pass and correctly left alone - it powers Home (`/dashboard`), one of an employee's two allowed pages. Re-confirmed, no change.
- `tender_documents`/`tender_requirements`: both LOOK like the same gap shape at first read (0045 added a bare `is_company_member(company_id)` branch to each, for a company's own private template-copy/requirement-override rows), and 0077's own Part D comment exempted both with reasoning that turns out to be imprecise ("already readable by authenticated users for EVERYONE... unaffected by any role"). But the actual policy text (not the comment) also requires `exists (select 1 from tenders t where t.id = ... and (t.owner_company_id is null or is_company_member(t.owner_company_id)))` - a plain, non-`security definer` subquery against `tenders`, which therefore runs under its OWN RLS, including `tenders`' own blanket "employee has no access" RESTRICTIVE policy (0077 Part C) that hides EVERY `tenders` row - shared or private - from anyone whose role is `employee` in ANY company. That `EXISTS` can never be true for an employee, so both tables transitively return zero rows regardless of their own `company_id`. Confirmed live, not reasoned from the text alone: seeded one company/owner/employee/tender(`owner_company_id` = that company)/`tender_packs`/one `tender_documents` row/one `tender_requirements` row (both `company_id` = that company). As the employee: `select ... from tenders where id = '<tender>'` -> 0 rows; `select ... from tender_documents where tender_id = ...` -> 0 rows; `select ... from tender_requirements where tender_id = ...` -> 0 rows; `select ... from tender_packs where tender_id = ...` -> 0 rows (already covered). As owner: all four return the real row, unaffected.

**This is itself the valuable, reportable result the directive asked for if the sweep came back clean**: the table-level RLS side of this bug class is now genuinely exhausted and mechanically re-checkable with the query above, not just "checked by eye one more time."

**Part B: checking real app-layer callers for those 3 candidates found a different, bigger problem.** Per the directive's own "check the real app-layer caller(s) to judge actual reachability" step, traced how an employee would actually reach `/tenders/[id]` (where `tender_documents`/`tender_requirements` are read) - `nav-items.ts`'s own `isNavItemActive()` treats `/tenders/*` as a drill-down FROM Home, and Home genuinely links into `/tenders/[id]` via its dispatch/command-center cards. `AppShell.tsx`'s `isEmployee` only swaps the nav list and the subscription banner - it never gates page content, so the full `/tenders/[id]` page (compliance report, pack review, pricing, tasks, documents) genuinely renders for an employee who follows that link, the same "nav hides it, nothing blocks the page" shape 0117/0118 already found for `/billing`/`/pipeline`/`/discovery`.

Oriented from `f6d49d1` (own prior pass's sibling: a test-only commit adding missing intake coverage, no production code). `git fetch`/`merge --ff-only` confirmed clean - still at `f6d49d1`, no new commits, no collision. Backlog cross-checked against the recent chain: 19 total, 3 genuinely open (`start_payfast_checkout()`'s revenue gap, the impersonation session-refresh gap, `held_registrations`-vs-CV) - self-consistent, none touched this pass.

Per the directive's own suggested angle, rotated to `/toolkit`'s other calculators now that the SANRAL B6 one (`f7e0509`, prior pass) has had its own dedicated read: `cidb-grade` and `deadline-calculator` had never had one. Read `app/lib/cidbGrading.ts`/`.test.ts` and `app/lib/publicHolidays.ts`/`.test.ts` end to end, plus both calculators' client components (`CidbGradeClient.tsx`, `DeadlineCalculatorClient.tsx`).

**CIDB grade calculator: genuinely clean.** `CIDB_GRADING_TABLE`'s 9 bands are contiguous with no gaps/overlaps (own test already asserts this), boundaries match the published cidb Standard for Contractor Grading Designation table exactly, `requiredGradeForValue()`'s inclusive-lower-bound rule is correctly implemented and documented, and its own trailing `return 9` is dead code (the loop's `band.maxValue ?? Infinity` already covers Grade 9) but harmless - not a bug, just a redundant line already covered by the loop. `bandForGrade()`/`gradeSufficientForValue()` are both correct and covered. No code change here.

**Found a real, reachable bug in the deadline calculator's own "today."** `DeadlineCalculatorClient.tsx`'s `today()` was `new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)` - `toISOString()` is always UTC, regardless of the viewer's device/browser timezone. Since this app's own established convention everywhere else that needs "today"/"now" in South African terms (`lib/dates.ts`, `lib/tenderActivity.ts`, `emailBrand.ts`, `scripts/send-founder-digest.ts`'s `sastDateKey`) explicitly uses `timeZone: "Africa/Johannesburg"` (SAST = UTC+2, no DST) rather than raw UTC or the implicit device locale, this stood out as the exact bug class already fixed repeatedly elsewhere in this session (a date computed in the wrong reference frame) - just never checked in this one file.

**Reproduced for real**, not assumed: `new Date("2026-11-05T23:30:00Z").toISOString().slice(0, 10)` -> `"2026-11-05"`; the real SAST calendar date at that same instant (01:30 on 2026-11-06 local) is `"2026-11-06"`, confirmed via `Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-CA", { timeZone: "Africa/Johannesburg" })`. This is not a rare edge case - it is the real UTC-vs-SAST date for every single day, during the ~2 hours before UTC midnight (00:00-02:00 SAST). Any user, anywhere, opening the calculator in that daily window saw yesterday's date silently pre-filled as "today" in the Start/From date field; if left unchanged (a realistic default-accepting use of a quick lookup tool), both "add working days" and "count working days between dates" compute off the wrong start date, and the "upcoming public holidays" list is keyed off it too.

**Fixed** by adding `sastToday(now: Date = new Date())` to `lib/publicHolidays.ts` - this file's natural home, since it already owns every other SAST/holiday rule - using the same `now.toLocaleDateString("en-CA", { timeZone: "Africa/Johannesburg" })` pattern `send-founder-digest.ts` already established for exactly this (en-CA locale formats as `YYYY-MM-DD`). `now` is injectable only for tests; `DeadlineCalculatorClient.tsx`'s own local `today()` was deleted and its `useSyncExternalStore` call now reads `sastToday` directly, matching how every other "what's today" read in this app already goes through an explicit-timezone helper rather than the device/server's implicit one. CIDB's calculator has no date logic at all, so no equivalent gap there.

Added 2 new tests to `lib/publicHolidays.test.ts`: the exact 2026-11-05T23:30Z counter-example (asserts `sastToday` returns `"2026-11-06"`, explicitly asserting it disagrees with the raw UTC slice at that instant), and a daytime-UTC sanity check where the two agree. Confirmed genuinely red-then-green: temporarily reverted only `sastToday()`'s body to the old `toISOString()` call and re-ran - the new counter-example test failed (`"2026-11-05"` vs `"2026-11-06"` expected), the sanity check still passed; restored the fix - both pass. Full regression: `node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/*.test.ts` - 232/232 (230 prior + 2 new), 0 failures. `npx vitest run` - 37 files / 342 tests, all passing (confirms nothing using `publicHolidays.ts` via the vitest/bundler path regressed). `npx tsc --noEmit` on the full `app/` project - 0 errors. `npx eslint "app/lib/publicHolidays.ts" "app/lib/publicHolidays.test.ts" "app/app/tools/deadline-calculator/DeadlineCalculatorClient.tsx"` - clean, no findings.

**Backlog: 19, unchanged** - standalone bug, fixed; not a new judgment-call item. `held_registrations`-vs-CV, `start_payfast_checkout()`'s revenue gap, and the impersonation session-refresh gap all untouched, as directed.

Committed and pushed directly to `main` (no PR - small, fully verified, no live-DB access):
- `app/lib/publicHolidays.ts`
- `app/lib/publicHolidays.test.ts`
- `app/app/tools/deadline-calculator/DeadlineCalculatorClient.tsx`

To verify independently: `cd app && node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/publicHolidays.test.ts` (13/13), or `node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/*.test.ts` for the full suite (232/232). To see the bug directly: `node -e 'console.log(new Date("2026-11-05T23:30:00Z").toISOString().slice(0,10))'` (prints the wrong, UTC date) vs the same instant through `Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-CA", {timeZone:"Africa/Johannesburg"})` (prints the correct SAST date, one day later).

Confirmed via `node --experimental-strip-types -e` that every `PROJECT_TYPE_MATRICES`/`TECH_POSITION_ROWS`/`MAN_POSITION_ROWS` data table has the right row/column lengths and correct on-diagonal 5s (no transcription-length bug) before looking at the scoring logic itself - genuinely clean there.

**Found, in the scoring logic itself**: `estimateSanralConventional()`'s management-points range handles a position whose `managerial` flag isn't on file (unknown) by scoring it both ways and reporting the spread, since reading a position as managerial changes its own denominator (15 -> 30) as well as its points. For <=6 such ambiguous positions on one tender it brute-forced all `2^n` combinations - correct. Above 6, it silently fell back to trying only 2 scenarios: every ambiguous position managerial, or none of them (`const scenarios = unknownIdx.length <= 6 ? 1 << unknownIdx.length : 2`). That is not a sample of the true range: because reading a position as managerial always adds points to the numerator but ALSO always costs exactly +15 on the denominator regardless of which position it is, a position with a low/zero managerial-position-held score should stay non-managerial even while OTHER positions are worth flipping - the true worst/best case is generally a MIXED combination, which "all true" and "all false" can both miss entirely.

This is reachable on every real tender today, not a contrived edge case: `compliance-data.ts`'s own comment states positions come from `tender_pack_assignments` because `tender_requirements` "isn't seeded by anything yet" - and `tender_pack_assignments` has no `managerial` column at all, so `managerial: p.req ? p.req.managerial : null` is `null` for every single position, on every tender, right now. Book 1's own SETUP sheet has up to 10 non-alternate key-person slots (`docs/specs/SANRAL-Tender-Automation-Specification.md`, positions 11/12 are the alternates), several of which (PL/CE/RE/RM, repeated across a multi-section contract) are manager-eligible at once - more than 6 is a realistic shape for a larger Conventional tender, not a hypothetical.

**Reproduced for real** with a disposable Node script (`npx vite-node`, since this module - like several `app/lib/*.ts` files - resolves fine under Next.js/vitest's bundler resolution but needs explicit import extensions to run standalone): built 7 manager-eligible positions (one of each MAN_POSITION_COLUMNS code) where 3 have a strong managerial-position-held score and 4 have zero. The pre-fix code reported `management: { min: 3.6, max: 5 }`. An independent brute-force oracle over the true `2^7 = 128` combinations found the true range is `{ min: 3.2, max: 5 }`, achieved at mask `CE:true, RM:true, CE(T):true` (a genuine mix) - not at all-true or all-false, the only two the old code ever tried. The displayed range understated how low the true worst case goes by 0.4 points (12% of the 0-15 management band) - directly undermining the report's own "Clears the threshold even at the bottom of every unknown range" outlook line, which depends on this exact number.

**Fixed** by replacing the `2^n`/2-scenario code with an exact O(n log n) solve: since every ambiguous position's denominator delta is the same constant (+15) regardless of which position, for any fixed count `k` of positions chosen managerial, the extreme numerator for that `k` is always the `k` positions with the largest (for max) or smallest (for min) own managerial-vs-non swing - sorting once and scanning every `k` from 0..n finds the true global extreme for any n, not just n<=6. Verified the derivation is exact, not just "better", with a randomized differential test (500 trials, n<=6, comparing the new code against the OLD code's own exhaustive brute force byte-for-byte, after first fixing a flawed rounded-vs-unrounded comparison in the test harness itself) - zero mismatches - and separately re-ran the real n=7 counter-example and the 128-combination oracle: new code now reports `{ min: 3.2, max: 5 }`, matching exactly.

While reproducing this, also found `sanralScoring.ts` has never had a test file, in either this repo's `.test.ts` (plain `node --experimental-strip-types --test`) or `.spec.ts` (vitest) convention - and traced why: its own import of `./sanralMatrices` (no `.ts` extension) cannot resolve under the plain node runner at all (confirmed: adding a `.test.ts` file for it breaks the whole `node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/*.test.ts` glob with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`), unlike every other module this convention covers (`tenderCompliance.ts`, `personCredentials.ts`, etc.), which already import their own local deps with the explicit extension `vitest.config.ts`'s own comment documents as the reason `.test.ts` exists as a separate convention from `.spec.ts`. Fixed that one-line import to `./sanralMatrices.ts` so a real test file can actually run here, matching the rest of the codebase - this had silently kept this scoring engine, the one genuinely live-tender-affecting piece of `/toolkit`, outside both test conventions since it was written.

Added `app/lib/sanralScoring.test.ts` (new file): the n=7 counter-example asserting against the independent brute-force oracle, an n<=6 case re-checked against the same oracle (guards the previously-correct path), a sanity check that a position with a known managerial flag is never treated as ambiguous, and a `pastPerformanceFromExperience()` best-3-of-N check (that function read clean on inspection but had no coverage either). Confirmed genuinely red-then-green: reverted only the algorithmic change (kept the import-extension fix, otherwise the file can't load at all) and re-ran - the n=7 test failed (`3.6` reported vs `3.2` expected), the other 3 passed; restored the fix - all 4 pass. Full regression: `node --experimental-strip-types --test app/lib/*.test.ts` - 230/230 (226 prior + 4 new), 0 failures. `npx vitest run` - 37 files / 342 tests, all passing (confirms the extensionless-import fix didn't disturb anything using `sanralMatrices.ts` via the vitest/bundler resolution path, e.g. `tenderRoles.ts`). `npx tsc --noEmit` on the full `app/` project - 0 errors. `npx eslint "app/lib/sanralScoring.ts" "app/lib/sanralScoring.test.ts"` - clean, no findings.

**Backlog: 19, unchanged** - standalone bug, fixed; not a new judgment-call item. `held_registrations`-vs-CV, `start_payfast_checkout()`'s revenue gap, and the impersonation session-refresh gap all untouched, as directed.
